⭐ ⭐ ⭐ Looking for Cantonese-speaking learners of Korean (online experiment)
⭐ ⭐ ⭐ 招募文案（粵語母語人士）
大家好，我係梨花女子大學韓國學系嘅朴善姬。本研究旨在觀察韓國人同韓語學習者對韓語句子嘅語法性判斷同句子理解情況，誠邀你參與本實驗。
研究題目：以第三語言習得韓語疑問詞內嵌句嘅研究
研究負責人姓名及所屬機構：朴善姬（梨花女子大學）
研究目的：觀察韓國人同韓語學習者對韓語句子嘅語法性判斷同句子理解情況
參與基準及研究對象人數：以粵語（廣東話）為母語嘅成年人（年滿19歲），英語能力達中級或以上（TOEIC 550分或以上、TOEFL iBT 57分或以上，或IELTS 5.0或以上；如冇公認成績，以自我報告確認），並且韓國語能力試驗（TOPIK）達3級或以上（3至6級）嘅韓語學習者，共82名（預備實驗2名＋正式實驗80名）。（排除基準：唔係以粵語為母語，或韓語・英語能力未達上述基準）
研究期間及招募期間：自生命倫理委員會批准之日起至2028年5月31日
參與次數與時間：參與1次（大約需要60至80分鐘）
實驗內容：語言背景問卷＋課題1（判斷句子嘅自然程度）＋課題2（選擇句子嘅意思）＋課題3（自定步速閱讀）＋英語及韓語能力測試（填充）
實驗指引及查詢：實驗全程喺網上進行（喺約定時間連接Zoom進行，唔會開鏡頭）。如喺實驗過程中感到不適或者唔想繼續參與，可以隨時中止而唔會有任何不利。如對研究有任何疑問，請聯絡以下電郵：朴善姬
koreanresearchlab@gmail.com
研究參與申請方法：有意參與研究嘅人士，請點擊以下連結或者掃描QR碼申請。申請之後，研究者會個別聯絡你，約定參與時間。參與本研究嘅人士將獲得謝禮（可以由你揀200港幣嘅香港星巴克禮券，或者30,000韓元嘅韓國Olive Young禮品卡）。
申請連結：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1SDLTIcTjNoimQwIEM72Zkx30SCNnRmNvz-Q1KDJEaXw/viewform
多謝你參與研究。
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

title: Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Turn Messy Notes into Polished Documents
bodyText:

»
Announcements
Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Turn Messy Notes into Polished Documents  - ITSC
From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We've all been there — furiously jotting down notes during a call, only to end up with a jumble of half-sentences and abbreviations.
Copilot Chat
can transform your rough notes into clean, professional documents!
Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
"I took these rough notes during a call. Please transform them into a well-structured meeting summary with: (1) Meeting overview, (2) Key discussion points, (3) Decisions made, (4) Action items with owners. Clean up the grammar and make it professional. Here are my notes: [paste your messy notes here]"
Why this works:
Specifying the exact output structure (overview, discussion, decisions, actions) tells Copilot how to organize your chaos into something shareable. No more spending 20 minutes reformatting your notes!

Bonus tip:
You can also say "Turn these notes into a formal report" or "Convert these bullet points into a paragraph-style email update." Copilot adapts to whatever format you need!
Want to enhance your Copilot skills? Check out previous
All IT - Microsoft Copilot Chat Usage Tips
for even more helpful guidance and best practices.
(Please log in with your M365 staff or student account to view this page)

Announcements
(19 November) Join our D&I Festival 2026/27: Sensing Inclusion! | 齊來參與多元共融節2026/27：感・共融！  - Diversity and Inclusion Office
From: Diversity and Inclusion Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
dio@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【 Sensing Inclusion｜D&I Festival 2026/27 】
Take 5 minutes. Navigate the world from a new perspective.
Drop by and experience inclusion through four quick, interactive activities engaging your sight, touch, taste and imagination. Discover how people connect, create and navigate the world in different ways.
19 November 2026 (Thursday) | G/F Lobby & Piazza, YIA
12:00 noon–3:00 pm
Mental Wellness · VR Experience
Step into an immersive virtual reality experience that offers a different perspective on mental well-being and encourages reflection on empathy and understanding.
Aroma Stone Painting Workshop
Create and personalise an aroma stone alongside instructors from the Down Syndrome Association's Cheuk Yip Centre, celebrating creativity, talent and inclusion.
Sign Language · Bubble Tea Tasting
Learn a few everyday signs while enjoying a refreshing drink and explore how communication extends beyond spoken language.
Braille Leather Pouch Workshop
Discover the basics of Braille and customise a leather pouch with embossed dots, exploring how information can be communicated through touch.
Four Experiences. One Afternoon. A New Perspective.
Walk-ins welcome; no advance registration required. Places, drinks and materials are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Please follow the participation arrangements announced on-site.
-------------------------------------------------------
【 感・共融｜多元共融節2026/27 】
停下五分鐘，換個角度看世界。
透過四項輕鬆而富互動性的體驗活動，運用視覺、味覺、觸覺和想像力，感受不同人士認識世界、溝通交流及展現才華的方式，從日常之中發現共融的新視角。
2026年11月19日（星期四）|YIA大堂及廣場
中午12時至下午3時
情緒健康・ VR 體驗
透過沉浸式虛擬實境體驗，從不同角度了解情緒健康議題，反思同理心與彼此理解的重要。
彩繪擴香石工作坊
與香港唐氏綜合症協會卓業中心導師一同創作及裝飾擴香石，感受創意、才能與共融的力量。
手語傳意・手搖滋味
一邊品嚐特色飲品，一邊學習簡單日常手語，體驗語言以外的溝通方式。
點字皮革收納包工作坊
認識點字，親手刻印專屬皮革收納包，探索以觸覺傳遞資訊的另一種方式。
四項體驗．一個下午．一個全新視角

Announcements
Training Caring Professionals to Leading Brief Mindfulness Practices and Programmes  - Department of Educational Administration and Policy
From: LAU Ngar-sze, Elsa
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ngarszelau@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Organised by:
The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
Professional Practice & Assessment Centre
The Hong Kong Polytechnic University | Department of Applied Social Sciences
Project Objectives
The Mindful Facilitator Project aims to:
Test the effects of a formal professional training programme tailored for health and social care professionals.
Provide practice knowledge and skills for caring professionals who is interested teach brief mindfulness practices and programmes in their work.
Targets
Applicants should meet the following requirements:
Any caring professionals from disciplines (Education, Social Work, Counselling, Nursing and Allied Health Professionals) with a bachelor’s degree or above;
Completed an 8-week MBI course, such as a Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), or Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT).
Intentions to apply mindfulness in professional practice.
Able to access to WhatsApp or Signal to complete Ecological Momentary Assessment#.
Training Dates
Batch A
Whole day Skills Training:
2027 Jan 10, 24, 31, & Feb 28
and/or
2-days Residential Overnight Training:
2027 Feb 12 night to 14 afternoon
OR
Batch B
Whole day Skills Training:
2027 May 2, 16, 23 & June 13
and/or
2-days Residential Overnight Training:
2027 May 28 night to 30 afternoon
Trainers
Five experienced MBSR/MBCT teachers will share the teaching of the programme.
Programme Fee
Free
More Project Details and Application Form
Please refer to the QR code on the original poster for more project details and the application form.
Enquiry
Email:
mindstudy@polyu.edu.hk
Telephone:
67150918
正念引導員計劃（The Mindful Facilitator Project）
培訓關懷專業人員帶領簡短正念練習及課程
主辦機構：
香港理工大學
專業實踐及評估中心
應用社會科學系
一、計劃目標（Project Objectives）
本計劃旨在為醫療、健康及社會服務領域的專業人員提供正念培訓，並達成以下目標：
評估專業培訓的成效：
透過專為醫療、健康及社會服務專業人員設計的正規培訓課程，研究及評估培訓的實際效果。
提升正念實踐及帶領能力：
為有興趣在日常工作中帶領簡短正念練習及相關課程的關懷專業人員，提供所需的實踐知識、技巧及能力。
二、參加對象及資格（Targets）
本計劃歡迎符合以下條件的專業人員報名參加：
專業背景及學歷：
來自教育、社會工作、輔導、護理及專職醫療等領域的關懷專業人員，並持有學士學位或以上學歷。
正念課程經驗：
曾完成為期八星期的正念介入課程（Mindfulness-Based Intervention, MBI），例如：
正念減壓課程（Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction, MBSR）
正念認知治療課程（Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy, MBCT）
實踐意願：
有意將正念練習應用於自身的專業工作及服務之中。
通訊工具要求：
能夠使用 WhatsApp 或 Signal，以完成生態瞬時評估（Ecological Momentary Assessment, EMA）。
三、培訓日期（Training Dates）
本計劃設有 A 組及 B 組，參加者可按個人時間安排選擇合適的組別。
A
組（
Batch A
）
全日技巧培訓（
Whole-day Skills Training
）
日期：
2027年1月10日
2027年1月24日
2027年1月31日
2027年2月28日
及／
或
兩天住宿培訓（
Residential Overnight Training
）
日期：
2027年2月12日晚上至2月14日下午
或選
擇
B
組（
Batch B
）
全日技巧培訓（
Whole-day Skills Training
）
日期：
2027年5月2日
2027年5月16日
2027年5月23日
2027年6月13日
及／
或
兩天住宿培訓（
Residential Overnight Training
）
日期：
2027年5月28日晚上至5月30日下午
四、培訓導師（Trainers）
本計劃將由
五位具豐富經驗的正念減壓課程（
MBSR
）及正念認知治療課程（
MBCT
）導師
共同參與教學，分享正念課程的帶領方法及教學經驗。
五、課程費用（Programme Fee）
費用：全
免
參加者無須繳付課程費用。
六、計劃詳情及報名方法
如欲了解更多計劃詳情及填寫報名表格，請掃描原始宣傳海報上的二維碼（QR Code）。
七、查詢及聯絡方法（Enquiry）
如對本計劃有任何疑問，歡迎透過以下方式聯絡主辦單位：
電郵：
mindstudy@polyu.edu.hk
電話：
67150918
計劃簡
介
「正念引導員計劃」由香港理工大學相關學術單位推行，旨在協助教育、社會工作、輔導、護理及其他醫療健康領域的專業人員，將正念理念與練習融入日常專業服務。
透過有系統的技巧培訓及住宿培訓，參加者有機會向具經驗的正念導師學習，進一步掌握帶領簡短正念練習及相關課程所需的知識與技巧。

2026 Hong Kong Neurodiversity Conference
I am pleased to share the upcoming 2026 Hong Kong Neurodiversity Conference, co-organized by the Department of Educational Psychology, Faculty of Education, CUHK and the NeuroDiversity Association Hong Kong, and sponsored by the Croucher Foundation.
The Conference aims to bring academic insights on neurodiversity into dialogue with real-world practice, through academic presentations, sharing sessions, interactive booths, and exhibitions hosted by local practitioners and organizations.
We look forward to bringing together researchers, practitioners, advocates, families, and the wider community to exchange knowledge and experiences.

2026香港腦力多元研討會
2026香港腦力多元研討會將於2026年11月21日（星期六）在香港中文大學舉行，由香港中文大學教育學院教育心理學系及香港腦力多元協會合辦，並獲裘槎基金會贊助。
會議旨在連結腦力多元的學術研究與實務工作，透過學術演講、分享環節、互動展位及展覽，促進大眾對腦力多元的理解與知識交流。
歡迎教育工作者、相關專業人士、腦力多元倡議者、家長及照顧者，以及希望了解腦力多元的大眾參加。

From: Zhou Zhenyi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155198832@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Your Language Classroom Experience Matters! Share Your Views for a Chance to Win a HK$200 E-Gift Card!

Dear Students,
What makes a language classroom experience positive and predictable? We would love to hear your thoughts!
The LEaPP Lab at the Department of Educational Psychology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), invites you to participate in a research study exploring university students' experiences of language teaching and learning.
Who Can Participate?
Aged 18 or above;
Currently learning a second/foreign language in the formal classroom setting
What Does Participation Involve?
Complete an online questionnaire, which will take approximately
15–20 minutes
.

Participation Reward: HK$200 E-Gift Card!
Participants whose responses meet the study's data quality requirements will be eligible to enter a lucky draw for a
HK$200 e-gift card
.
After data collection has ended, selected winners will be contacted by email to receive their e-gift cards.
How to Participate
Ready to share your experience?

Click here to read the study information and complete the questionnaire
Participation is entirely voluntary. Your responses will be treated confidentially and used for academic research purposes. Please refer to the informed consent form at the beginning of the questionnaire for further details.
If you have any questions, please contact the research team at
xinjiechen@cuhk.edu.hk
.
Thank you for sharing your experience and supporting our research!
LEaPP Lab
Department of Educational Psychology
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
中文版本
你的語言課堂經歷，值得我哋聽到！分享你的想法，即有機會贏取港幣
200
元電子禮券！

各位同學：
你有沒有留意過自己在語言課堂中的學習及上課經歷？我哋想聽聽你的想法！
香港中文大學教育心理學系 LEaPP Lab 現正邀請你參加一項有關語言教學與學習經歷的研究，了解大學生對語言課堂及教學的體驗。
參與資格
年滿18歲或以上;
目前正在正規課堂環境中學習第二語言/外語
參與內容
填寫一份網上問卷，預計需時約
15–20
分鐘
。

參與禮遇：港幣
200
元電子禮券！
研究團隊將根據問卷回答的資料質素，確認參加者是否符合抽獎資格。符合資格的參加者將有機會透過抽獎，贏取一張
價值港幣
200
元的電子禮券
。
問卷收集結束後，研究團隊將透過電郵聯絡得獎者，安排發放電子禮券。
參與方式
想分享你的語言課堂經歷？

按此閱讀研究資料並填寫問卷
參與本研究完全出於自願。所有問卷回答均會保密處理，並只用於學術研究。有關研究詳情，請參閱問卷開始前的知情同意書。
如有任何疑問，歡迎電郵聯絡研究團隊：
xinjiechen@cuhk.edu.hk
。
多謝你嘅時間、分享同支持！
香港中文大學教育心理學系

Your Language Classroom Experience Matters! Share Your Views for a Chance to Win a HK$200 E-Gift Card!

Dear Students,
What makes a language classroom experience positive and predictable? We would love to hear your thoughts!
The LEaPP Lab at the Department of Educational Psychology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), invites you to participate in a research study exploring university students' experiences of language teaching and learning.
Who Can Participate?
Aged 18 or above;
Currently learning a second/foreign language in the formal classroom setting
What Does Participation Involve?
Complete an online questionnaire, which will take approximately
15–20 minutes
.

Participation Reward: HK$200 E-Gift Card!
Participants whose responses meet the study's data quality requirements will be eligible to enter a lucky draw for a
HK$200 e-gift card
.
After data collection has ended, selected winners will be contacted by email to receive their e-gift cards.
How to Participate
Ready to share your experience?

Click here to read the study information and complete the questionnaire
Participation is entirely voluntary. Your responses will be treated confidentially and used for academic research purposes. Please refer to the informed consent form at the beginning of the questionnaire for further details.
If you have any questions, please contact the research team at
xinjiechen@cuhk.edu.hk
.
Thank you for sharing your experience and supporting our research!
LEaPP Lab
Department of Educational Psychology
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

From: Chaplain's Office

【午間心靈綠洲】一直希望為忙碌的校園生活提供一片可以稍作停留、讓心靈得蒙滋潤的空間。今次我們特別呈獻一場來自崇基圓夢計劃的音樂會。
崇基圓夢計劃鼓勵同學在學業以外，主動設計並實踐具意義的夢想，透過學院的支持，豐富個人經歷與成長。
今次「音·繫·崇基」音樂會，正是兩位同學以音樂連結崇基的一次實踐——由音樂系同學盧頌熹 (Rex Lo) 及趙朗熙 (Janson Chiu) 共同創作，
並由 Rex 以單簧管演出，與大家分享一段屬於崇基的音樂肖像。
歡迎各位到來，一同見證這份從圓夢計劃延伸出來的音樂分享。
【Midday Oasis】Midday Oasis has always aimed to offer a brief pause in the midst of our busy campus life.
This time, we are delighted to present a concert that grows out of the Dreaming Through Chung Chi Scheme.
The Dreaming Through Chung Chi Scheme encourages students to design and realize meaningful projects beyond their regular studies, with the College’s support to enrich their experiences and growth.
“Chung Chi in Harmony: A Musical Portrait” is a collaborative creation by music students Rex Lo and Janson Chiu, performed by Rex on the clarinet—an intimate sharing of a musical portrait of Chung Chi.
All are warmly welcome to join us for this musical moment rooted in the Dreaming Through Chung Chi Scheme.

Training and assessments are free of charge

bodyText:

From: Office of Academic Links
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
tomlai@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The JC School of Public Health and Primary Care (SPHPC) and Office of Academic Links (Global) will host the
APRU Global Health Conference 2026
at Henry Cheng International Conference Centre, CUHK during 6-9 December. We are now recruiting CUHK students to serve as Student Ambassadors and to support the conference. We welcome enthusiastic students to join the team, extend a warm welcome to guests from around the world, and contribute to the success of this major international conference.
Main Duties
Student ambassadors will assist with the following tasks:
Welcoming guests and providing directions during registration, breaks, lunches and the welcome reception
Ushering guests during the opening and closing ceremonies
Providing on-site support in concurrent sessions
Responding to general enquiries about the conference venue, CUHK, and local attractions
Providing other logistical and event support as requested by the organizing team
Eligibility
Applicants should:
Be currently enrolled CUHK full-time undergraduate or postgraduate students
Have good communication skills in English
Be responsible, punctual and willing to work as part of a team
Be friendly, proactive and comfortable interacting with international participants
Duty Period
Dates
: 7–9 December 2026
Duty hours
: Morning, afternoon and full-day shifts will be available. Please indicate your availability in the application form.
Briefing
A briefing for selected student ambassadors will be held on the morning of 4 December 2026. The exact time will be confirmed later. Attendance is strongly recommended.
Remuneration
Selected student ambassadors will receive
HK$70 per hour
for duties performed during 7-9 December 2026.
Application
Please complete the
application form
by
18 November 2026
. Selected students will be notified by 25 November 2026.

Announcements
“In Dialogue with China” Talk Series – The Changing Global Order, China’s “Dual Circulation” Strategy, and the Greater Bay Area Development 「訪談中國」講座系列 - 變化中的全球秩序、中國「雙循環」戰略與粵港澳大灣區發展 - Office of University General Education
From: General Education China Programme, Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are pleased to invite you to attend the following talk under the “In Dialogue with China” Talk Series, to be delivered by Professor Li Chen, Centre for China Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Talk Title:
The Changing Global Order, China’s “Dual Circulation” Strategy, and the Greater Bay Area Development
Abstract:
This talk reviews the profound structural shifts in global geopolitics and political economy during the recent decades and China’s “Dual Circulation” development strategy as a response to these changes. It examines the challenges and opportunities facing China’s economic development and reforms in the increasingly complex and volatile geopolitical and geo-economic environment. It discusses the strategic importance of Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area under China’s “Dual Circulation” paradigm in the changing global context.
Date:
11 November 2026 (Wednesday)
Time:
6:45 – 8:15 pm
Venue:
Lecture Theatre 2 (LT2), Yasumoto International Academic Park, CUHK
Language:
English
Registration link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741701
All CUHK staff and students are welcome to join. Please visit the following website for further information about the talk series:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/in-dialogue-with-china-talk-series/
Should you have any questions, please feel free to write to
ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk
or contact us at 3943 0595.
我們誠邀各位參加「訪談中國」講座系列，講座將由香港中文大學中國研究中心黎晨教授主講。詳情如下：
講座題目：
變化中的全球秩序、中國「雙循環」戰略與粵港澳大灣區發展
講座摘要：
講座回顧近數十年來全球地緣政治和政治經濟重大的結構性轉變，以及中國如何發展出「雙循環」戰略應對全球變局。講座將探討在日益複雜且動蕩的地緣政治與地緣經濟環境下，中國在推動經濟發展與改革時面臨的挑戰和機遇，並討論在全球格局不斷變化下，香港及粵港澳大灣區在中國「雙循環」發展格局下的戰略重要性。
日期：
2026年11月11日（星期三）
時間：
晚上6:45 至8:15
地點：
香港中文大學康本國際學術園二號演講廳（LT2）
語言：
英文
報名連結：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741701

Student Helper Recruitment for a Psychology Survey Project  - Department of Psychology
From: Dr. Xianmin Gong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
xianmingong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are looking for student helpers to support our research project, “Older Adults’ Pursuit and Experience of Happiness in Daily Life.”
This project explores how adults aged 60 and above pursue and experience happiness in their everyday lives. It includes:
Three survey waves completed at different time points;
A two-week daily diary survey involving brief daily questionnaires.
Project duration: 1 Nov 2026 - 31 March 2026
What will student helpers do? Your main responsibilities will include:
Contacting older adult participants;
Explaining the study procedures and survey tasks clearly and patiently;
Sending reminders to help participants complete the surveys;
Following the research team’s procedures for protecting participants’ privacy.
If you have any questions, feel free to contact the researcher Dr. Xianmin Gong (Department of Psychology) at xianmingong@cuhk.edu.hk.

[Equal Opportunity Youth Ambassador Scheme 2026/27]  - Office of Student Affairs
From: Office of Student Affairs

Dear students,
Are you passionate about promoting diversity, equal opportunities, and inclusion? Be a part of the impactful journey! The Equal Opportunities Commission (EOC) invites enthusiastic students from tertiary education institutions to apply for the Youth Ambassador Scheme.
Join the Equal Opportunity Youth Ambassador Scheme to learn more about equal opportunities through experiential learning activities. You can acquire skills and knowledge beyond classroom, expand your social network, and strengthen your connection and sense of belonging to the community including the EOC.
Youth Ambassadors who attain a satisfactory attendance rate and complete the tasks assigned under the Scheme will receive the following rewards:
A certificate issued by the EOC
A reference letter signed by EOC Chairperson
Online credential on Youth Ambassadors’ LinkedIn
“Most Active Participation Award” (To be awarded to dedicated Youth Ambassadors only)
The Scheme is now open for applications until 17 November 2026 (Tuesday)
.  All full-time students studying diploma courses or above, regardless of gender, race, family status, or ability, are welcome to join the Scheme.  The organiser would also provide reasonable accommodation for students with disabilities in accordance with their needs.  For details, please refer to the Scheme’s website
www.eoc.org.hk/youth
.
Students are also required to complete the
CUWebform
for our records and further processing on or before the application deadline.
For enquiries on the Equal Opportunity Youth Ambassador Scheme 2026/27, please feel free to contact Ms Dorothy SAM, Senior Corporate Communications Manager (T: 2106 2124; email:
dorothysam@eoc.org.hk
) or Miss Agnes LAU, Corporate Communications Manager (T: 2106 2250; email:
agneslau@eoc.org.hk
). Thank you!
Best regards,
Student Experience and Development Section
Office of Student Affairs

招募典禮學生工作人員（2026年12月1日及2日）
拓展及籌募處現正為即將舉行的活動公開招募學生工作人員，協助現場運作與物資支援。歡迎細心、有責任感及具良好溝通能力的同學報名參與。
活動日期：2026年12月1及2日（星期二及星期三）
時薪：HKD 70
備註：如能出席全部兩天工作者，將獲優先考慮。
主要職責：
協助嘉賓登記、簽到及引導接待
協助典禮現場物資維護及遞送
協助場地佈置、物資搬運及復原
支援其他現場突發及營運事宜
我們期望你：
具良好溝通技巧、主動積極且具責任感
守時並能配合現場團隊分工
能全程出席上述工作時段及相關簡報會（暫訂於2026年11月30日以 Zoom 形式舉行）

angelalau@cuhk.edu.hk
）
Recruitment of Student Helpers for Ceremony (1 & 2 December 2026)
Office of Institutional Advancement is currently recruiting Student Helpers to provide on-site operational support for an upcoming event. Students who are responsible, detail-oriented, and possess strong communication skills are warmly invited to apply.
Event Dates: 1 & 2 December 2026 (Tuesday & Wednesday)
Hourly Rate: HKD 70
Remarks: Candidates who are available on both days will be given priority consideration.
Main Responsibilities:
Assist with guest registration, reception, and ushering
Provide on-site logistics support
Assist with venue setup, logistics transport, and pack-down
Support other general administrative and ad-hoc on-site tasks
We are looking for candidates who:
Possess strong communication skills, initiative, and a high sense of responsibility
Are punctual and capable of working effectively in a team
Are available for the full working shifts and the online briefing session (tentatively scheduled for 30 November 2026 via Zoom)
For further details, please refer to the
application form
. Interested students are welcome to complete the form. Suitable candidates will be contacted by phone and provided with additional information about the role.

angelalau@cuhk.edu.hk

(The application below is conducted in Chinese only.)
日期：2026年11月6日(星期五)
時間：下午12時半至2時
地點：香港中文大學利黃瑤璧樓5樓505室
語言：廣東話
講者：孫啟烈教授(銅紫荊勳賢，太平紳士)
免費登記：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13746084
講者簡介：
孫啟烈教授幼受庭訓，其父輩自1948年來港創業後，一直服務於製造業，從暑期學徒，到放洋歷練，五十年的工商貿易經驗，令其具備廣泛的人脈，並從中融匯了營商、議政、社會公職和同鄉社團等互補長短的網絡關係。
講座簡介：
五十年代始，紡織業是香港的領頭羊，所有從事生產的，基本上圍繞紡紗、織布，再衍生其他行業，機修、模具、五金、塑膠，之後服裝電子、玩具、日用品等民生商品，經蓬勃發展進入今天的智能生產和製造，也把中國從勞力密集型打造成世界工廠以至今天被西方世界批評「產能過剩」的社會。香港回歸已近三十年，經濟發展榮辱互見，孫啟烈教授將以資深企業家和大家分享他對未來社會發展的趨勢看法。

hkiaps@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
(The application below is conducted in Chinese only.)
日期：2026年11月6日(星期五)
時間：下午12時半至2時
地點：香港中文大學利黃瑤璧樓5樓505室
語言：廣東話
講者：孫啟烈教授(銅紫荊勳賢，太平紳士)
免費登記：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13746084
講者簡介：
孫啟烈教授幼受庭訓，其父輩自1948年來港創業後，一直服務於製造業，從暑期學徒，到放洋歷練，五十年的工商貿易經驗，令其具備廣泛的人脈，並從中融匯了營商、議政、社會公職和同鄉社團等互補長短的網絡關係。
講座簡介：
五十年代始，紡織業是香港的領頭羊，所有從事生產的，基本上圍繞紡紗、織布，再衍生其他行業，機修、模具、五金、塑膠，之後服裝電子、玩具、日用品等民生商品，經蓬勃發展進入今天的智能生產和製造，也把中國從勞力密集型打造成世界工廠以至今天被西方世界批評「產能過剩」的社會。香港回歸已近三十年，經濟發展榮辱互見，孫啟烈教授將以資深企業家和大家分享他對未來社會發展的趨勢看法。

Student Helper Recruitment – CUHK Graduate Employment Survey 2026  - Career Planning and Development Centre (CPDC), OSA

To understand the employment situation of the University’s graduates, the Career Planning and Development Centre (CPDC) of the Office of Student Affairs conducts the Graduate Employment Survey (GES) every year.
The project is now looking for two student helpers to assist in collecting data and generating reports:

Full-time undergraduates or postgraduates from any discipline;
Solid verbal skill in both Cantonese and Mandarin is desirable.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other general IT applications, as well as experience in telephone outreach duties, will be an advantage.

Handling survey data and preparing reports as required
Phone calls to graduates to conduct survey
Documentation

Monday to Friday
Time:
Preferably no less than 2 days a week, no less than 3 hours a day, within Monday to Friday
(Detailed timeslots will be discussed after your application)
Location:
Career Planning and Development Centre, 2/F, Benjamin Franklin Centre, CUHK

$67/Hr
Please submit your CV by email to CPDC (
CUHKCareer@cuhk.edu.hk
). Personal information like name, student ID No. and Phone No. should also be provided in the email.
Application deadline
:
On rolling basis
*Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be informed.

title: Celebrate the Festive Season at German Christmas Night!
bodyText:

»
Events / Activities
Celebrate the Festive Season at German Christmas Night!  - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
modernlang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear students,
Get ready to kick off the Christmas season with warmth, music, and delicious treats!
You are warmly invited to join
German Christmas Night
, hosted by the German Programme of the Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages.
About German Team & the Event
We are CUHK’s German language and cultural programme team!
German Christmas Night is a cozy, open cultural gathering to celebrate traditional holiday festivities (
Weihnachten
) and the time in the run-up to it: Advent.
No German language skills are required
—whether you study German, speak it natively, are an exchange student, or are just curious to experience the culture and meet new friends, everyone is welcome!
What’s Waiting for You?
  DIY Cookie Decoration:
Decorate authentic German Christmas cookies.
  Authentic German Food:
Enjoy traditional German food.
  Festive Vibes:
Sing along to a classic Christmas tune or two and soak in the cozy atmosphere.
  Meet New Friends:
Connect with fellow CUHK students with a connection to German and German-speaking countries as well as with exchange students from these countries.
Event Details
  Date:
Thursday, 19 November 2026
  Time:
6:00 PM
  Venue:
i-Lounge, 3/F, Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA)
  Admission: Free of charge (Open to all CUHK students)
How to Register
To facilitate planning, please register by Mon 16 Nov 2026.
Registration Link:
https://forms.gle/1x8uQBaFtfnuREWb6
(You can also scan the QR code on our poster or check out our Instagram
@cuhk_german
!)
Come celebrate, chat, and share the holiday spirit with us.
We look forward to seeing you there!
Warm regards,
The German Programme Team
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages

For enquiries, please write to:

bodyText:

Announcements
Sustainable Development Goals x General Education (SDG Study Scheme) – Start Your Sustainability Journey in Term 2!   - Office of University General Education
From: Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sdg-ouge@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

SDG Study Scheme
– Learn. Act. Achieve
Are you passionate about sustainability and making a real impact?
Join the
SDG Study Scheme
by the Office of University General Education (OUGE) – a unique opportunity to integrate the
United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
into your General Education journey at CUHK!

Why Join?
The SDG Study Scheme empowers you with essential knowledge and practical experience for tackling the challenges of tomorrow. This is your chance to showcase your sustainability competency and potential! Let’s be part of a community striving for a better future together!

What’s in the Scheme?
The SDG Study Scheme comprises three components, combining knowledge-based learning with experiential learning:
1.
Understand SDGs with a global vision
Finish the short online introductory course -
How to Achieve the SDGs
by the SDG Academy, and
pass
a
short
quiz
on the
SDG Community Blackboard site
.
2.
Equip yourself with SDG-related k
nowledge
Take
two to three
SDG-GE
(General Education) courses
, each carrying at least 2 units
:
Students admitted in
2021-22
: take at least
3
SDG-GE courses
Students admitted in
2022-23 or after
: take at least
2
SDG-GE courses
3.
Take action to help the communities
Complete one of the following action items:
one
SDG-SE (Social Engagement) course
of at least two units
; or
at least 26 hours
of co-curricular
Volunteer Activity (SDG-VA)
.
Learn more:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/sdg-study-scheme-overview/

Certification
Upon completing the Scheme, you will be awarded the
SDG Explorer Certificate
to recognize your achievements in both SDG knowledge and community engagement.
Apply for your certificate here:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=12998341

Actions to take!
1. Join the SDG Community!
Join the SDG Community to connect with like-minded students and receive updates on SDG-related activities and the SDG Study Scheme.
Sign up here:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=10231196
2. Plan Ahead: Enroll in SDG courses in Term 2!
Take your GE studies further – enroll in courses labelled with SDGs.
These courses not only enrich your sustainability competency but also empower you to engage with global and local sustainability challenges through meaningful learning and actions.
Browse the list of SDG-related GE courses offered in Term 2 and enroll early:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/wp-content/uploads/learning/2627T2_SDG-Class-Offerings.pdf
3. Follow us on Instagram and share with your friends!
Connect with us on Instagram at @
sdg_ge_cuhk
and scan the QR code below to follow us.

Enquiry
Email us at:
sdg-ouge@cuhk.edu.hk

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:

"Science and China" 2026-Distinguished Academician Lecture Series: Gaze at the Stars, Explore the Extreme Universe
“科学与中国——千名院士·千场科普”是由中国科学院学部发起、中国科学院等单位共同主办的科普行动，旨在弘扬科学精神、普及科学知识，激发公众特别是青年学子的科学兴趣与创新热情。本次活动由香港中文大学举办，特邀崔向群院士、林海青院士莅临中大，围绕光学天文观测、理论计算与超导物理等前沿领域开展科普讲座，展现我国科技创新实力，启迪青年学子的科学兴趣与探索精神。

emilyleung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Integrating Mindfulness into Professional Practice: A Mindfulness Facilitator Training
Are you a professional in healthcare, social work, psychology, or education who wants to integrate mindfulness into your service, but feels unsure about how to introduce it safely and flexibly?
Many frontline practitioners have learned approaches that incorporate mindfulness (such as ACT or DBT), but due to limited course hours, may feel their core grasp of mindfulness needs a deeper, more solid foundation.
Taught in Cantonese, this training is designed specifically for professionals working with adult service users. It moves beyond standard 8-week group training to focus on practical 1-on-1 applications, short workshops, and experiential creative tools!
3 Programme Highlights:
Creative & Diverse Modalities: Go beyond foundational practices with Mindful Tea Drinking, Mindful Clay, and Mindful Jar creation—engaging ways to introduce mindfulness to your clients.
Tailored for Helping Contexts: Learn to guide mindfulness safely, ethically, and adaptively within individual counseling or group sessions.
Comprehensive Support System: Includes 6 months of structured learning, a 3-day silent retreat, small-group tutorials, and post-course practice supervision.
Trainer: Prof. Stanley Chan
• Adjunct Assistant Professor, JC School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
• Educational Psychologist (HKDEP Registered)
• Oxford Mindfulness Foundation (OMF) Certified Trainer
• Mindfulness Network (UK) Approved Supervisor
Course Schedule & Logistics
Stage 1: Theory & Core Skills (Location: D' Hub, Prince Edward)
• Full-Day Sessions (09:30 – 18:30):
Dec 19, 2026 (Sat) | Jan 2, Jan 16, Jan 30, Jan 31 (Sun), Feb 13, 2027 (Sat)
• 1st Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): March 7, 2027 (Sun)
Stage 2: 3-Day Silent Retreat (Non-overnight, Venue TBC)
• Full-Day Retreat (09:30 – 18:30 TBC): March 26–28, 2027 (Easter Holiday, Fri–Sun)
• 2nd Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): April 10, 2027 (Sat)
Stage 3: Practice & Integration (Location: D' Hub, Prince Edward)
• Full-Day Sessions (09:30 – 18:30):
April 24, May 1, May 8, 2027 (Sat)
• 3rd Group Tutorial (1.5 hrs/group): May 22 & May 29, 2027 (mornings)
Post-Course Supervision Stage:
• 2 sessions of small group practice supervision (1.5 hrs each) within 30–90 days following Stage 3.
Entry Requirements:
1. Mindfulness Foundation: Completion of an 8-week mindfulness course (MBCT, MBCT-L, or MBSR) by an accredited organization/teacher.
2. Professional Qualification: Bachelor’s degree in healthcare, health, or social services with active membership in a regulated local professional body (e.g., Registered Social Worker, Educational/Clinical Psychologist, Registered Nurse).
3. Silent Retreat Experience: Completion of one 5-7 day or two 3-day overnight silent retreats. (Note: Applicants currently pending retreat completion may still apply provided they commit to fulfilling it before completing this training.)
Fees:
• Application Fee: HKD $300
• Tuition Fee: HKD $29,500
Application Deadline: 16 November 2026 (Admissions on a rolling basis—early submission is strongly encouraged!)

Check your sleep and earn $600 coupons. The current project attempt to recruit patients with insomnia for testing a non-pharmacological intervention 評估睡眠狀況，即可獲得價值 600 HKD的超市禮物券。本計畫目前正在招募失眠患者，以測試一項非藥物干預。 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Cornelius San Yeung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155249610@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
成日失眠，食藥無用，怎麼改善？
聲音刺激 (acoustic stimulation) 是一種全新的干預手段，初步研究發現經特殊處理的低頻聲波可有望改善睡眠品質。本研究用於調查聲音刺激是否能顯著改善失眠症狀，現招募符合以下條件的人群參與研究：
18至45歲成年人
無嚴重精神障礙疾病
確診患有失眠症（即出現失眠症狀，每週發作至少三次，持續不少於三個月，並對日間工作、學習或社交造成影響）
能閱讀繁體中文或廣東話
研究流程
:
佩戴14天體動手錶、填寫睡眠日記。
前往睡眠研究室，完成一天全日檢測（認知測試、情緒睡眠評估、問卷填寫）, 當晚接受多導睡眠檢查。聲音刺激有機會在深度睡眠期出現。
完成整個研究，即可獲得一份專屬睡眠報告 & 價值600的購物禮券，如你對研究感興趣，可點選以下連結報名，我們將在兩個工作日以內聯繫符合條件的報名者。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ
Suffering of insomnia, no effective use of hypnotics, how to do?
Acoustic stimulation
is a novel intervention method. Preliminary studies suggest that specially processed low-frequency sound waves may help improve sleep quality. This study aims to investigate whether acoustic stimulation can significantly alleviate symptoms of insomnia.
We are now recruiting participants who meets all the following:
Aged
18 to 45
No history of severe psychiatric disorders
Diagnosed with
insomnia disorder
(i.e., experiencing insomnia symptoms at least three times per week for a minimum of three months, with negative impact on daytime work, study, or social functioning)
Able to read Traditional Chinese or Cantonese
Study Procedures
Wear an
actigraphy watch for 14 days
and complete a
sleep diary
Attend the
Sleep Research Laboratory,
for a full-day assessment, including:
Cognitive testing
Mood and sleep evaluations
Questionnaire completion
Overnight
polysomnography (sleep study)
Acoustic stimulation may be delivered during deep sleep
Participant Benefits
A
personalized sleep report
prepared by experts
A
$600 supermarket shopping voucher
​For enrollment, please fill the online form below.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ

Student Helper Recruitment: Website Redesign & Revamp
We are seeking a proactive and skilled student helper to lead the revamp and modernization of our website (approximately 10 pages).
Key Responsibilities
Audit and redesign the layout, visual structure, and navigation across ~10 pages.
Ensure responsive, mobile-friendly design and cross-browser compatibility.
Optimize site speed, accessibility, and user experience (UX/UI).
Collaborate closely with the project team to update and organize page content.
Requirements & Qualifications
Target Major:
Current undergraduate or postgraduate student majoring in
Computer Science
, Information Engineering, or a related computing discipline.
Experience:
Minimum
2 years of hands-on experience
in web design, UI/UX design, or front-end development (e.g., HTML/CSS/JavaScript, React/Vue, or CMS platforms such as WordPress/Webflow).
Strong eye for visual hierarchy, typography, and clean, user-friendly layouts.
Independent problem-solver with good communication skills and ability to meet agreed project milestones.
A portfolio or links to prior web design projects is strongly preferred.
Appointment Details
Work Mode:
Flexible / Hybrid (mostly remote with occasional coordination meetings).
Workload & Duration:
Estimated 50 total hours across 8 weeks (negotiable based on project scope and student schedule).
Remuneration:
HKD10000-15000 depending on experiences.
How to Apply
Interested applicants should submit the following to
wingchee@cuhk.edu.hk
with the subject line
"Application: Student Helper (Website Revamp) - [Your Name]"
:
Brief CV / Resume (including current year of study and major).

Audit and redesign the layout, visual structure, and navigation across ~10 pages.

Optimize site speed, accessibility, and user experience (UX/UI).
Collaborate closely with the project team to update and organize page content.

Target Major:

Computer Science
, Information Engineering, or a related computing discipline.

Minimum
2 years of hands-on experience

Flexible / Hybrid (mostly remote with occasional coordination meetings).

Announcements
EPIN Term 2 Courses – Step Beyond the Classroom, Into the World of Innovation  - Minor Programme in Entrepreneurship and Innovation (EPIN)
From: Minor Programme in Entrepreneurship and Innovation (EPIN)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
epin@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

EPIN Term 2 Courses – Step Beyond the Classroom, Into the World of Innovation
This Term 2, EPIN invited you to immerse yourself in hands-on learning experience through courses covering business consulting projects, innovation bootcamp, startup practicums and opportunities to learn directly from industry leaders. No matter your discipline, you will have the chance to broaden your perspective, develop practical skills, and explore new possibilities in innovation and entrepreneurship.
Explore our upcoming courses below and find the one that matches your aspirations.
1. EPIN3010 Business Model Innovation for Startups​
​

From Idea to Impact: Learn How Successful Businesses Are Buil
t
Want to understand how successful businesses create value and grow? In this course, you will learn practical tools for analyzing and designing business models while working on a real startup consulting project. Partner with entrepreneurs, evaluate business opportunities, and develop strategies to support venture growth.
Instructor:
Prof. Andy Wong, Co-director of EPIN
Credit:
3
Date and time:
Monday 10:30-13:15
2. EPIN3020 Innovation Bootcamp

Under This Year’s Theme:
Legacy Reboot: Tradition Meets Transformation
How can traditional businesses stay competitive in a rapidly changing world? Through field research, design thinking workshops, and an intensive 3-day Innovation Bootcamp, you'll work in multidisciplinary teams to tackle real challenges faced by local businesses and industries. From identifying customer needs to building prototypes and pitching solutions, you'll learn innovation by doing.
Theme:
Legacy Reboot: Tradition Meets Transformation
Instructor:
Mr. Henry Tam, Co-founder of Design for HK
Credits:
1
Course Format:
Field Trip + 3-Day Intensive Innovation Bootcamp
Key Dates:
Field Trip: Mar 12
Innovation Bootcamp: Mar 19 & 20
Final Pitch Presentation: Mar 21
3. EPIN3040 Entrepreneurship Practicum

Step Into the Startup World: Learn Entrepreneurship by Doing
What is it really like to work in a startup? Experience entrepreneurship firsthand by working directly with startups and entrepreneurial ventures in Hong Kong's vibrant innovation ecosystem. Through at least 32 hours of fieldwork, you'll contribute to real projects in areas such as business strategy, user experience, fundraising, and market development while building practical entrepreneurial skills.
Instructor:
Prof. Tina Choi, Professional Consultant of MGNT
Credits:
2
Date & Time:
Thursday, 5:30pm - 7:15pm (meetings arranged in selected weeks only)
4. EPIN4020 Creative Problem Solving

Beyond the Classroom: Tackle Tomorrow's Challenges with Today's Leaders
How do leaders make decisions when there are no obvious answers? In this course, you'll explore complex challenges shaping Hong Kong's future through discussions with business leaders, entrepreneurs, policymakers, and industry experts. Through research, presentations, and interactive discussions, you'll learn to analyze issues from multiple perspectives and develop innovative solutions.
Instructors:
Mr. Paul Cheng, JP, BA, MBA, Honorary Fellow, CUHK, Veteran Public Leader & Author
Prof. Andy Wong, Co-director of EPIN
Prof. Tina Choi, Professional Consultant of MGNT
Credits:
3
Date & Time:
Wednesday, 5:30pm - 8:15pm
5.
EPIN2900/EPIN3900 / EPIN4900 Internship in Entrepreneurship and Innovation

Turn Your Internship Experience into Academic Credit
Completed a startup- or innovation-related internship? These courses allow you to convert valuable internship experience into academic credit. Reflect on your learning, connect theory with practice, and demonstrate your contributions to innovative projects, ventures, or organizations.
Instructor:
Prof. William Wong, Professor of SEEM
Credits Available:
EPIN2900 (1 credit): For students who have completed a full-time internship of at least 6 weeks.
EPIN3900 (2 credits): For students who have completed a full-time internship of at least 12 weeks.
EPIN4900 (3 credits): For students who have completed a full-time internship of at least 6 months.
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
(HK$150 cash coupon for a 30–60 minute study) Are you face blind? Or are you exceptionally good at recognizing faces? Do you have a good memory? Here's your chance to learn more about your face recognition ability, working memory, personality, and more—with rewards!  - Management
From: Huiyao Liao
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
huiyaoliao@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Researchers at The Chinese University of Hong Kong are now recruiting participants for a 30–60 minute study. Participants will be invited to complete four short surveys/tests, which include assessments of your personality, a test of your working memory, a vocabulary test, and a test of your face recognition ability.
If you are interested, at the end of the study we can provide feedback on your level of face recognition ability, working memory, and vocabulary relative to all study participants. If you complete all four tests, you will receive a HK$150 ParknShop coupon as a reward.
Research target:
• CUHK students or staff.
• Good command of English (The majority of survey questions will be in English).
• Can understand and speak Mandarin Chinese (some tests, including the vocabulary test, will be conducted in Mandarin and Simplified Chinese, as the standard test toolbox was developed by mainland educational institutions: Tsinghua University and the Institute of Psychology, Chinese Academy of Sciences).
• Have access to a desktop or laptop with a microphone (the tests are best displayed on a desktop or laptop; issues may arise when displayed on a mobile phone or tablet; the vocabulary test also requires you to speak words, so a microphone is needed).
Interested participants please fill out the screening survey via the link below:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0Py8TJxIQUFSaHQ
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purposes and will be kept strictly confidential. This research has been approved by the CUHK Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics (SBRE) Committee (Application Reference No.: SBRE-22-0178).

From: Peggy Chan

=== 歡迎轉發及介紹家人朋友參加 ===
【坊間流行方法與促進母子健康的關係 】
研究目的：研究產前課程對母子健康短期及長期效果
完成每次會面評估均會有車馬費
完成所有訓練及所有會面評估可獲額外感謝金
參加條件：
18歲或以上本地居民
正懷有單胞胎 (懷孕30週或以下)
以中文作為家中主要溝通語言
在威爾斯親王醫院做產檢
研究內容：
隨機分配至不同產前課程
訓練期由懷孕中後期至BB出世
每週在家進行5日訓練 (訓練時間約5 至 40 分鐘)
訓練前會進行一次評估* (完成後可獲車馬費 $50 )
*參加者可選擇是否會受邀到威爾斯親王醫院進行磁力共振掃描
小朋友 0- 2歲期間進行定期跟進會面評估  (完成每次可獲車馬費 $300 )
評估內容包括: 腦電圖、健康問卷、嬰兒行為評估、家中語言採樣語言及認知發展測試(附參考報告) 等
評估及跟進會面地點: 中文大學
=== 歡迎轉發及介紹家人朋友參加 ===
請透過以下連結報名：https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=gTdBhKa7s0W74E8XxpDaakfaYLvTVDZKiyvisUIka4ZURE5HQlROTE1RTTJEWUpIWDdEVTJGR01JOC4u
如有任何問題，歡迎致電 / Whatsapp諮詢 (電話: 69207828）
=== Feel free to share with family and friends ===
【Recruitment: Pregnant Mothers for Prenatal Course Research】
Up to HK$1,550 for completing all training and assessments
Purpose of the Study:
To investigate the short- and long-term effects of prenatal courses on maternal and child health.
Eligibility Criteria:
Local resident aged 18 or above
Currently pregnant with a singleton (30 weeks or less)
Chinese is the primary language spoken at home
Doing antenatal check-ups at Prince of Wales Hospital.
Study Details:
Participants will be randomly assigned to different prenatal courses
Training period: From mid to late pregnancy until the baby is born
Home-based training 5 days per week (each session lasts 5–40 minutes)
One pre-training assessment (HK$50 reward)
*Some participants may be invited for an MRI scan at Prince of Wales Hospital
Follow-up assessments from birth until the child is 2 years old (HK$300 reward per follow-up)
Each assessment includes: EEG, health questionnaires, infant behavior evaluation, home language sampling, and cognitive development testing (with reports)
Location for assessments and follow ups: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Speaker:
Dr. Marie Escribe
Affiliation:
Hong Kong Baptist University

Date:
20 November 2026 (Friday)

Time:
12:30 p.m.

Venue:
Room 214, Li Dak Sum Building, CUHK
Generative AI has sparked intensive discussions about the future of translation and language professions. While some view AI as a disruptive force that may diminish the role of human translators, others see new opportunities emerging from technological innovation.
In this talk, Dr. Marie Escribe will explore how the translation profession has historically adapted to technological changes and examine how AI is reshaping, rather than replacing, the work of language professionals. Drawing on both academic research and industry experience, she will discuss the skills, competencies, and career pathways that are becoming increasingly important in the AI era, while reflecting on how translators and educators can strike a sustainable balance between embracing and critically engaging with automation.

Environmental Forum “Is Urban Forest a Utopia Forest in the City?” 環保座談會「城市林（Urban Forest）是烏托邦式的城市森林？」 - New Asia College
From: New Asia College
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
nac@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
試想像一個城市，樹木不僅點綴街道景觀，更能改善公眾健康、提升生物多樣性、緩解氣候變化，並重新連繫人與自然。這樣的願景究竟能否實現？還只是現代城市中的烏托邦想像？
是次座談會邀得國際樹木學會註冊資深樹藝師及城市綠化專家
王卓粵先生
主講，將以其多年樹木管理、城市綠化及生態保育工作的豐富經驗，探討城市林的發展潛力與現實挑戰，帶領大家重新思考自然與城市共存的可能性。
無論您對環境保護、生態保育、可持續發展、城市規劃感興趣，還是單純希望了解身邊的綠色空間，歡迎踴躍參與，一同探索城市林的未來發展與價值。誠邀學生及教職員參與！

：
新亞書院環境保護委員會
活動詳情

講題：
城市林（Urban Forest）是烏托邦式的城市森林？
日期：
2026年11月27日（星期五）
時間：
下午1:00 – 2:00（12:45開始接待）
地點：
新亞書院雲起軒活動室  (見
位置圖
)
語言：
粵語
費用：
HK$20 (完成活動後，新亞學生可獲退還費用)
*
活動將提供麵食午餐
網上登記
：
請於2026年11月20日或之前透過以下連結網上報名
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13746262
查詢：
新亞書院輔導處王先生 （電話：3943-1690 電郵：
jackwong@cuhk.edu.hk
）或梁女士 (電話：3943-9589; 電郵：
angelaleung@cuhk.edu.hk
)。
Imagine a city where trees do more than beautify streets, where they improve public health, enhance biodiversity, mitigate climate change, and reconnect people with nature. Is such a vision achievable, or is it simply a modern-day utopia?
This Environmental Forum features
Mr. Chiky C.Y. Wong
, an ISA Board Certified Master Arborist and urban greening specialist. Drawing on his extensive experience in tree management, urban greening, and ecological conservation, Mr. Wong will explore the potential and practical challenges of developing urban forests, while inviting participants to rethink the possibilities of harmonious coexistence between nature and the city.
Whether you are interested in environmental protection, ecology, sustainability, urban planning, or simply wish to learn more about the green spaces around us, this talk promises to offer valuable insights and stimulating discussion. We warmly welcome all students and staff to join us!

藥物與我們的健康息息相關，不論是長期服用的處方藥物，或是日常使用的維他命與保健品，若使用不當，可能影響療效甚至對身體造成不必要的風險。本講座講解正確的購藥途徑、服藥注意事項、居家及旅遊藥物保存方法，協助您與家人建立正確的藥物管理習慣。

語言： 廣東話
對象： 中大全職教職員及學生

網上報名：

Health Talk organized by Robert Dan Health Education Centre, University Medical Service Office - Know My Medications
Medications play a vital role in our health. Whether taking long-term prescription medicines or daily vitamins and supplements, improper use can reduce their effectiveness or lead to unnecessary health risks. Announcements
Free PEMF Therapy for Achilles Tendinopathy – Experience Cutting-Edge Treatment (Normally HK$10,000+ Value!) 免費PEMF治療跟腱病——市值過萬療法，跟腱病患者福音！！ - Dept of Orthopaedics and Traumatology
From: Pam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wenjiepan@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
研究目的: 本研究旨在評估脈衝電磁場治療對跟腱病病患者的治療效果。
研究對象: 1. 年齡18歲或以上
2. 中段跟腱病患者患者
3. 維多利亞體育學院評估—跟腱問卷：跟腱炎的嚴重程度指數<60
內容: 脈衝電磁場治療+足部功能評估+ 復健治療
脈衝電磁場治療（PEMF）係一種無痛、非入侵性嘅新療法，研究顯示可以：
快速減輕疼痛同腫脹
促進跟腱自然修復，等你好返得更快
改善血液循環，等你可以重新輕鬆行路、行山、做運動
無需食藥、無副作用，科學實證有效！ 現誠邀您參加臨床研究，親身體驗PEMF嘅效果。
地點: 沙田威爾斯親王醫院
有興趣的參加者，請在網上登記並且填寫1份篩查問卷:
https://qualtricsxmjfcmmgpdf.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3eYVkGnolhErPAG
參加者於網上登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，所有資料將會保密。經過篩選後，研究員會以電話或WhatsApp主動聯絡合資格者，並進一步解釋治療詳情。如有任何查詢，請聯絡研究人員辦公室電話:
2636 4171
This study aims to evaluate the effect of a Pulsed Electro-Magnetic Field Therapy for Midportion Achilles Tendinopathy
Target participant:
1. > 18 years old
2. mid- Achilles tendinopathy patients
3. VISA-A score <60
Content: Pulsed electromagnetic field therapy (PEMF)+ rehabilitation exercises
Venue: Prince of Wales Hospital, Shatin, Hong Kong.
Interested participants, please fill out the following questionnaire:
https://qualtricsxmjfcmmgpdf.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3eYVkGnolhErPAG
If you are qualified we will contact you by phone or WhatsApp. If you have any enquiry about the study, please contact number:
2636 4171

bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/11/06
»
Events / Activities
Invitation to Ethereal Music Amidst the Clouds: An Evening of Traditional Chinese Music 誠邀參加「樂飄梅雲：傳統中國音樂晚會」 - New Asia College
From: New Asia College
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
nac@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
新亞書院誠邀您參加「樂飄梅雲：傳統中國音樂晚會」，於初冬時節相聚新亞校園，在悠揚樂韻中感受中華傳統音樂的深厚底蘊與魅力。
是次音樂會由中大校友國樂薈萃擔綱演出，並聯同新亞國樂會參與演出。樂團成員主要由中大校友及老師組成，將為觀眾帶來廣東音樂、江南絲竹、南音及多首經典民族器樂作品，呈現中國不同地域音樂文化的特色與風貌。
活動詳情：
日期：2026年11月19日（星期四）
時間：晚上7:15至9:15
地點：新亞書院 梅雲堂 – 許國浩堂
費用：免費入場（須預先登記）
音樂會精選曲目包括《將軍令》、《彩雲追月》、《春江花月夜》、《流波曲》、《歡樂歌》及《金蛇狂舞》等，帶領觀眾穿梭於中國傳統音樂的豐富世界。
歡迎中大學生、教職員及校友踴躍參加，與我們共度一個充滿文化氣息的音樂晚會。
網上登記：
新亞學生經RAS 系統登記:
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/eventlist?id=47
其他中大師生及校友登記:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13745205
**名額有限，先到先得。
贊助機構：
田家炳基金會
如有查詢，請聯絡新亞書院學生輔導處楊先生（電話：3943 7612；電郵：
jasonyeung@cuhk.edu.hk
）或王先生（電話：3943 1690；電郵：
jackwong@cuhk.edu.hk
）。
新亞書院校園文化委員會
New Asia College warmly invites you to join
Ethereal Music Amidst the Clouds: An Evening of Traditional Chinese Music
, and immerse yourself in the rich heritage and timeless beauty of traditional Chinese music on a delightful early winter evening at the New Asia College campus.
The concert will be presented by the CUHK Alumni Chinese Music Ensemble, with a joint performance by the New Asia Chinese Music Society. Comprising primarily CUHK alumni and teachers, the ensemble will perform a diverse repertoire of Cantonese music, Jiangnan silk and bamboo music, Nanyin, and other celebrated traditional instrumental works, showcasing the unique musical traditions and cultural characteristics of different regions of China.
Event Details:
Date: Thursday, 19 November 2026
Time: 7:15 p.m. – 9:15 p.m.
Venue: Hui Kwok Hau Hall, Mei Yun Tang, New Asia College
Admission: Free of charge (Advance registration required)
The programme features a selection of beloved classics, including “The General’s Command”, “Colorful Clouds Chasing the Moon”, “Moonlit Night on the Spring River”, “Flowing Waves”, “Song of Joy”, and “Dance of the Golden Snake”, offering audiences an enchanting journey through the rich world of traditional Chinese music.
We warmly welcome all CUHK students, staff members, and alumni to join us for an enjoyable evening of music and cultural appreciation.
Online Registration:
For New Asia students via the RAS System:
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/eventlist?id=47
For other CUHK students, staff members, and alumni:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13745205
Seats are limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.
Sponsor:
Tin Ka Ping Foundation
For enquiries, please contact Mr. Jason Yeung (Tel: 3943 7612; Email:
jasonyeung@cuhk.edu.hk
) or Mr. Jack Wong (Tel: 3943 1690; Email:
jackwong@cuhk.edu.hk
), Dean of Students’ Office, New Asia College.
Committee on College Culture,
New Asia College

From: SUE GAO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155229912@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Introduction】: This research study, titled “Compensation of White Matter Pathways and Networks in Chinese Children with Developmental Dyslexia in Hong Kong,” is led by Prof. Jingjing Zhao from the Department of Psychology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
【Description of the study】: The purpose of this study is to explore how white matter pathways in the brain may compensate for reading difficulties in Chinese-speaking children with developmental dyslexia in Hong Kong.
【Study Procedures】
● Reading and Cognitive Assessments: Your child will participate in reading and cognitive assessments lasting approximately 30–40 minutes. You are not required to complete any of these tasks.
● Brain Imaging (MRI Scan): Your child will also undergo a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan lasting about 20 minutes. The MRI procedure is non-invasive, painless, radiation-free, and no sedation. Please inform the research team in advance if your child has claustrophobia, metal implants, or a pacemaker.
Target participants: Children aged 8–16 years, whose parents are native Mandarin or Cantonese speakers, are eligible to participate.
【Data Confidentiality and Usage】:All data will be handled in accordance with data protection and privacy regulations. All collected data will be anonymized and will not include identifiable information (e.g., name, ID number, contact details). Data will be used solely for academic research purposes.
針對多種神經發育學習障礙的閱讀困難跨診斷研究
現正招募：
8-16歲、廣東話為母語的兒童
（1）正常發展或
（2）被診斷或懷疑有任何一項：
（i）自閉症
（ii）注意力缺陷
（iii）讀寫障礙
測試内容：
語言、記憶及認知能力測試
磁力共振掃描（MRI）
時間：2小时
地點：威爾士親王醫院（第一城）
合資格參與者完成所有測試後可獲得:
綜合語言能力評核報告
最高達$200 現金
兒童磁力共振影相電子版
神經指標分析報告

【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 9 November to 13 November: (1) Job Preparation Series: Writing Impressive Application Letters, (2) Writing Success: Academic Essays, (3) Writing Success: Reflective Writing, (4) Job Preparation Series: Writing Impressive Resumes, (5) Global Citizenship Series: Intercultural Communication, and (6) Job Preparation Series: Ace Your In-person and Video Job Interviews. This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。

https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/SC/index.aspx

Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html

以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html

Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.

Events / Activities
HAPPY HOUR @ The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) - 古人的情情色色 ︳ Complimentary light lunch and beverage  - ILC
From: ILC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Happy Hour @ The Independent Learning Centre (ILC)
Calling all students and staff!
Join us for a new round of Happy Hour at the ILC with fun activities and lots of laughter!
Here is what we have in store for you:
From boardgame strategies to horoscope
From chair stretching to everyday math starting with HKID numbers
From movable-type printing to ancient passions
...and ending with Wine & Cheese pairing
Sixth Event in the Series:
“
古人的情情色色
”

Date:
20 November 2026

Time:
1:00 pm – 2:00 pm

Venue:
Seminar Room, 1/F, Wu Chung Library
In ancient times, when the need to conform to socially acceptable moral standards was strong, passion and sensuality were nonetheless present in Chinese writing. So how did the ancients handle “taboo” subjects such as romantic fulfillment, lust, and wild fantasies on sex?  Reading ancient Chinese erotic literature often challenges one's worldview, casting doubt on our taken-for-granted assumptions. Are you ready to explore culture through a new lens and uncover an alternative aspect of our historical antecedents?
Join us for an hour of food, drinks, joy and good vibes before kickstarting your weekend!
Register NOW at:
https://ilc.link/HH2026

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

bodyText:

2026/11/06

Announcements
(Earn $700!!!) Recruiting adults aged 18–65 who have recovered from depression to participate in a study on depression recurrence (participants on medication are welcome if condition is medically stable)  (獲得 $700!!!) 誠邀年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與預測抑鬱症復發相關的研究(歡迎仍在服藥但病情穩定者參加) - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，探討運用語音分析能否預測抑鬱症復發。現招募年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與研究。詳情如下：
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者
廣東話為母語
使用智慧型手機並可持續連接互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
接受臨床評估作為篩查
填寫問卷
連續
7
天
於指定的手機應用程式以語音方式記錄情緒狀態
一年後接受跟進臨床評估
完成整個實驗及跟進評估，可以獲得最多HK$700作為研究津貼
如有興趣參與研究，請按以下連結填寫篩選問卷。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e9b0QXbpcuCUxrE
若您適合參與研究，研究人員會聯絡您解釋研究詳情。
閣下留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp:(+852- 53202853)。
If you are interested, please complete the following screening questionnaire.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e9b0QXbpcuCUxrE
If you are suitable for participating in the study, the researchers will contact you to explain the study details.
Information collected will be only used for research purposes and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852-53202853).

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Announcements
Student Intern Recruitment - Digital Mental Health Research Team  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Are you interested in mental health research and looking for hands-on research experience?
The Artificial Intelligence and Digital Mental Health Research Team, Department of Psychiatry, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is recruiting Student Interns to support ongoing research projects in digital mental health.
K
ey
Responsibilities
Download, organize, and manage study data and PDF reports from Qualtrics
Perform data entry, verification, and database maintenance
Maintain participant records and research documentation
Serve as a secondary rater for selected clinical interviews following training
Assist with other research-related tasks as required
Requirements
Proficiency in spoken Cantonese
Strong attention to detail and sense of responsibility
Basic computer skills (e.g., Excel, Word)
Good interpersonal and communication skills
Eligibility
Year 2 or above undergraduate students from Psychology, Medicine, Public Health, Social Sciences, Nursing, or other related disciplines are welcome to apply.
Working Location:
Prince of Wales Hospital
Principal Investigator:
Professor Li Man Ho
Internship Type
: Unpaid internship
Application form:
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/a2DNZycEz0
你是否對精神健康研究感興趣，並希望獲得實際研究經驗？
香港中文大學精神學系李朝江家族睡眠檢查室的研究團隊現正招募學生實習生，協助團隊進行各項研究及行政工作。
主要職責
整理及管理研究數據和從 Qualtrics 下載PDF 報告
進行資料輸入、核對及資料庫維護工作
維護研究參與者紀錄及研究文件
接受培訓後，擔任部分臨床訪談的第二評分員
協助處理其他研究相關工作
申請要求
能說流利廣東話
做事細心、認真負責
具備基本電腦技能（如 Excel、Word）
具良好人際溝通能力
申請資格
大學二年級或以上本科生，並修讀心理學、醫學、公共衞生、社會科學、護理學或其他相關學科
工作地點：
威爾斯親王醫院
首席研究員：
李汶浩博士
實習性質：
非受薪實習

bodyText:

Announcements
(Earn $200!!) Recruiting teenagers (aged 18 to 24) to participate in depressive disorder study (welcome healthy people) (獲得 $200!!)誠邀18-24歲青少年參加與抑鬱症狀相關的研究(歡迎健康人士) - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，主要探討運用語音分析檢測青少年的憂鬱症狀。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲的青少年參與研究，歡迎所有健康人士、抑鬱和焦慮人士參加。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至24歲青少年,
除了抑鬱和焦慮外，沒有確診其他精神障礙
能說流利的廣東話
使用智慧型手機（附錄音機）並可持續存取互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
通過篩查訪談後，在手機
連續 7 天
使用指定的訊息應用程式
使用手機上的錄音功能進行數位語音錄音，包括（a）指定的段落閱讀和（b）引導音訊日記。
每天
早上
和
晚上
，在應用程式分別回答4個指導性問題
進行跟進訪談
完成實驗及跟進評估後，可以獲得$200現金津貼。
有興趣的參加者請按以下連結填寫問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_801s3xAKvKm1Uma
研究員將通過WhatsApp聯絡合適的參加者，並詳細解釋研究內容。
閣下留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp:(+852- 53202853)。
For participants who are interested, please click the link below to complete the questionnaire:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_801s3xAKvKm1Uma
The research team will contact eligible participants via WhatsApp to explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purposes and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852-53202853).

title: Recruiting volunteers for "HK Farmability" Board Game Ambassador 港農物語推廣義工招募
bodyText:

Events / Activities
Recruiting volunteers for "HK Farmability" Board Game Ambassador 港農物語推廣義工招募 - Lee Woo Sing College
From: Ricky Tai
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rickytai@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Become a "HK Farmability" Board Game Ambassador!
Are you interested in education, environmental protection, or local agriculture?
Do you enjoy playing board games?
Would you like to step into schools and bring meaningful issues to students?
We are a group of students designed an
original board game "HK Farmability 港農物語,
" where students role-play as local farmers and experience the real challenges of Hong Kong agriculture—weather changes, market fluctuations, and land pressure—while learning about the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). No pressure at all! Play, learn, and have fun—while gaining a deeper understanding of Hong Kong and sharing what you've learned through voluntary service!
"HK Farmability" is supported by Lee Woo Sing College. We are now recruiting university volunteer ambassadors! Even if you are unable to attend the service sessions, you are welcome to join the HK Farmability training and workshop to try out the game. GLA students can also earn GLA points!
Your Role:
Attend a one-day training to learn the board game rules and facilitation skills
Work in small groups to visit secondary schools
Lead 45-minute (or longer) workshops—teach the secondary school students while playing
Guide students to reflect on their game experience and connect it to real-world issues
What You Will Gain:
Complete training (Hong Kong agriculture background + board game rules + facilitation skills)
Standardised lesson plans and facilitator's guidebook

Volunteer hours
(only applicable to those who attend service sessions; training hours are also counted and can be used for hour-based certificate applications) (e.g. Agency for Volunteer Service)

GLA points for GLA students (for students from Lee Woo Sing College):
Participating in training/workshop: 0.5 activity point
Participating in service activities (optional; priority given to those who have attended training): 0.5 contribution point per session
Activity Details:
Training / Workshop:
16 November 2026 (Monday)
18:45 – 20:30
Agnes Lau Seminar Room, LG1, Lee Woo Sing College
Introduction to Hong Kong's agricultural situation and SDG background, board game rules explanation, guest sharing on farming experience, board game trial play
Provisional Service Dates:
(Interested participants may join more than one service session and earn corresponding service hours and GLA points)
27 November 2026 (Fri) AM
4 December 2026 (Fri) 13:30–14:10
22 January 2027 (Fri) 16:00–18:00
29 January 2027 (Fri) 16:00–17:00
If you have any enquiries or if you would like to join this meaningful project, please contact with Mr. Anson LAW via wscollege@cuhk.edu.hk.

拍攝現場聽得最多「後期搞得啦！」——真係得！？
由短片、電視劇撈到金像電影嘅現役「剪片佬」，話你聽點樣撐住一間「急救房」！
《拍片唔難：影片製作入門工作坊系列》第二場業界分享會，帶你走入香港電影剪接師嘅真實世界，探討重塑故事嘅無限可能。
今場分享會，你將會瞭解到：

入行實錄
｜香港電影剪接師嘅入行經過與生存之道。

踩過界發展
｜剪接 x 導演 x 發行，點樣喺影視圈多元發展？

終極指南
｜俾想入行同學嘅「避坑」與實戰建議。
嘉賓講者
鄭偉麟
｜香港電影剪接師
剪接作品：
《逆流大叔》、《飯戲攻心》、《
4
拍

家族》、《夜王》

ilc.link/filming

Subject: 研究資助局公眾講座 -
兒童發展、學習與家庭介入
(Research Grants Council Public Lectures to be conducted in Cantonese)
香港高等院校進行了很多令人振奮的學術研究計劃。為了讓市民更了解本地研究的重要性及價值，研究資助局定期舉辦公眾講座，向大眾分享最新研究成果。
研資局將於今年﹙2026﹚舉辦一系列與STEAM教育相關的公眾講座，講題包括人工智能與文物保育、網上訂價、兒童教育及宇宙探索。這些講座旨在提升市民對相關方面最新研究成果的認識。講座詳細內容如下：講座以粵語進行。免費入場，座位先到先得，有興趣人士亦可於網上收看講座現場直播或稍後重温。詳細內容如下：(
https://www.ugc.edu.hk/big5/rgc/about/events/lectures/lectures.html
)
The Hong Kong higher education sector has undertaken many exciting academic research projects. To raise public awareness of the significance and values of the local research work, the Research Grants Council regularly organises public lectures to share the latest research results with the public.
This year (2026), the RGC has organised a series of public lectures related to STEAM education, covering topics including cultural preservation with artificial intelligence, online pricing, children education, and universe exploration (conducted in Cantonese). These lectures aim to enhance the awareness of the latest researches in related areas. Please refer to Chinese version for more details.

陳果導演作品放映及映後座談
香港有個荷里活 (2002)｜導演：陳果
金像獎導演陳果以超現實色彩交織出一則關於階級、慾望與都市變遷的寓言。導演藉由木屋區與摩天大樓的並置，以黑色幽默與荒誕現實主義的筆觸，書寫後九七時期香港的集體焦慮。
是次活動將先放映全片，映後特別邀請導演陳果親臨現場，圍繞獨立電影精神、社會地景與角色塑造等展開深度對談，並設現場 Q&A 環節。
二十餘載閃逝，大磡村早已消失。重溫這部作品，讓我們可以探討城市重組、邊緣命運與身份認同的演變。誠邀各位一同蒞臨，重新審視香港。
電影榮獲第39屆金馬獎最佳導演、最佳造型設計及最佳音效；以及第9屆香港電影評論學會大獎最佳編劇與推薦電影。
日期：2026年11月17日（星期二）
時間：7:00 - 9:00 pm（放映）｜晚上 9:00 - 9:30 pm（映後座談及問答環節）
地點：康本國際學術園一號演講廳（YIA LT-1）
放映作品：香港有個荷里活（2002年，108分鐘，中文字幕）
座談嘉賓：陳果導演
對象：中大學生及教職員、校友及公眾人士
費用：免費參加，先到先得
即時報名：
報名《香港有個荷里活》電影放映及座談
合辦單位：山城影院 (OSA) ｜ 自學中心 (ILC) ｜ 書寫力量 ｜ 中大電影學會
Director Fruit Chan Film Screening & Post-Screening Q&A
Award-winning director Fruit Chan uses surrealist elements to craft a dark fable about class, desire, and urban transformation. By contrasting a squatter village with neighboring luxury skyscrapers, the film employs dark humor and absurd realism to capture the collective anxiety of post-1997 Hong Kong.
The event will begin with a full screening of the film, followed by an in-depth conversation with Director Fruit Chan himself. He will share his insights on the spirit of independent filmmaking, social landscapes, and character development, followed by a Q&A session.
More than two decades have flown by, and Dai Hom Village has long since vanished. Revisiting this masterpiece allows us to explore urban redevelopment, marginalization, and the evolution of cultural identity. We invite you to join us and rediscover Hong Kong through his lens.
Hollywood Hong Kong won Best Director, Best Makeup & Costume Design, and Best Sound Effects at the 39th Golden Horse Awards. It was also awarded Best Screenplay and named a Recommended Film at the 9th Hong Kong Film Critics Society Awards.
Event Details
Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026
Time: 7:00 PM - 9:00 PM (Screening), 9:00 PM - 9:30 PM (Post-screening Talk & Q&A)
Venue: Yasumoto International Academic Park, Lecture Theatre 1 (YIA LT-1)
Screening Title: Hollywood Hong Kong (2002, 108 mins, with Chinese subtitles)
Guest Speaker: Film Director Fruit Chan
Target Audience: CUHK students, staff, alumni, and the public
Admission: Free (First-come, first-served)

  [Online experiment] Looking for native English speakers 
Prof. Haerim Hwang (Department of English, CUHK) is looking for participants for a study on language production.
Which participants are we looking for?
- English is your first/native and dominant language
- Your graduate degree is not in the field of linguistics
- Can use your laptop/computer and have access to stable internet (no smartphones, laptops, or hotspot)
- Can participate in an experiment on Zoom in a quiet environment
- Have Chrome on your laptop/computer
How do I participate?
1. Fill out this questionnaire
-- English speakers: https://forms.gle/ttuhGGCwRx2n95kBA
2. Our research team will reach out to you, confirming your availability.
3. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete these tasks.
What do I get out of the study?
You will get HK$250 in cash upon the completion of the task.
Your participation will enhance our understanding of how people process English sentences.
Questions?
Contact Prof. Haerim Hwang at haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk

From: Fong Ki Tuen
