2026 中大劇賽招募中
一個舞台，四間劇社，幕幕屬於你我的故事
你喜歡劇場嗎？
你喜歡與一群志同道合的夥伴共同進退嗎？
無論你是戲劇愛好者、表演新手，還是希望有新嘗試，現在就是踏上舞台的最佳時機。
中大劇賽匯聚各個劇社，透過戲劇創作與演出，展現獨特的故事和創作理念。從編劇、導演、演員、舞台管理、燈光、音響、服裝，以至前台及宣傳工作，每一個崗位都不可或缺，才能共同成就一部作品。
為籌備 2026 中大劇賽，以下劇社現正招募臺前幕後工作人員：
聯合劇社
逸夫劇社
和聲劇社
伍宜孫劇社
立即聯絡各劇社報名參加，親身體驗由排練到公演的製作歷程，結識一群熱愛戲劇的夥伴，一同創造屬於你們的舞臺故事。
無論你有沒有戲劇經驗，只要你對劇場充滿好奇與熱情，2026 中大劇賽都歡迎你的參與。
One Stage. Four Drama Societies. Countless Stories Waiting to Be Told.
Do you love theatre?
Are you looking to be part of a passionate team and work towards a shared goal?Whether you're a theatre enthusiast, a first-time performer, or simply someone looking for a new challenge, now is the perfect time to get involved.
The CUHK Drama Competition brings together students from different Colleges and drama societies across the University to create and stage original productions. It is a celebration of creativity, collaboration, and storytelling, where diverse artistic styles and ideas come to life on stage.Whatever your interests or experience level, there is a place for you in the theatre.
To prepare for the 2026 CUHK Drama Competition, the following drama societies are now recruiting both cast and crew members:
United Drama Society
Shaw Drama Society
Wo Sing Drama Society
Wu Yee Sun Drama Society
Join one of the drama societies today and experience the full theatre-making journey, from the first rehearsal to opening night. Meet like-minded friends, discover new talents, and help bring unforgettable stories to life.
No theatre experience? No problem.
All you need is curiosity, enthusiasm, and a willingness to learn.
Come be part of the 2026 CUHK Drama Competition and create something extraordinary together.

For enquiries, please write to:

【
#CUbicZine
】 從零起步到被跨國企業收購｜飛的創辦人蕭達文的創業與突圍之道
近年全球創科浪潮洶湧，初創企業如雨後春筍，然而在跨國巨頭大打「燒錢戰」的激烈競爭下，本地科技平台要由零突圍並持續生存，箇中挑戰實不容小覷。在急速變化的市場裡，如何把校園所學化為貼地應用，更是知識轉移的重要實踐。
「在一個變化迅速的世界裡，最大的風險，反而是完全不願冒險。」——這是香港本地網約的士平台「飛的」創辦人、中大信息工程校友蕭達文（Simon）謹守的創業信條。從當年拋開包袱在旺角街頭舉牌推廣，到凌晨三點系統崩潰時冷靜「救火」，他總是以「打機」心態看待挫折，在不確定性中展現出工程師務實而堅韌的本色。
今期《CUbicZine》專訪 Simon，聽他細說從一個業餘 side project 發展成月訂單破百萬、最終被 Uber 收購的十餘年創業路。面對資本巨擘，他憑藉對香港市場的敏銳洞察與敏捷開發，開創出屬於小公司的突圍之道。走過商業巔峰，如今他選擇轉向教育與非牟利領域，將實戰心法反哺校園與社會——「願意冒險，能夠孤獨、持續地做事」，為有志創業的中大人樹立兼具魄力與溫度的榜樣。
▍ 閱讀專訪
【CUbicZine 2026年10月號】從零起步到被跨國企業收購｜飛的創辦人蕭達文的創業與突圍之道 - CUHK InnoPort
專訪重點
▍ 從小試牛刀到百萬平台：以本土敏捷打法打破跨國巨頭壟斷
▍ 凌晨三點的救火日常：工程思維化解危機，把挫折視為升級經驗
▍ 功成身退後再出發：商業終局並非終點，以實戰心法育才傳燈
【CUbicZine】From Zero to Acquisition | How FlyTaxi Founder Simon Siu Navigated Challenges and Built Success
In recent years, the global innovation and technology landscape has accelerated rapidly, seeing startups mushroom across sectors. Yet against the backdrop of fierce competition and aggressive subsidy wars waged by multinational giants, building a homegrown tech platform from scratch and sustaining real-world viability presents an entirely different set of challenges. In such a fast-evolving market, turning campus learning into practical, down-to-earth solutions has become a compelling practice of knowledge transfer.
In this issue of CUbicZine, Simon Siu, a CUHK Information Engineering alumnus and founder of FLY TAXI (“飛的”), reflects on more than a decade of entrepreneurship—from a weekend side project to scaling a platform handling over one million monthly orders, and ultimately achieving an acquisition by Uber. For him, competing with global giants was not about outspending them, but about agility, deep local insight, and an engineer’s pragmatic mindset. Guided by his belief that “the biggest risk in a rapidly changing world is not taking any risks at all,” he weathered everything from street-level leafleting to 3 a.m. system crashes, treating every setback like leveling up in a game.
Having scaled the heights of commercial success, his greatest satisfaction now comes from giving back—stepping into education and mentorship to help aspiring campus innovators navigate the market, embrace calculated risks, and make a visible difference in society.

bodyText:

AI Ethics & Research Integrity Workshops  - CUHK Library
From: CUHK Library
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
research@lib.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Join us for the AI Ethics & Research Integrity Workshops. All CUHK students and staff are welcome.
1. Responsible Use of AI in Medical Research
Description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming medical research in numerous ways. This transformation is visible across five trends with ethical implications: AI is moving upward in the research workflow, from editing assistance toward hypothesis generation and analysis; the consistency and quality of publications are under pressure; increasingly autonomous AI agents are appearing as core contributors, supporting contributors, and even as research participants; disclosure remains a sticky and unevenly practiced issue; and AI is entering research oversight, where errors, bias, confidentiality breaches, deskilling, and unclear attribution carry particular weight.This interactive session will offer practical responses to these trends and provide an opportunity to exchange ideas and learn more about the ethical implications of using AI.
Date and Time:
18 Nov 2026 (Wed) 2:30 p.m.–4:30 p.m.
Venue:
User Education Room G/F, University Library
Registration:
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/event?id=117972
2. Doing Science With Generative AI: From AI Slop to Responsible AI
Description:
The increasing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in scholarship has generated concerns about the quality, integrity, and reliability of outputs. Public discussions often contrast AI slop, characterized by heavily automated, poorly validated, and low-quality content, with responsible AI use, in which researchers employ AI tools transparently, critically, and with appropriate human oversight. These should be understood as the two ends of a spectrum. Between these poles lies a range of intermediate grey practices, including what has recently been described as vibe scholarship: the production of apparently credible academic work through substantial AI assistance while the author’s engagement with, understanding of, or validation of the underlying arguments, evidence, methods, or literature may be limited. Conceptualizing AI-assisted research as a continuum provides a framework for evaluating scholarly practices based on numerous factors, and can inform discussions about authorship, research integrity, peer review, and the responsible governance of AI in science.
Date and Time:
19 Nov 2026 (Thu) 2:30 p.m. – 3:30 p.m.
Venue:
Zoom and User Education Room, G/F, University Library
Online mode registration
:
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/event?id=117976
In-person mode registration
:
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/event?id=117974
Speaker:
Dr. Mohammad Hosseini is an Assistant Professor at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, Department of Preventive Medicine, specializing in research integrity, AI ethics, and open science. He is the co-editor in chief of
Accountability in Research
, and a member of the Global Young Academy. As a researcher and educator, he promotes the responsible integration of AI into research, aiming to help researchers anticipate risks, uphold scientific integrity, and engage thoughtfully with social and environmental impacts of their work.
If you have any questions, please contact the Research and Learning Support team, CUHK Library at
research@lib.cuhk.edu.hk
.

Dear Students,
Co-op@CUHK Field Trip to Beijing (19 - 24 Dec 2026)
Have you ever wondered what it is like to experience China's dynamic business environment and technological innovation first-hand? This winter, Co-op@CUHK invites you to join an exciting six-day field trip to Beijing and explore one of the world's most vibrant economic and cultural centres!
Organised by the
Office of Co-operative Education Programme (OCEP)
, the Co-op@CUHK Field Trip to Beijing will take place from 19 to 24 December 2026. Through visits to leading enterprises, renowned universities, and iconic cultural landmarks, participants will gain a deeper understanding of China's economic development, technological advancement, and rich cultural heritage. The field trip is designed to broaden students' perspectives, enhance their global awareness, and provide valuable insights into emerging industries and career opportunities.
This credit-bearing field trip is associated with COOP1001 Field Trip to China, and participating students will be enrolled in the course in Term 2, 2026-27. Upon successful completion of the field trip and fulfilment of course requirements, students will earn 1 unit.
Please refer to the attached poster for field trip details, itinerary highlights, and package information.
Registrants will be notified of the application result in late November 2026.
All
successful applicants will be required to attend a mandatory pre-trip briefing session, tentatively scheduled for early December 2026.
Please note that the package fee does not include visa application fees. Students who require a visa are responsible for arranging their own visa applications. Payment details will be provided in the confirmation email.
If you are interested in joining this unique learning journey, please register [
here
] by
23:59, 10 November 2026 (Tuesday)
. As places are limited, applications will be processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
Beyond industry immersion field trips,
Co-op@CUHK
aims to develop students’ workplace competencies and career-readiness skills, followed by a 6-to-8-month full-time, full-pay placement with one of our 150+ corporate partners across Hong Kong, the Chinese Mainland, and Asia! Open to Year 2 and above local and non-local students from all disciplines,
applications for Co-op Cohort 6 are now open
. Learn more and
enrol
now!
More details on our
website
,

and

Page. For enquiries, please send an email to
coop@cuhk.edu.hk
or contact Ms. Zoe Hung at 3943 5674.
Best regards,

bodyText:

[Reminder] Call for nominations for SCGE Exemplary Teaching Award in General Education 2026  - Office of University General Education
From: Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ouge@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Members of the CUHK Community,
We are pleased to announce that nominations for the Exemplary Teaching Award in General Education 2026 are now open.  This Award is presented annually to recognize teachers for their outstanding contributions to teaching and learning in General Education (GE). Departments, Faculties, Programmes of Study, Colleges, GE teachers, and undergraduate students are welcome to submit nominations.
Nominees should hold a full-time appointment.  All nominations, upon endorsement by heads of the respective units, will be reviewed by SCGE and its Standing Committee, with primary consideration given to evidence of sustained excellence in the nominee’s contributions to GE.  Relevant supporting documentation, including records of the nominee’s contributions to GE during the past two academic years (i.e. 2024-25 and 2025-26 for the current call) should be submitted to facilitate the evaluation.  Contributions to teaching and learning will be evaluated based on the following objectives of the CUHK GE Programme and expectations of GE courses:
Objectives of CUHK GE Programme:
Provide a broad intellectual perspective and to instill an understanding of the values of different academic disciplines;
Develop sensitivity to the common concerns of human existence especially from the perspective of the Chinese culture;
Help students develop their own judgment and sense of values;
Cultivate awareness of the connections among different fields of knowledge; to develop the potentiality for integrating different fields of knowledge as needed; and
Equip students with life-long learning capacities especially through understanding of the connections between academic pursuits and life experience.
Expectations of GE courses:
GE courses should be at the same intellectual level as major courses, and should carry the same workload as major courses with the same number of units.
Upon receipt of each nomination, the Office of University General Education (OUGE), as the secretariat of SCGE, will contact the nominee concerned directly for the required supporting materials.  More information about the Award can be found on the OUGE website:
https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/oge/eta
.  Nominations should be made through the
online nomination form
by 16 November 2026.
For any inquiries, feel free to contact us at
ouge@cuhk.edu.hk
or call us at 3943 7075.
Thank you for helping us recognize the exceptional educators who contribute to our community.
Best regards,
Office of University General Education

活動地點： 沙田區（詳細地址將於成功報名後通知）
活動內容：(所需時間約一小時)
1. 影片講解：深入淺出地介紹前列腺增生及前列腺癌的檢查與治療知識。
2. 前列腺篩查：合資格人士可獲免費前列腺特異抗原（PSA）測試乙次.
• 測試方式：我們將以指尖採血方式為參加者抽取血液樣本，並透過PSA檢測機進行現場測試，約十分鐘即可得知結果。

• 性別：男性
• 年齡：50-75歲
• 從未接受前列腺相關檢查

https://urologycentre.com.hk/zh-hant/diseases/detail/how-to-investigate-and-make-diagnosis-for-prostate-cance
r
參加者提供的所有資料將會被保密。如有任何查詢，請與我們聯絡 （Whatsapp: 5160 6904；電郵：yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk）。
According to data from the Department of Health, prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers among men in Hong Kong. Early screening can effectively reduce related health risks. This event is organized by the S.H. Ho Urology Centre of CUHK, providing free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) testing services for eligible individuals.
Event Venue: Shatin District (the exact address will be provided after successful registration)
Event Details: (Estimated duration: about one hour)
Video Presentation: An easy-to-understand introduction to the examination and treatment of prostate cancer and benign prostatic hyperplasia
Prostate Screening: Eligible participants will receive one free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) test.
Testing Method: We will collect blood samples from participants via a fingertip blood test and conduct an on-site PSA test using a PSA testing device. Results will be available in about ten minutes.
Eligibility:
Gender: Male
Age: 50-75 years old
Have never undergone any prostate-related examination
If you are interested in participating, please fill in the online form below;
https://forms.office.com/r/HRJspBWSW6
For more information about the assessment of prostate cancer risk, please visit the following website:
https://urologycentre.com.hk/zh-hant/diseases/detail/how-to-investigate-and-make-diagnosis-for-prostate-cancer
All information provided by participants will be kept confidential. For any enquiries, please contact us (WhatsApp: 5160 6904; Email: yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk)

title: [6 Nov Anthropology Friday Seminar] Huang Shan, "The Limits of Experiment: Place- and Life-Making at the Edge of Hong Kong"
bodyText:

[6 Nov Anthropology Friday Seminar] Huang Shan, "The Limits of Experiment: Place- and Life-Making at the Edge of Hong Kong"  - Anthropology
From: M.W.Leung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
anthropology@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Title: The Limits of Experiment: Place- and Life-Making at the Edge of Hong Kong
Speaker: Huang Shan (Centre for Cultural Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Date: Friday 6 November, 2026
Time: 1:00-2:30pm
Mode: In-person
Venue: Room 114, Humanities Building, New Asia College, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Abstract:
This talk explores a decade of experiments in agricultural revitalization and community-building in a seaside town on Lantau Island. Drawing on fieldwork and collaborative research since 2016, I follow a cohort of young community organizers for whom crafting alternative ways of living and remaking places became a single endeavor, pursued through engagements with land, food, local history, and social networks at different scales. Initially sparked by debates over land reclamation and development on Lantau, these attempts gradually took on multiple forms. I focus on two dimensions of this work: turning harvests from scattered small farms into products under a shared community brand, and cultivating an open-ended network of relationships within and beyond the local community. Attending to the labor, improvisation, and negotiations involved, I draw on theories of experiment and the politics of life to consider what these efforts made possible and where they reached their limits. Whereas analyses of Hong Kong’s politics and culture often privilege major events, moments of rupture, and particular forms of action, this talk traces these experiments alongside the changing lives of those who sustained them, asking how a different understanding of activist personhood and theory of change might help us rethink the legacies and afterlives of social activism.
Bio:
Huang Shan received his PhD in Anthropology from Stanford University in 2024 and is a Postdoctoral Fellow at the Centre for Cultural Studies at CUHK. His research explores the intersections of political anthropology, urban studies, critical theory, and public humanities. He is developing a book project that examines Hong Kong s post-Handover political culture through the politics of space, time, and life, drawing on long-term collaborative research embedded in experimental socio-environmental projects on the city s urban peripheries. He is interested in enabling new interfaces between intellectual work and social life through new methodology, ethics, and aesthetics. He co-authored
Reappearing Mui Wo
(Typesetter, 2024).

Multicultural Psychological Support Service (MPSS) – English Mental Health First Aid Course for Non-local
students
Dear Students,
To strengthen non-local students' resilience and equip students to cope with life’s challenges, sign up for the 12-hour Mental Health First Aid Standard Course taught by qualified counsellors who are certified MHFA trainers by The Mental Health Association of Hong Kong.
Upon completion of the course, participants will be able to:
Identify the signs and symptoms of common mental health and substance use challenges;
Provide someone with initial support until they are connected with appropriate professional help;
Identify risk factors and warning signs for mental health and addiction concerns; and
Learn strategies to help someone in both crisis and non-crisis situations, and know where to turn for help.

To strengthen non-local students' resilience and equip students to cope with life’s challenges, sign up for the 12-hour Mental Health First Aid Standard Course taught by qualified counsellors who are certified MHFA trainers by The Mental Health Association of Hong Kong.
Upon completion of the course, participants will be able to:
Identify the signs and symptoms of common mental health and substance use challenges;
Provide someone with initial support until they are connected with appropriate professional help;
Identify risk factors and warning signs for mental health and addiction concerns; and
Learn strategies to help someone in both crisis and non-crisis situations, and know where to turn for help.

Dear Students,
You are invited to participate in a CUHK research study exploring university students' learning experiences and how students respond to changing technology and unfamiliar situations.
Participation involves:
A short PRE survey (approximately 10 minutes) now.
A POST survey (approximately 10 minutes) in December 2026.
As a token of appreciation, the first 25 eligible students who complete the PRE survey will receive a HK$50 coupon. An additional HK$50 coupon will be offered to these participants upon completion of the POST survey.
Each student is eligible for one coupon per survey only. Duplicate submissions will not qualify for additional coupons.
Participation is entirely voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential and will not affect your academic standing.

Dear colleagues and students,
The Center for Archaeology and Cultural Heritage Studies (CACHS) invites you to two public lectures by Graeme Were, Honorary Professor of Anthropology at the University of Bristol and Distinguished Visiting Professor at Minjiang University. The talks explore the role of museums in traditions of care across Asia, and how archives shape family memory and social repair in Vietnam.
Archives, Families and the Search for Information: Prison Museums, Memory Politics and Social Repair in Vietnam
Speaker: Graeme Were, Honorary Professor of Anthropology, University of Bristol, and Distinguished Visiting Professor, Minjiang University
Date and time: Tuesday, 10 November 2026, 4:30 pm-6:15pm
Venue: CUHK ELB LT1 (利黃瑤璧樓 LT1室)
Moderator: Cheung Chin Hung Sidney, Professor, Dept. Anthropology
Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13744146
Both talks will be delivered in English and are open to the public. Please register in advance for each talk you wish to attend.
We look forward to seeing you.
Best Regards,

Announcements
【12 weeks weight loss program】 Recruiting individuals with central obeisty aged 40-64 in the study  【12週科學減重計劃】中央肥胖改善計劃誠邀40-64歲合資格人士參與 - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education; Program Director: Prof. Eric Tsz-chun POON
From: HE Ye
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
heye@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學體育運動科學系誠邀中央肥胖人士參與健康管理研究！
研究目的：
中央肥胖與血糖異常、心血管疾病及其他代謝健康問題的風險增加有關。為應對這一公共健康挑戰，香港中文大學體育運動科學系正開展健康生活方式計劃，提供個人化健康支援。
參加條件：
年齡：40-64歲
平時少做運動/無規律運動習慣
中央肥胖：男性腰圍 ≥ 90 cm; 女性腰圍 ≥ 80 cm
過去三個月體重變動≤5%
現時沒有服用長期藥物
參加方法：
掃描海報二維碼或通過鏈接作網上登記【
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2bLgS3k7oUW0TMa
】
研究團隊會進行初步篩選，以了解您是否符合基本參加資格
成功通過初步篩選後，預約檢查時間
前往香港中文大學汾陽體育館參加檢查
如果符合參加條件，將會被隨機分組，正式開展後續正式的生活方式干預計劃
參與地點：
香港中文大學汾陽體育館G02室
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
何小姐
WhatsApp: 94463265
電郵: heye@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[
數據安全聲明
]
所有檢測結果加密儲存，僅供研究團隊匿名分析，您可隨時要求刪除個人資料
[
歡迎邀請身邊感興趣的親友參加
]
Study Purpose:
Central obesity is associated with an increased risk of abnormal glucose regulation, cardiovascular disease, and other metabolic health problems. To help address this growing public health concern, the Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is launching a Healthy Lifestyle Program that offers personalized health support for individuals with central obesity.
Recruitment criteria:
Aged between 40 and 64 years
No regular exercise habits
Central obesity: waist circumference ≥ 90 cm for men and ≥ 80 cm for women
Body weight fluctuation ≤5% in the past three months
Not taking any chronic medication
Study arrangement:
Scan the QR code to register (
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2bLgS3k7oUW0TMa
)
The study team will select participants based on the registration information
Arrange a screening time
Arrive at CUHK Kwok Sports Building for the test
If you are eligible, you will be randomly assigned to start the formal Healthy Lifestyle Intervention Program
Study Location:
Room G02, Kwok Sports Building, Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin
Contact Us
If you are interested and have any inquiries, please feel free to contact us:
Ms. He
WhatsApp: 94463265
Email: heye@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[Data safety] All data obtained during the study will be kept strictly confidential
.
[Welcome to invite friends and family who are interested in participating in our study]

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

2026-2027 Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS)
The Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS) is a voluntary, self-financed dental service scheme offered through the University’s contracted service providers,
Health & Care Dental Services Limited
and
Quality HealthCare Dental Services Limited
.
The Scheme aims to provide eligible University members with the added convenience of receiving dental services at participating off-campus dental clinics at concessionary rates.  Full-time students, full-time staff and their dependents, as well as eligible retirees and their dependents, are eligible to enroll in the Scheme.
The Scheme is now open for applications.  Membership is valid from
1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027
.
For details of the Scheme, please visit the following webpage:
https://www.umso.cuhk.edu.hk/form-download/
2026-2027
自費牙科服務計劃
「自費牙科服務計劃」是一項自願參加及自行支付費用的牙科保健計劃，由大學委聘的牙科服務提供者
恒健牙科服務有限公司
及
卓健牙科服務有限公司
提供服務。
本計劃旨在為合資格的大學成員提供更便捷的選擇，讓參加者可於校外指定牙科診所享用優惠收費的牙科服務。 全日制學生、全職職員及其家屬、以及合資格退休員工及其家屬均可參加本計劃。

香港中文大學中醫學院中西醫結合醫務中心
中大中醫健康月
中醫義診服務
中大中醫診所舉行「中大中醫健康月」活動，以中醫養生理念為基礎，提倡預防保健及慢性病調理，為社區人士提供專業的中醫健康支援。活動內容包括中醫義診服務、巡迴展覽及其他推廣活動等。
現誠意邀請您參加我們的中醫義診服務，享免診金優惠。
無論您是關注日常健康，或正與慢性病同行，都歡迎參與，一同探索中醫智慧，邁向更健康的生活。
中醫義診服務詳情﹕
指定診所﹕
香港中文大學中醫學院中西醫結合醫務中心
地址﹕沙田威爾斯親王醫院舊座4樓4L
活動日期﹕
9/11/2026 – 9/12/2026
合資格對象﹕
新症病人 或 一年內未曾到中大中醫診所求診之人士
收費﹕
優惠期內可享﹕
內科診金﹕全免
診症連針灸﹕$290
藥費﹕$80起/ 每劑
(額外藥費另計﹕內科診症人士必須於中大中醫診所配發藥物，否則須付原額診金)
查詢及預約﹕
2873 3100 / cuscmclinics@cuhk.edu.hk

上述服務必須由香港中文大學中醫學院中西醫結合醫務中心之指定中醫師進行，所有治療服務內容將根據臨床決定。

Complimentary Chinese Medicine General Consultation
CUSCM clinic is launching the “CUSCM Wellness Month” initiative. Grounded in traditional Chinese medicine wellness principles, the campaign promotes preventive healthcare and chronic disease management, offering professional Chinese medicine health support to the community. Activities include complimentary Chinese medicine consultations, roving exhibitions and other promotional events. We sincerely invite you to participate in our complimentary Chinese medicine general consultation service and enjoy the promotional offers.
Details of Complimentary Chinese Medicine General Consultation:
Designated Clinic﹕
Integrative Medical Centre, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK
Address﹕4L, 4/F, Old Block, Prince of Wales Hospital
Promotional Period﹕
9/11/2026 – 9/12/2026

New Patients or whose have not visited CUSCM clinics within 1 year

Eligible participant could enjoy the following offers during promotional period﹕
Chinese Medicine General Consultation﹕Free of Charge
Chinese Medicine General Consultation and Acupuncture Treatment﹕$290
Chinese Medication﹕$80 up/ per dose
(Extra or precious Chinese medicines cost are excluded; medication must be dispensed at our clinics, otherwise the participant will need to pay for the original consultation fee)
Inquiry and Appointment﹕
2873 3100 / cuscmclinics@cuhk.edu.hk
Terms and Conditions﹕
The above services will be provided by designated Chinese medicine practitioner of Integrative Medical Centre, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK.
This promotion offer is applicable to new patients or whose have not visited the clinics within 1 year.
This promotional offer cannot be used in conjunction with other promotional offer and discount offer.
The above services are available in limited quota and will be offered on a first-come, first-served basis.
CUHK Chinese Medicine Clinics (CUSCM Clinics)* reserve the right of final decision.

The Chinese University of Hong Kong Chinese Medicine Specialty Clinic cum Clinical Teaching and Research Centre (CU Campus)

Announcements
A New Area A University General Education Course – “Understanding Modern China” (UGEA1555) Term 2 大學通識教育四範圍新科目：認識現代中國 （UGEA1555） - Office of University General Education
From: General Education China Programme, Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Are you interested in gaining a deeper understanding of China’s remarkable transformation over the past century and its impact on today’s world?
The Office of University General Education is pleased to introduce UGEA1555 “Understanding Modern China,” a new 3-unit General Education course (Area A: Chinese Cultural Heritage) to be offered on a pilot basis in 2026-27.
Starting from the 2027-28 academic year, “Understanding Modern China” (UGCP1000) will replace “Understanding China” (UGCP1001) as a University Core requirement for all undergraduate students. As part of the University’s preparation for this transition, UGEA1555 will be offered as a pilot course, providing students with an opportunity to explore this important subject and enjoy special flexibility in meeting graduation requirements.
Why Take UGEA1555?
“Farewell to slogans. Read, discuss, and understand modern China as it is.”
The course introduces important ideas, events and agents that have shaped the historical process of modernization in China, with a view to providing a conceptual framework for a systematic and structured understanding of modern China.
Topics
Understanding the transition from imperial to modern China: the historical perspective
Economic transformation in modern China
Social change and cultural transformation in modern China
Chinese modernization: visions for the future
Special Pilot Arrangement
Students who complete UGEA1555 with a grade of D or above may choose to use the course to fulfil either:
Three units of the Area A General Education requirement, or
Both the UGCP1001 (1-unit) requirement and two units of the Area A General Education requirement
This special arrangement offers you greater flexibility in planning your studies.

We warmly invite you to enrol in UGEA1555 “Understanding Modern China” and deepen your understanding of the historical developments, social transformations and modernization journey that continue to shape China today.
To enrol in UGEA1555 Understanding Modern China, students must satisfy one of the following enrolment requirements:
Have completed UGFH1000 In Dialogue with Humanity or UGFN1000 In Dialogue with Nature and obtained at least a passing grade; or
Enrol in UGEA1555 concurrently with UGFH1000 In Dialogue with Humanity or UGFN1000 In Dialogue with Nature in either Term 1 or Term 2.
For more information about the course, please visit the following website:

Office of University General Education
你是否有興趣深入瞭解中國在過去一個世紀中的蛻變，及其對當今世界的影響？
自2027-28 學年起，「認識現代中國」（UGCP1000）將取代「認識中國」（UGCP1001），作為所有本科生必須修讀的大學核心課程。為全面推出該科目作相關準備，大學通識教育部於2026-27學年開設UGEA1555「認識現代中國」，作為大學通識教育四範圍的一門新的3學分的科目（範圍A︰中華文化傳承），進行試教，為同學提供探索現代中國的機會，並在滿足畢業要求方面享有特別的靈活性。
為何選修
UGEA1555
？
「用知識打破壁壘，以思考撥開迷霧。」
本科目介紹中國現代化歷史進程中的重要思想、事件和推動者，提供一個系統而有條理的概念性框架，以此理解現代中國。
涵蓋課題
理解中國從帝制到共和的轉變︰歷史背景
現代中國的經濟轉型
現代中國的社會變遷和文化轉型
中國式現代化︰朝向未來的願景
特別安排（只限
UGEA1555
）
修畢UGEA1555且成績達D級或以上的學生，可選擇以此科目滿足：
大學通識教育範圍A （3學分）的要求，或
UGCP1001（1學分）及大學通識教育範圍A（2學分）的要求 。

bodyText:

CLCP4793 – Special Topics in Putonghua (Medicine & Healthcare): Master Putonghua for Medical Settings! CLCP4793 普通話專題科（醫學）：掌握醫療場景下的普通話溝通技巧！ - Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
From: Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
CLA_UPD@CUHK.EDU.HK
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
“探热”普通話點講啊？“吊鹽水“呢？普通話“體檢”原來係指“驗身”！想知多啲同醫療健康相關嘅普通話詞彙？又想改善下同內地醫護人員或者病人溝通果陣時嘅表達？咁就快啲來報名修讀CLCP4793喇！
CLCP4793 是一門高級普通話課程，課程通過模擬真實醫療語境，豐富學生的醫療及健康相關詞彙，提升學生在該領域的普通話溝通能力。對醫療場景下的普通話使用或相關話題感興趣的所有同學都可以報名修讀！

課程特色：
聚焦醫療與健康主題，提升醫療場景下的普通話表達能力
角色扮演模擬多個專科診症場景：呼吸科、消化科、心臟科、內分泌科、骨科等
邀請醫療從業者及中大醫學院教授參與分享及指導
藉助Micro-Modules 輔助學習，介紹內地醫療制度、醫學生培訓等

適合對象： 醫學院學生及對相關話題感興趣的所有中大學生
註冊方式： CUSIS
查詢： cla_upd@cuhk.edu.hk / 3943-822
Ever wondered how to say “fever check” or “IV drip” in Putonghua?
If you're curious about medical-related Putonghua vocabulary or want to improve your communication with healthcare professionals or patients from Mainland China, this course is for you!
CLCP4793
is an advanced Putonghua course designed to enrich students’ vocabulary and communication skills in medical and healthcare contexts. All CUHK students interested in the use of Putonghua in medical settings or related topics are welcome to enroll—no medical background required!

Course Highlights:
Focus on healthcare and medical topics to enhance Putonghua communication in medical settings
Role-play simulations of specialist consultations: pulmonology, gastroenterology, cardiology, endocrinology, orthopedics, etc.
Guest sharing and guidance from medical professionals and Faculty of Medicine of CUHK
Supplementary Micro-Modules introducing Mainland China’s healthcare system, medical education, and more

Who Should Join:
CUHK medical students and any students interested in medical Putonghua or healthcare-related topics

CUSIS

Consider taking CLCP4773 Putonghua Speech Training (Presentation Skills and Test Preparation)! 13.	準備普通話公開考試的同時，還想進一步提升口語表達能力？ 歡迎選修 CLCP4773普通話口才訓練（表達技巧及備考科）！ - Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
From: Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
CLA_UPD@CUHK.EDU.HK
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
CLCP4773
普通話口才訓練（表達技巧及備考科）
Putonghua Speech Training (Presentation Skills and Test Preparation)
本科為應試備考科目，由國家級普通話水平測試員授課，供計劃參加普通話公開試（PSC&COPA等）的學生修讀。
教學內容包括字詞及篇章朗讀的指導及訓練、詞語及表達方式選擇判斷訓練、名量詞搭配練習等，提供不同語境的說話指導和練習，幫助學習者在普通話字詞和篇章朗讀及說話方面達到考試要求，進一步提升口語表達能力。
This is an advanced course on Putonghua examination preparation taught by a nationally certified Putonghua Proficiency Test examiner. It is targeted at those students who will be taking a public examination in Putonghua, such as the Putonghua Shuiping Ceshi (PSC), the Computerized Oral Proficiency Assessment (COPA), etc.
The course covers instruction and practice in reading words, phrases, and passages aloud; exercises in selecting appropriate vocabulary and expressions; and practice in matching measure words with nouns. It also provides speaking guidance and practice in a variety of contexts, helping learners meet examination requirements in Putonghua word and passage reading as well as speaking, while further enhancing their spoken communication skills.

教學內容包括字詞及篇章朗讀的指導及訓練、詞語及表達方式選擇判斷訓練、名量詞搭配練習等，提供不同語境的說話指導和練習，幫助學習者在普通話字詞和篇章朗讀及說話方面達到考試要求，進一步提升口語表達能力。
This is an advanced course on Putonghua examination preparation taught by a nationally certified Putonghua Proficiency Test examiner. It is targeted at those students who will be taking a public examination in Putonghua, such as the Putonghua Shuiping Ceshi (PSC), the Computerized Oral Proficiency Assessment (COPA), etc.
The course covers instruction and practice in reading words, phrases, and passages aloud; exercises in selecting appropriate vocabulary and expressions; and practice in matching measure words with nouns. It also provides speaking guidance and practice in a variety of contexts, helping learners meet examination requirements in Putonghua word and passage reading as well as speaking, while further enhancing their spoken communication skills.

bodyText:

Announcements
CLCC2903 Medical Cantonese II – Advance Your Clinical Communication in Cantonese!  - Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
From: Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
CLA_UPD@CUHK.EDU.HK
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Do you know how to discuss patient history or mental health in Cantonese?
Want to learn how to handle emergencies, surgical procedures, or sensitive conversations like palliative care in a hospital setting?
CLCC2903 is an intermediate-level course designed for CUHK students who wish to deepen their Cantonese skills in medical contexts.
Course Highlights:
Focus on Cantonese used in clinical scenarios: history taking, surgery, emergencies, mental health, and more
Role-play and interactive tasks based on real-life hospital settings
Learn how to communicate with empathy on sensitive topics such as bad news delivery and end-of-life care
Learning Outcomes:
Participate in simple conversations on medical topics
Use learned vocabulary and sentence structures in short connected utterances
Communicate fluently in real-life healthcare interactions
Format & Assessment:
3-hour face-to-face lectures
Presentation (30%) | Participation (20%) | Test/Quiz (50%)
Open to:
All CUHK students, especially those who have taken CLCC1903 or have basic Cantonese proficiency and wish to enhance their clinical communication skills
Registration:
CUSIS

Enquiries:
cla_upd@cuhk.edu.hk / 3943-8224

CLCC2903
醫學粵語（二）
——
進階醫療溝通，用粵語更貼近病人！
你知道怎樣用粵語表達「病歷詢問」或「心理輔導」嗎？
想學習如何在醫院中以粵語處理緊急情況、手術安排，甚至是與病人家屬進行安寧照顧的溝通？
CLCC2903 是一門進階醫學粵語課程，專為希望提升醫療場景下粵語溝通能力的中大學生而設！

課程特色：
聚焦醫療場景下的粵語表達，包括病歷詢問、手術、急症、心理健康等
模擬真實臨床情境，進行角色扮演與語言任務
涵蓋敏感話題的溝通技巧，如壞消息傳達、安寧照顧、情緒支援等

學習成果：
能在預設醫療主題中進行簡單對話與討論
運用所學詞彙與句式進行成段溝通
在真實語境中流暢地與病人及醫護人員互動

授課模式與評核：
面授課堂（3小時）
簡報（30%）| 課堂參與（20%）| 測驗／小測（50%）

適合對象：
所有中大學生，尤其是已修讀 CLCC1903 或具備基本醫學粵語能力者，並希望進一步提升臨床溝通技巧者

註冊方式：
CUSIS

【中大研究招募】12週運動體適能及體溫調節能力研究
免費參與12週運動計劃，探索你的體能與體溫調節能力！

完成研究可獲
：
·
HK$200購物禮
券
·
運動手
錶
·
個人體適能及生理評估報
告
·
12週專業運動指導及跟進（運動組
）
香港中文大學體育運動科學系現正招募
18–40歲健康成年人
，參與一項為期12週的運動體適能改善研究！
研究目的
運動除了能改善心肺適能及整體健康，是否也能提升人體在溫熱環境下的體溫調節及
體溫調節
能力？
本研究旨在比較不同運動訓練方式對
體適能、運動能力及體溫調節能力
的影響。
參加資格

18–40歲
，男女均可
華人
BMI介乎
18.5–25.0 kg/m²
平時較少運動或沒有規律運動習慣
身體健康，適合進行運動訓練及相關測試
其他健康及安全條件將於正式參加前進一步篩查
。
研究內容
符合資格的參加者將被
隨機分配
至以下其中一組：
1.     高強度間歇運動組（HIIT）
2.     中等強度持續運動組（MICT）
3.     低強度步行組（WALK）
4.     對照組（Control）
運動組將接受為期
12週、每週3次
的運動訓練，由專業運動指導人員及研究團隊提供指導與跟進。
研究評估包括
：
·       身體成分（肌肉量、脂肪量等）
·       心肺適能及運動能力
·       肌肉力量
·       日常身體活動及飲食習慣
·       體溫調節及耐熱能力測試（受控溫熱環境下約30分鐘步行）
·       體溫調節測試前後採集血液樣本
測試時間：
干預前、第6週、第12週及約4個月後的跟進測試。
參與福利
HK$200購物禮券 + 運動手錶 + 個人研究評估報
告

香港中文大學體育運動科學系
香港沙田

生

。

！
CUHK Research Recruitment | 12-Week Exercise & Thermoregulation Study
Join Our 12-Week Exercise Programme and Discover Your Fitness & Thermoregulation!

Upon completion of the study, participants will receive:
·
HK$200 Shopping Voucher
·
Sports Watch
·
Personalised Fitness & Physiological Assessment Report
·
12 Weeks of Professional Exercise Guidance and Follow-up (Exercise Groups)
The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at
The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)
is recruiting
healthy adults aged 18–40
to participate in a 12-week exercise and heat tolerance research study!
Study Purpose
Can regular exercise improve not only physical fitness and overall health, but also the body's ability to regulate temperature and thermoregulation?
This study aims to investigate how different exercise training programmes affect
physical fitness, exercise capacity, and thermoregulatory responses
.
Who Can Participate?

18–40 years old
, males and females welcome
Ethnic Chinese
BMI between
18.5–25.0 kg/m²
Physically inactive or without a regular exercise routine
Generally healthy and suitable for exercise training and fitness testing
Additional health and safety eligibility criteria will be assessed before formal enrolment.
What Does the Study Involve?
Eligible participants will be
randomly assigned
to one of four groups:
1.     High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT)
2.     Moderate-Intensity Continuous Training (MICT)
3.     Low-Intensity Walking (WALK)
4.     Control Group
Participants assigned to the exercise groups will complete a
12-week training programme with 3 sessions per week
, supported by trained exercise professionals and research staff.
Study assessments include:
·       Body composition (muscle and fat mass)
·       Cardiorespiratory fitness and exercise capacity
·       Muscular strength
·       Physical activity and dietary habits
·       Thermoregulation  testing (approximately 30 minutes of walking in a controlled warm environment)
·       Blood sampling before and after the thermoregulatory assessment
Assessment Schedule:
Before the intervention, at Week 6, at Week 12, and at an additional follow-up approximately 4 months later.
Participant Benefits
HK$200 Shopping Voucher + Sports Watch + Personalised Assessment Report
Participants in the exercise groups will also receive 12 weeks of professional exercise guidance and follow-up support!
Study Location
Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Sha Tin, Hong Kong
Interested? Sign Up Now!
Scan the QR code on the poster to register!
Potentially eligible participants will be contacted by the research team for further screening and assessment arrangements.
Contact: Mr. Chen
WhatsApp:
5534 4775
Email:
chenyonghui0601@link.cuhk.edu.hk
Data Privacy: All information collected will be used for research purposes only, kept strictly confidential, and analysed using de-identified data.
Feel free to share this opportunity with friends who may be interested in supporting exercise science research!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

日期：2026年11月19日（星期四）
時間：下午3時至4時30分
地點：香港中文大學圖書館地下數碼學術研究室
主持：香港中文大學中國語言及文學系崔文東教授
語言：粵語
講題：【葉靈鳳寓港後所涉藝文人事】
講者據與葉靈鳳有關的書畫實物或文獻圖檔，漫談葉靈鳳與藝文界交遊的人和事，希望透過相關作品與史料，勾勒其寓港後的文化活動及人際網絡。
講者：許禮平先生，廣東揭陽人。50年代生於澳門，長居香港。70年代先後服務於中華書局海外辦事處、香港中文大學中國文化研究所中國語文硏究中心。80年代創辦問學社、翰墨軒，推動兩岸四地出版和書畫展覽等文化交流事宜。90年代主編《名家翰墨》月刊、叢刊。著有《舊日風雲》及《掌故家高貞白》等。
講座報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13744698

[Max. HKD$1200] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [最高可獲HKD$1200][長者認知及聽力測試報告+ 兒童IQ智商測試報告] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗 - Brain and Mind Institute
From: LEUNG Mei Yee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
我們是
香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（BMI）
的研究團隊。我們團隊誠摯邀請有聽力損失的長者及其孫子女來參與一項互動研究。
參與者需符合以下條件：
長者：
65歲或以上，存在聽力損失，
無其他已知認知障礙症狀， 且
有意願配戴助聽器
孩童：
6-9歲
，無其他已知發展問題，母語為廣東話
實驗內容：本實驗共分為兩節（每節約1.5至2小時）：
- 第一節：長者將獨自參與一項
認知及聽力檢測
（當日孫子女無需到場）
- 第二節：長者將與孫子女一同進行
簡單遊戲
，期間我們將使用安全且非侵入性的
「近紅外光譜儀」（fNIRS）
進行腦部掃描
- 請注意：參與者必須先完成第一節的實驗，且結果符合研究要求，方會獲邀參與第二節的實驗
完成整個實驗後，您可獲得：
- 長者：一份
認知能力測試報告
+ 一份
純音聽力測試報告
- 孩童：一份
非語言智商測試報告
+ 一份
價值HKD$80的禮物
報酬：
現金HKD$400-1200
，以及免費停車券（如適用）
實驗地點：香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（位於校園內）
如您對本研究感興趣，請點擊以下連結填寫報名表格：
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
如祖孫兩位初步符合條件，我們將會儘快與您聯絡！
如有疑問，請發送電郵至 meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk，
亦可致電或Whatsapp 95867123 查詢。
我們期待你的參與！
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We are researchers from the
Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong
. Our team sincerely invites grandparents with hearing loss and their grandchildren for a social interaction study.
Participants need to be:
- Grandparent:
65+ years old with hearing loss
, with no other diagnosed cognitive impairment, interested in fitting hearing aids
- Grandchild:
6-9 years old
with no other developmental problems; speaking Cantonese as the first language
What is involved? The experiment consists of two sessions (approx. 1.5-2 hours each):
- Session 1: The grandparent will participate alone in a
cognitive and hearing test
. (The grandchild does not need to attend)
- Session 2: The grandparent and grandchild will participate together in some
simple games
while using
fNIRS
(
functional near-infrared spectroscopy
, safe and non-invasive!!!) brain scanning device
- NOTE: Participants must first complete Session 1 and meet the study's requirements to be invited to Session 2
What you'll get (upon completion of the entire study):
- For the grandparent:
A cognitive test report
and
a pure-tone audiometry
(hearing test) report
- For the child:
An non-verbal IQ test report
and
a gift (~HKD$80)
Reward:
HKD$400-1200 allowance
and free parking ticket.
Location: Brain and Mind Institute, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (In campus).
If you are interested in our study, please fill in the form below via the following link:
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
We will contact you afterwards if the dyad are suitable.
For inquiries, please contact: meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk,
call or Whatsapp 95867123.
We look forward to your participation!

From: Rachel Chen

rachelchen@cuhk.edu.hk

CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project
Funded by The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust, CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project (“
the Project
”) brings together the strong expertise of CUHK Faculties of Engineering and Education. The Project’s objective is to create a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) curriculum, a sustainable AI education model, with relevant supporting infrastructure to establish a conducive ecosystem in AI education for Hong Kong’s secondary schools.
About Toolkit Team
To facilitate teachers’ teaching and students’ learning AI, the Toolkit Team is responsible for developing AI toolkits to support the Project’s AI Curriculum. The Toolkit team is also responsible for managing the Project’s AI Education and Exploration Lab (“the Lab”) at CUHK, as well as to develop AI-related demonstrations to be exhibited at the Lab and offer AI educational activities such as workshops and courses.
The Project team is looking for part-time students focusing on
AI event and materials development
. Job responsibilities and requirements are as follows:
No. of Vacancies:
5
Salary:
HKD 67 per hour
Working Hours:
A minimum of 4 hours/ week and maximum 17 hours/ week
Working Location:
Rm 902, 9/F, William M. W. Mong Engineering Building (ERB), CUHK
OR
HKSTP
Job Descriptions
To support the Project’s events, such as AI lab demo introduction, being tutor of AI workshops and lectures, etc.;
To support the teaching materials preparation work, such as AI camp and lab visits;
To support administration of Project’s workshops and courses, such as event planning, manpower and logistic arrangements;
To support the activity design of the Project’s AI toolkits to jointly create better AI educational technology products for secondary school students; and
To handle any ad hoc duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Study Year Requirements
Full-time undergraduate students
Full-time postgraduate students
Other Requirements
Good written and verbal skills in English;
Good written and verbal skills in Chinese/ Cantonese;
Willing to speak in front of 15-20 secondary school students;
Experience in STEM/AI-related teaching, education materials development or STEM/AI event planning would be a plus;
Enthusiasm in information technology education, enjoyment in meeting people at junior secondary level and sharing passion for AI topics and demonstrations; and
Possess good organizational skills, inter-personal skills, presentation skills, communications skills, logical thinking and able to work independently.
(Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview)
Please submit your CV and state the position(s) that you want to apply by email to Miss. Rachel CHEN (rachelchen@cuhk.edu.hk) by 23:59, 06 Nov 2026 (Fri).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project
Funded by The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust, CUHK Jockey Club AI for the Future Project (“
the Project
”) brings together the strong expertise of CUHK Faculties of Engineering and Education. The Project’s objective is to create a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) curriculum, a sustainable AI education model, with relevant supporting infrastructure to establish a conducive ecosystem in AI education for Hong Kong’s secondary schools.
About Toolkit Team
To facilitate teachers’ teaching and students’ learning AI, the Toolkit Team is responsible for developing AI toolkits to support the Project’s AI Curriculum. The Toolkit team is also responsible for managing the Project’s AI Education and Exploration Lab (“the Lab”) at CUHK, as well as to develop AI-related demonstrations to be exhibited at the Lab and offer AI educational activities such as workshops and courses.
The Project team is looking for part-time students focusing on
web application
. Job responsibilities and requirements are as follows:
No. of Vacancies:
5
Salary:
HKD 67 per hour
Working Hours:
A minimum of 4 hours/ week and maximum 17 hours/ week
Working Location:
Rm 902, 9/F, William M. W. Mong Engineering Building (ERB), CUHK
OR
HKSTP
Job Descriptions
To assist in developing web applications related to AI education and AI toolkits;
To work with designers to develop websites’ user interface;
To conduct research and experiments on web technologies and frameworks;
To document code and maintain code repositories; and
To handle any ad hoc duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Study Year Requirements
Full-time undergraduate students
Full-time postgraduate students
Other Requirements
Basic knowledge of JavaScript/ HTML/ CSS;
Basic knowledge of using Git for project version management;
Experience in front-end development, particularly responsive web design/UI/UX design would be a plus;
Possess a good track record in technical development; and
Responsible, willingness to learn and able to work independently.
(Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview)
Please submit your CV and state the position(s) that you want to apply by email to Miss. Rachel CHEN (rachelchen@cuhk.edu.hk) by 23:59, 06 Nov 2026 (Fri).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

From: 人間佛教研究中心 Centre for the Study of Humanistic Buddhism
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cshb@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【精彩上線｜紀念星雲大師百歲誕辰系列講座】
為紀念星雲大師百歲誕辰，香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心與佛學研究中心聯合舉辦 「人間佛教的文本、行跡與時代開展」 系列講座。我們特別邀請了宗教學、文學、哲學、出版、媒體與博物館學等領域的頂尖專家學者，帶來 9 場重磅專題演講！內容橫跨跨跨文化對話、文學考察、媒體實踐到新博物館學，從多元視角深化對星雲大師思想的理解。本次系列講座全面開放線上參與，歡迎大眾踴躍共霑法益。
題目：
星雲大師歌詞創作的「人間」應用特質
時間：11月19日 | 週四 14:30 - 16:30
講者：林仁昱教授 | 中興大學中文系特聘教授兼藝術中心主任
主持：陳劍鍠教授 | 香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心主任
形式：ZOOM網絡會議
ZOOM ID: 964 5779 7423，密碼: 999999
報名：https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741303
演講簡介：
星雲大師在倡議與實踐「人間佛教」的道路上，不僅以歌曲來推廣理念，許多歌曲也成為導引新時代儀節與活動的重要部分。從1950年代作〈西方〉以取代念佛共修的傳統迴向四句偈，作〈佛化婚禮祝歌〉來適應建立「佛化家庭」的重要典儀；1970年代作〈三寶頌〉濃縮歷代各種〈三皈依〉偈讚歌詞要義，更方便傳唱應用；到2000年以後，創作眾多「人間音緣」歌詞，廣徵作曲，使相同歌詞可有不同風格的譜曲，靈活運用於各種弘法與社會活動，充分表現「人間」應用的特質。本次講座將順著時代脈絡，剖析歌詞內涵與實際應用情形，論述其具體意義及影響力。
On his path of advocating and practicing "Humanistic Buddhism," Venerable Master Hsing Yun not only promoted Buddhist concepts through songs, but many of his musical works also became essential components guiding rituals and activities in the modern era.
Historically, this practical approach unfolded across several key stages: In the 1950s, he composed Western Land (〈西方〉) to replace the traditional four-line verse for the dedication of merit during collective chanting cultivation, and penned the Blessing Song for Buddhist Weddings (〈佛化婚禮祝歌〉) to accommodate the pivotal rituals of establishing "Buddhist Families." In the 1970s, he authored the Ode to the Triple Gem (〈三寶頌〉), which condensed the essential meanings of various historical verses praising the Three Refuges into a format more accessible for singing and collective use. From 2000 onward, he created numerous lyrics for Sounds of the Human World (「人間音緣」) and openly solicited musical compositions, allowing the same lyrics to be adapted into diverse musical styles and flexibly utilized in various Dharma propagation and social events. This approach fully exemplifies the characteristics of "humanistic" and practical application.
Following a chronological framework, this lecture will analyze the inner connotations and practical applications of these lyrics, discussing their concrete significance and far-reaching influence.
嘉賓簡介：
林仁昱，中興大學中文系特聘教授兼藝術中心主任，以佛教文學與文化、敦煌文獻與文學、歌謠俗曲與風俗為研究領域，重要著作有：《敦煌佛教歌曲之研究》、《廿世紀初中國俗曲唱述人物》、《敦煌佛教讚歌寫本「原生態」與應用研究》，近期刊登於期刊的單篇著作有：〈星雲大師1950－70年代佛教歌詞創作探究〉、〈星雲大師「人間音緣」歌詞的文學表現及其效應〉、〈《觀音十二圓覺》的菩薩化身與度化對象探究〉、〈觀音與地藏組合供奉的信仰意義與衍發現象〉、〈現代東亞佛誕節文藝與文化考察—以臺灣、日本、馬來西亞為探究核心〉等。

Assess the safety, efficacy and tolerability of a CUHK proprietary Chinese medicine formula – A 9-month trial targeting patients with diabetes <6-year disease duration and on two or less oral drugs 津貼高達一千港元!以確認香港中文大學研發的專利中藥配方的安全性、療效及耐受性。招募糖尿病人(六年內確診，飲食控制或服用2種或以下口服糖尿藥)參與為期九個月的研究 - Department of Medicine and Therapeutics
From: Maggie Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
maggielee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期九個月，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病 (例如:心臟病或中風等重大併發症)
沒有服用中藥
身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
患糖尿病6 年或以下
目前飲食控制或用2種或以下口服糖尿藥 [例如metformin（品牌藥名：Glucophage）或/及 gliclazide（品牌藥名：Diamicron）]
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，但具備以下其中一項風險因素，我們會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）作篩查
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 9-month clinical study on the use of oral Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses (e.g., heart disease or stroke)
Not taking Chinese medicine
Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes within the past 6 years
Diet control alone or taking no more than 2 oral diabetes medications [e.g., metformin (Glucophage®) and/or gliclazide (Diamicron®)]
Not sure if you have diabetes? If you have any of the following risk factors, we can arrange a 75 g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) for diabetes screening
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes

Study Procedures: Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365

Announcements
[Free of charge] UP TO HKD$1000 ALLOWANCE! Assess the safety, efficacy and tolerability of a CUHK proprietary Chinese medicine formula – A 9-month trial targeting patients with diabetes <6-year disease duration and on two or less oral drugs 津貼高達一千港元!以確認香港中文大學研發的專利中藥配方的安全性、療效及耐受性。招募糖尿病人(六年內確診，飲食控制或服用2種或以下口服糖尿藥)參與為期九個月的研究 - Department of Medicine and Therapeutics
From: Maggie Lee
maggielee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期九個月，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病 (例如:心臟病或中風等重大併發症)
沒有服用中藥
身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
患糖尿病6 年或以下
目前飲食控制或用2種或以下口服糖尿藥 [例如metformin（品牌藥名：Glucophage）或/及 gliclazide（品牌藥名：Diamicron）]
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，但具備以下其中一項風險因素，我們會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）作篩查
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 9-month clinical study on the use of oral Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses (e.g., heart disease or stroke)
Not taking Chinese medicine
Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes within the past 6 years
Diet control alone or taking no more than 2 oral diabetes medications [e.g., metformin (Glucophage®) and/or gliclazide (Diamicron®)]
Not sure if you have diabetes? If you have any of the following risk factors, we can arrange a 75 g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) for diabetes screening
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes

Study Procedures: Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365

國際中醫藥循證醫學研討會—構建高質量臨床證據
【邀請函及海報徵稿】
尊敬的中醫藥業界同仁、學者及專業人士：
香港中文大學中醫學院謹定於 2026年12月5日（星期六） 舉辦「國際中醫藥循證醫學研討會—構建高質量臨床證據」。本次研討會匯聚多位國際及本地頂尖中醫藥與循證醫學專家，共同探討中醫藥臨床研究的最新進展與高質量證據的構建策略。我們誠邀廣大中醫藥從業員、研究人員及相關領域專業人士踴躍報名參加。
研討會詳情
● 日期：2026年12月5日（星期六）
● 時間：下午1時30分至6時10分
● 地點：香港中文大學康本國際學術園3號演講廳 (LT3)
● 語言：英語及中文
● 費用：免費
● 註冊中醫進修學分：CME-PP0018-SCM0537（4.5 分）
● 報名截止日期：2026年12月1日 ● 報名連結：https://clinic.scm.cuhk.edu.hk/ISECM/registration.aspx
主講嘉賓（排名不分先後）
● 卞兆祥教授（香港中醫醫院醫院行政總監）
● 周怡君教授（香港中文大學醫學院助理院長、內科及藥物治療學系副教授（臨床）、一期臨床研究中心外部事務策略總監）
● 李相勳教授（慶熙大學韓醫學院副院長兼教授）
● 林志秀教授（香港中文大學中醫學院院長、香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究
所所長）
● 溫澤淮教授（廣東省中醫院藥物臨床試驗機構副主任兼教授）
循證醫學研究海報展示—徵稿邀請
本次研討會特別設有循證醫學研究海報展示，旨在提供交流與展示最新科研成果的平台。歡迎各位研究人員及業界同仁踴躍投稿！
● 截稿日期：2026年11月13日
● 投稿詳情及指引：請參閱會議網站（https://clinic.scm.cuhk.edu.hk/ISECM/registration.aspx）
主辦及支持單位
● 主辦單位：香港中文大學醫學院中醫學院
● 合辦單位：中國中醫藥循證醫學中心協作網絡建設單位、香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所、香港中文大學中醫專科診所暨臨床教研中心
● 支持單位：香港中文大學粵港澳大灣區發展辦公室
查詢及聯絡
● 電郵：isebcm.scm@cuhk.edu.hk
● 電話：(852) 3943 3440 / (852) 3943 1551
期待您的參與，共同推動中醫藥循證醫學的發展！
香港中文大學中醫學院 敬啟
International Symposium on Evidence-Based Chinese Medicine: Constructing High-Quality Clinical Evidence
[Invitation & Call for Posters]
Dear Colleagues and Professionals in Chinese Medicine,
The School of Chinese Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), cordially invites you to attend the "International Symposium on Evidence-Based Chinese Medicine: Constructing High-Quality Clinical Evidence" to be held on Saturday, 5 December 2026. Bringing together leading international and local experts, this symposium will focus on the latest developments in clinical research and strategies for constructing high-quality evidence in Chinese Medicine. We welcome all Chinese medicine practitioners, researchers, and healthcare professionals to join us.
Symposium Information
● Date: Saturday, 5 December 2026
● Time: 1:30 p.m. – 6:10 p.m.
● Venue: LT3, Yasumoto International Academic Park, CUHK
● Language: English & Chinese
● Fee: Free
● CME Accreditation: CME-PP0018-SCM0537 (4.5 Points)
● Registration Deadline: 1 December 2026 ● Online Registration: https://clinic.scm.cuhk.edu.hk/ISECM/registration.aspx
Featured Speakers
● Prof. BIAN Zhaoxiang — Hospital Chief Executive, The Chinese Medicine Hospital of Hong Kong
● Prof. CHOW Yee Kwan Elaine — Assistant Dean (Health Systems), Faculty of Medicine, CUHK; Associate Professor (Clinical), Department of Medicine and Therapeutics, CUHK; Director of External Affairs Strategy, Phase I Clinical Trial Centre, CUHK
● Prof. LEE Sanghoon — Deputy Director, International Education Institute of Korean Medicine; Professor, College of Korean Medicine, Kyung Hee University
● Prof. LIN Zhi-Xiu — Director and Professor, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK; Director, The Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK
● Prof. WEN Zehuai — Director and Professor, Center for Clinical Research, Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine
Call for Poster Submissions
We are pleased to announce that a Poster Exhibition on Evidence-Based Medicine Research will be featured at the symposium. We invite interested researchers and practitioners to submit their work to showcase their latest scientific achievements.
● Submission Deadline: 13 November 2026
● Submission Guidelines: Please refer to the official conference website (https://clinic.scm.cuhk.edu.hk/ISECM/registration.aspx).
Organizers & Supporters
● Organizer: School of Chinese Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
● Co-Organizers: Shenzhen Research Institute, CUHK; Sub-Center of the China Center for Evidence-Based Traditional Chinese Medicine; Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK; The Chinese University of Hong Kong Chinese Medicine Specialty Clinic cum Clinical Teaching and Research Centre
● Supporting Unit: Office for Greater Bay Area Developments, CUHK
Enquiries & Contact
● Email: isebcm.scm@cuhk.edu.hk
● Tel: (852) 3943 3440 / (852) 3943 1551
We look forward to your active participation!
Sincerely,
School of Chinese Medicine
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

The School of Chinese Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), cordially invites you to attend the "International Symposium on Evidence-Based Chinese Medicine: Constructing High-Quality Clinical Evidence" to be held on Saturday, 5 December 2026. Bringing together leading international and local experts, this symposium will focus on the latest developments in clinical research and strategies for constructing high-quality evidence in Chinese Medicine. We welcome all Chinese medicine practitioners, researchers, and healthcare professionals to join us.
Symposium Information
● Date: Saturday, 5 December 2026
● Time: 1:30 p.m. – 6:10 p.m.
● Venue: LT3, Yasumoto International Academic Park, CUHK
● Language: English & Chinese
● Fee: Free
● CME Accreditation: CME-PP0018-SCM0537 (4.5 Points)
● Registration Deadline: 1 December 2026 ● Online Registration: https://clinic.scm.cuhk.edu.hk/ISECM/registration.aspx

● Prof. CHOW Yee Kwan Elaine — Assistant Dean (Health Systems), Faculty of Medicine, CUHK; Associate Professor (Clinical), Department of Medicine and Therapeutics, CUHK; Director of External Affairs Strategy, Phase I Clinical Trial Centre, CUHK
● Prof. LEE Sanghoon — Deputy Director, International Education Institute of Korean Medicine; Professor, College of Korean Medicine, Kyung Hee University
● Prof. LIN Zhi-Xiu — Director and Professor, School of Chinese Medicine, CUHK; Director, The Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK
● Prof. WEN Zehuai — Director and Professor, Center for Clinical Research, Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine

「嶺南文化與世界」公開講座系列2026──藝文嶺南：工藝、詩畫與人文景觀，由香港中文大學中國文化研究所嶺南文化研究計劃與香港公共圖書館聯合主辦，首場講座在 10 月 25 日圓滿結束，第二場講座將於 11 月 28 日繼續在香港中央圖書館演講廳舉行，誠邀大家參加！
兩場專題講座聚焦嶺南在跨域交流中的文化生產與藝術創造，從清代廣州工藝實踐與嶺南羅浮人文地景兩個主題切入。一方面，探討廣東銅胎琺瑯器如何在中外貿易背景下融合西洋裝飾元素，體現廣州工匠對外來技術與審美的創新轉化；另一方面，考察蘇軾嶺南詩文對地方知識、人文景觀與文化記憶的建構作用，以及清代與之相關的《羅浮香影圖》。透過工藝、詩畫與人文景觀的視角進行觀察，本系列將展現嶺南文化在跨域和歷史互動中的創新活力。
本講座系列為香港研究資助局協作研究計劃「嶺南文化與世界」項目（2023–2026）活動，亦是弘揚中華文化系列的活動之一。

Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape, Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026
The Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026, themed “Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape” and jointly organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Public Libraries. The first lecture was successfully held on 25 October. The second lecture will take place at the Lecture Theatre of the Hong Kong Central Library on 28 November.
The two lectures, one focused on the craftsmanship of the region during the Qing
era, and the other on the humanistic landscape of Luofu, reveal how cross-regional interactions drove cultural and artistic production in Lingnan. The first lecture looks at how China’s trade with the West introduced Western decorative elements into Canton enamelled copperware, showcasing Guangzhou craftsmen’s innovative reinterpretation of Western techniques and aesthetics. The second lecture shifts focus to Su Shi’s Lingnan-themed verses, examining the construction of Lingnan’s humanistic landscape and cultural memory, as well as the creation of the
Paintings of Fragrant Dream of Luofu
during the Qing
dynasty. Approaching the core theme through the lens of craftsmanship, poetic painting, and humanistic landscape, this series reflects the innovative dynamics of Lingnan culture in cross-regional and historical interactions.
This public lecture series is part of RGC Collaborative Research Project “Lingnan Culture and the World” (2023–2026) and is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series.

2023
–2026）
Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape, Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026
The Public Lecture Series on “Lingnan Culture and the World” 2026, themed “Art and Literature of Lingnan: Craftsmanship, Poetic Painting, and Humanistic Landscape” and jointly organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Public Libraries. The first lecture was successfully held on 25 October. The second lecture will take place at the Lecture Theatre of the Hong Kong Central Library on 28 November.
The two lectures, one focused on the craftsmanship of the region during the Qing
era, and the other on the humanistic landscape of Luofu, reveal how cross-regional interactions drove cultural and artistic production in Lingnan. The first lecture looks at how China’s trade with the West introduced Western decorative elements into Canton enamelled copperware, showcasing Guangzhou craftsmen’s innovative reinterpretation of Western techniques and aesthetics. The second lecture shifts focus to Su Shi’s Lingnan-themed verses, examining the construction of Lingnan’s humanistic landscape and cultural memory, as well as the creation of the
Paintings of Fragrant Dream of Luofu
during the Qing
dynasty. Approaching the core theme through the lens of craftsmanship, poetic painting, and humanistic landscape, this series reflects the innovative dynamics of Lingnan culture in cross-regional and historical interactions.
This public lecture series is part of RGC Collaborative Research Project “Lingnan Culture and the World” (2023–2026) and is also one of the activities in the Chinese Culture Promotion Series.

Dear first-year students,
Ready to transform your university experience and stand out in today’s competitive business landscape?
The
International Business and Chinese Enterprise (IBCE)
and
Asian Business Studies (ABS)
transfer-in programmes are designed to cultivate regional expertise across diverse business contexts, while developing career readiness, professional networks, and focused skill sets.
To enhance your understanding of the programme features, application procedures, and selection process, an information and networking session will be held on
Nov 16
. You will also have the opportunity to meet IBCE and ABS students to hear about their firsthand experiences.
Please find the details below:
IBCE and ABS Information and Networking Session
Date: Nov 16, 2026 (Mon)
Time: 6:30 – 8:30pm
(light refreshments will be provided)
Venue: CYT203
Registration:
Click Here
(Deadline: by Nov 12, 2026)
Remarks: Registration is required to attend the session. Successful registrants will receive a confirmation e-mail closer to the event date.
About IBCE and ABS
IBCE – A Complete US-China Experience
In partnership with the University of South Carolina's Darla Moore School of Business, IBCE offers an unparalleled bi-continental education that develops your understanding of the US and Chinese markets.
Exclusive Bi-continental Cohort Exchange
: Gain international perspective and cultural fluency through a full year exchange in the US, building lifelong global connections.
Cutting-edge Business Training with Strong China Focus
: Develop your business acumen and regional expertise through specialized courses, China study trips, and direct connections with leading enterprises for long-term career success.
High-achieving Programme Network:
Learn alongside driven peers and connect with a powerful alumni network to accelerate your career development.
ABS – Your Personalised Gateway to Asia
ABS provides numerous avenues for exploring the world’s most vibrant economic region, allowing you to tailor your experience to your academic and career goals.
Flexible Exchange Opportunities in Asia:
Choose up to two exchanges across six Asian hubs on your own schedule for a unique regional exposure and cultural experience.
Practical Business Training with Asian Focus:
Gain tailored professional training, tackle real-world Asian business challenges through a corporate project, and explore diverse markets via study trips across Asia.
Vibrant Asian Community:
Connect with a multicultural programme community spanning Asia, gaining a distinct advantage in navigating diverse business environments.
To learn more about our programme, you may also refer to the
IBCE
and
ABS
Programme Brochures.
Should you have any questions, please feel free to contact Mr. Dennis Wong, Programme Manager at
denniswong@cuhk.edu.hk
.
We look forward to seeing you at the event.
Best regards,

4/F, Cheng Yu Tung Building, 12 Chak Cheung Street, Shatin, Hong Kong

From: Martina NGAI

Dear students,
Semester at Sea (SaS) is a multi-country study abroad programme that brings together students from around the world to live, learn, and travel aboard a floating campus. Students earn academic credit through courses taught by distinguished faculty while visiting multiple countries across several continents, combining rigorous academics with experiential and intercultural learning. The SaS hosts CUHK students each year. The programme typically has eight stops around the world, including Hong Kong.
SaS is inviting the CUHK community aboard during its docking in Hong Kong on 10 December 2026 (Thurs).
It is a valuable opportunity to learn more about university life on board and to foster cultural and academic exchange among students and scholars. Studying aboard a floating campus is a distinctive and enriching experience, and it offers a useful preview for students who may be considering future exchange opportunities. The Shipboard Welcome Event includes a ship tour, an academic exchange, and lunch with SaS students on board. Please see the table below for details of the event:
Theme
SaS Shipboard Welcome Event
Venue
MV World Odyssey, Tsim Sha Tsui Ocean Terminal
Program Date
10 December 2026 (Thursday) 1000-1300
Objectives
To gain first-hand insight into life and study aboard a floating campus
To engage in intercultural and academic dialogue with international students and faculty
Connect their classroom learning with a broader global perspective
Activities
Ship tour
Academic exchange with students and faculty on board
Lunch with SaS students in the dining hall on board
Eligibility
CUHK full-time undergraduate students from all disciplines are welcome to apply
Have a good command in English
Have a good academic performance
Outreach/ exchange experiences will be an advantage
Application
Interested students should complete the
online application form
by 12:00 noon on Wednesday, 4 November
,
and submit their supporting documents, including an unofficial transcript, a CV, an English language qualification (if any).

Please refer to the
SaS program website
for more details.

submit the application form before 12nn on November 4, 2026 (Wed).

Participant call for an fMRI experiment  - Prof. LIU Xiaonan, Department of Psychology
From: SHI Aike
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
Ak-Shi@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Hi all,
We are recruiting participants for an fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) experiment on learning and memory. The formal experiment will be an one-shot MRI scanning session taking place at the
Prince of Wales Hospital
. The estimated duration of the experiment is about
90 minutes
and you will receive
HK$200
immediately after finishing it as remuneration. The MRI scanning itself is harmless to you but potential injuries can occur (e.g., when metals are implanted in your body), so a safety screening will be performed before the experiment.
Interested students can email the experimenter (Ak-Shi@link.cuhk.edu.hk) for registration, and we will reply with available timeslots for both saftety check and formal experiment.
Please kindly note that students who have participated in our behavioral study (which were carried out by the same experimenter
Aike Shi
)
in the past three months
cannot attend the current experiment. Thanks for your understanding.
Best,
Aike Shi
Memory Lab

From: Amber Lam

Experiencing Chinese Culture Series 2026-27 – Chinese Calligraphy Workshop (Advanced)
Date: 25 November; 2, 9, 16, 23 & 30 December 2026 and 6, 13, 20 & 28 January 2027 (Wednesdays; except for 28 January; total 10 lessons)
Time: 6:00 p.m. - 7:30 p.m.
Venue: Experiential Learning Space, 1/F, West Wing, Art Museum, CUHK
Target Audience: CUHK Students, Staff and Alumni
Language: Cantonese
Registration:
Click here
Enquiries: 3943 5976 /
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
For details, please refer to the poster (Chinese version only).
活動簡介
：
本課程為中國書法進階班，主要教授行書和草書，旨在透過介紹和臨習二王體系帖學經典，讓學員漸進掌握行、草書的書寫技巧和賞鑒，加深對書法的認識，增進對中國文化藝術的熱愛。
導師簡介：
陳冠男博士，畢業於香港中文大學藝術系，現職中大文物館中國書畫主任（研究員），研究興趣為明清至近現代書畫。曾策劃多個展覽並編撰圖錄，最新近者是「香江藏珍——香港三大古書畫收藏」 （2025，與劉湘瀅合作）。其他曾參與撰寫之圖錄包括：《蓋蒂基金會贊助中國書畫在線圖錄》、「北山汲古系列：中國書法、中國繪畫、碑帖銘刻拓本」、《明畫全集．董其昌卷》等；另合編撰寫《丁衍庸書法》等專書。2018-19年度獲選為「利榮森紀念訪問學人」，任美國普林斯頓大學藝術與考古系唐氏東亞藝術中心及藝術博物館訪問學人。研究之餘也積極參與各種書畫展覽和比賽，並獲殊榮，作品為香港及海內外公私收藏。

title: 【Earn HK$500 coupon】 Recruiting adults (aged 18-65) to participate in research on online therapy for insomnia 【可獲得 500元現金券】招募成年人 (18-65歲)參與失眠的數碼化治療研究
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/30
»
Announcements
【Earn HK$500 coupon】 Recruiting adults (aged 18-65) to participate in research on online therapy for insomnia 【可獲得 500元現金券】招募成年人 (18-65歲)參與失眠的數碼化治療研究 - Psychiatry
From: Charis
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你是否經常在床上輾轉難眠，夜醒或早醒？你並不孤單——許多人都面臨著同樣的問題。我們誠邀您參與研究，讓專業數碼化治療助你改善睡眠！
研究目的
本研究旨在評估市民對數碼化失眠認知行為治療聊天機器人的遵從性，以及其對改善睡眠問題的效果。
治療方式
· 由專業臨床心理學家及精神科醫生設計的電子化治療
· 完全免費
參與資格
· 18至65歲能說廣東話流利溝通（能流利閱讀並理解廣東話）的香港居民
· 在過去一個月內，每週至少三晚出現睡眠困擾
· 最近四周或以上無需長期服藥
參與研究，獲得獎勵！
完成所有治療及後續測試後，您可獲得高達500港幣。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理聯絡。
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do you often toss and turn in bed, wake up frequently at night, or wake up too early? You are not alone—many people experience the same challenges. We invite you to participate in our study and explore professional digital treatment to improve your sleep!
Purpose of the Study
This research aims to evaluate the public’s adherence to a digital insomnia cognitive behavioural therapy chatbot and assess its effectiveness in improving sleep problems.
Treatment Method
· A professionally designed digital therapy created by clinical psychologists and psychiatrists
· Completely free of charge
Eligibility Criteria
· Hong Kong residents aged 18 to 65 who can speak in Cantonese fluently, read and understand Cantonese
· Experienced sleep disturbances at least 3 nights per week in the past month
· No need for long-term medication for the past four weeks or more.
Receive Rewards for Participating!
Upon completion of all treatment sessions and follow-up assessments, participants will receive up to HKD 500.
How to Join?
Click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact suitable participants to provide further details:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
