From: HE Chuting
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你想了解孩子對於學校或日常生活裡的“領導”的看法嗎？想知道孩子對於“當領導”的意願嗎？不要錯過這次有趣又有意義的研究機會。簡單進行線上研究，還有報酬可領喔~~
招募對象
：
在香港男女共校的小學就讀小1到小6的小學生以及其父親或母親
目前各個組別依舊在積極招募，各個組別依舊席位多多！誠摯邀請合乎要求的小朋友同家長參與~~如果你們身邊有合乎要求的小朋友和家長，也懇請幫我們多多宣傳~~
研究項目：
小學生、家長及老師的領導認知與刻板印象
研究內容（全程以中文進行）：
1.孩子：1對1線上訪談（需錄音），約需1小時。
2.家長：填寫1份網上問卷，約需1小時。
報酬：
家長和孩子完成各自的研究項目後，可獲得共100港幣報酬。
參與條件：
1.兒童參加者為在香港就讀男女共校的小學的小1到小6的小學生，家長參加者為該兒童的父親或母親。
2.兒童能講流利廣東話或普通話，家長能閱讀和書寫中文。
3.兒童可使用有互聯網、視頻和音頻功能的電腦或平板參與研究。
4.兒童沒有主要的身體障礙（如：視障、四肢不健全）和未被診斷有任何有關精神健康或主要的發展障礙的狀況（如：自閉症、過度活躍、讀寫障礙）。
5.請留意參加者需在此前沒有參與過本研究的“預實驗”或“教師部分”（如不清楚是否參與過也可先留下聯繫方式，稍後我們的研究人員將與您聯繫進行確認）。
如對本實驗感興趣，請通過以下鏈接報名
，我們的研究人員將盡快聯繫您：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KzWB6HhTtOhwou
參與純屬自願性質，所收集的資料只作研究用途及保密處理。如有任何疑問，請聯繫何小姐（conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk)。

From: Melinda Chuchu Liu
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155201160@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
生活充實定係空虛？課程有趣但一諗到未來職涯頭都大埋？
親愛的同學們，中大公共衞生及基層醫療學院研究團隊誠邀你參與一項本地大專學生幸福感和心理健康調查。花 15-20 分鐘分享你的幸福感同壓力，完成問卷並通過有效性檢核的受訪者可得 HK$100 惠康 / 屈臣氏 / Marks & Spencer / Sephora禮券或電子禮品卡！不需要高談闊論，只需要你真實的感受。
符合以下
4
個條件即可參與：
18-24 歲的香港永久性居民
本地全日制學士（Degree）或副學位（Asso/HD）課程學生（請在問卷中填寫學生電郵，僅用於資格檢核和發放禮券）
能閱讀和理解繁體中文或英文
能夠使用手機/平板/電腦填寫線上問卷
數據嚴格保密，参与完全自願，可以隨時停止。每位受訪者只能參與和領取酬謝一次。

APPLY NOW!!! MSc in Real Estate Programme (2027 intake)  房地產理學碩士課程（2027 年度入學）現正接受申請！ - MSc in Real Estate Programme Office
From: MSc in Real Estate Programme Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mscre@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

APPLY NOW!!! MSc in Real Estate Programme (2027 intake)

MSc in Real Estate (MRE) is the only master’s degree in Asia that draws on multi-disciplinal research and teaching resources ranging from real estate, business to hospitality.
The programme offers an experiential learning curriculum that integrates theory and real-world practice to ensure that students understand multiple phases of the real estate development from business, investment and community perspectives.
Graduates of our programme will find career opportunities in areas such as development planning, research and consultancy, valuation, real estate finance, investment and management.
The programme is professionally accredited by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS). Graduates are eligible to become chartered surveyors with only 2 years of relevant professional experience, compared with 5 or more years for non-accredited degree holders.
Eligible applicants are automatically considered for Admission Scholarship.
Apply NOW
to secure your place for the 2027 intake!

房地產理學碩士課程（2027 年度入學）現正接受申請！

香港中文大學商學院房地産理學碩士課程是亞洲唯一融合房地産、商業和旅遊資産學科研究和教學資源的碩士課程。
課程結合理論與行業實踐，透過體驗式學習，從商業投資和社區角度教授學生房地産不同發展階段的知識與技能。
課程畢業生職業前景廣闊，包括房地産規劃、開發、融資、投資、估價、資産管理、設施管理、租賃、營銷和諮詢領域等。
課程獲皇家特許測量師學會認証，畢業生於相關領域工作2年後可申請成爲全球認可的注冊測量師（非認証課程畢業生需要最少5年）。
符合條件的申請人將自動獲得入學獎學金資格。
把握2027入學機會，立即申請！

Announcements
Investor and Financial Education for All: Don’t Freestyle Your Investments!  - Department of Finance
From: Quantitative Finance Programme
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
qfin@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The IFEC is pleased to share with you the launch of our new education campaign “Investor and Financial Education for All: Don’t Freestyle Your Investments!” / 「投資理財  人人都要識︰投資切忌 Freestyle!」.
According to the IFEC’s “
Retail Investor Study 2025
”, close to 60% of young investors aged 18-29 reported making quick profits through short-term trading was their most important reason for investing. In response, this campaign aims to encourage young people to approach investing with the right mindset and do their research before investing, rather than blindly following the hype.
An energetic animated video has been launched, featuring IFEC Chin Junior and Mr. Chin sharing key investment Dos and Don’ts through an upbeat rap. Audiences are also encouraged to follow IFEC’s
Instagram
and use our comprehensive education resources to make informed investment decisions.

陳果導演作品放映及映後座談｜重溫後九七香港的美麗與哀愁
陳果導演作品放映及映後座談
香港有個荷里活
(2002)
｜
導演：陳果
金像獎導演陳果以超現實色彩交織出一則關於階級、慾望與都市變遷的寓言。導演藉由木屋區與摩天大樓的並置，以黑色幽默與荒誕現實主義的筆觸，書寫後九七時期香港的集體焦慮。
是次活動將先放映全片，映後特別邀請導演陳果親臨現場，圍繞獨立電影精神、社會地景與角色塑造等展開深度對談，並設現場 Q&A 環節。
二十餘載閃逝，大磡村早已消失。重溫這部作品，讓我們可以探討城市重組、邊緣命運與身份認同的演變。誠邀各位一同蒞臨，重新審視香港。
電影榮獲第39屆金馬獎最佳導演、最佳造型設計及最佳音效；以及第9屆香港電影評論學會大獎最佳編劇與推薦電影。
日期：2026年11月17日（星期二）
時間：7:00 - 9:00 pm（放映）｜晚上 9:00 - 9:30 pm（映後座談及問答環節）
地點：康本國際學術園一號演講廳（YIA LT-1）
放映作品：香港有個荷里活（2002年，108分鐘，中文字幕）
座談嘉賓：陳果導演
對象：中大學生及教職員、校友及公眾人士
費用：免費參加，先到先得
即時報名：
報名《香港有個荷里活》電影放映及座談
合辦單位：
山城影院 (OSA)
自學中心 (ILC)
書寫力量
中大電影學會

Film Screening & Q&A with Director Fruit Chan｜Revisiting the Melancholy and Beauty of Post-97 Hong Kong

Director Fruit Chan Film Screening & Post-Screening Q&A
Hollywood Hong Kong (2002) | Directed by Fruit Chan
Award-winning director Fruit Chan uses surrealist elements to craft a dark fable about class, desire, and urban transformation. By contrasting a squatter village with neighboring luxury skyscrapers, the film employs dark humor and absurd realism to capture the collective anxiety of post-1997 Hong Kong.
The event will begin with a full screening of the film, followed by an in-depth conversation with Director Fruit Chan himself. He will share his insights on the spirit of independent filmmaking, social landscapes, and character development, followed by a Q&A session.
More than two decades have flown by, and Dai Hom Village has long since vanished. Revisiting this masterpiece allows us to explore urban redevelopment, marginalization, and the evolution of cultural identity. We invite you to join us and rediscover Hong Kong through his lens.
Hollywood Hong Kong
won Best Director, Best Makeup & Costume Design, and Best Sound Effects at the 39th Golden Horse Awards. It was also awarded Best Screenplay and named a Recommended Film at the 9th Hong Kong Film Critics Society Awards.
Event Details
Date: November 17, 2026, Tue
Time: 7:00 PM - 9:00 PM (Screening), 9:00 PM - 9:30 PM (Post-screening Talk & Q&A)
Venue: Yasumoto International Academic Park, Lecture Theatre 1 (YIA LT-1)
Screening Title: Hollywood Hong Kong (2002, 108 mins, with Chinese subtitles)
Guest Speaker: Film Director Fruit Chan
Target Audience: CUHK students, staff, alumni, and the public
Admission: Free (First-come, first-served)

From: Ling Haofeng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀18至29歲香港年輕成人參加問卷研究— 「關於年輕成人經歷親友/重要的人離世的哀傷」 (完成研究最多可獲價值港幣$300元正超市禮券)
參加者納入標準：
18
至
29
歲
在香港居住的本地年輕成人
在過去
18
個月內經歷過親友
/
重要的人離世
能閱懂中文和以廣東話溝通
研究程序：
1
）基線問卷
填妥同意書後，參加者將完成一份20分鐘基線問卷
問卷問題將與面對及經歷親友/重要的人離世時的哀傷過程及對死亡的觀念有關
完成基線問卷將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
2
）第一輪跟進問卷
六個月後，我們會邀請參加者完成一份跟進問卷
完成第一輪跟進問卷的參加者將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
3
）第二輪跟進問卷
在完成第一輪跟進問卷的六個月後，我們會邀請參加者再次完成一份跟進問卷
完成第二輪跟進問卷的參加者將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
本研究均屬自願參與。研究資料會被保密，除研究人員外，任何人均不能獲取參與者所填寫的問卷資訊或錄音內容。本研究已通過香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會(CREC-2025.748)及香港中文大學調查和行為研究倫理(SBRE‐24‐0378)審查。
參加方法:
請用以下連結填寫同意書及問卷，完成後可獲送贈港幣
一百元
正超市禮券
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊合資格的香港年輕成人。
如有查詢，請與博士後研究員凌皓峰博士聯絡。
電郵: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp：44643831 (凌皓峰博士)
We are now inviting Hong Kong young adults to participate in a bereavement survey, titled “Trajectories of grief outcomes and the associated psychosocial predictors among recently bereaved young adults in Hong Kong: A retrospective longitudinal mixed-methods approach”. Participants will receive up to HK$300 coupons upon completion.
Participant Inclusion Criteria:
Local young adults aged 18 to 29 residing in Hong Kong.
Have experienced the death of a close friend/relative or an important person within the past 18 months.
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese.
1) Baseline Questionnaire
- After signing the consent form, participants will complete a 20-minute baseline questionnaire.
- The questionnaire will include questions about grieving process in response to the death of a loved one or significant person, and attitudes toward death
- Participants will receive HK$100 coupons for completing the baseline questionnaire.
2) First Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months later, participants who have completed the baseline questionnaire will be invited to complete a follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the first follow-up questionnaire will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
3) Second Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months after the first follow-up questionnaire, participants who have completed the first follow-up questionnaire will be invited to complete a second follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the second follow-up questionnaire after will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
Participation in this study is voluntary. The study data will be kept confidential and no one other than the researchers will have access to the questionnaire information or audio recordings completed by the participants. This study has been approved by The Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC (CREC-2025.748) and the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (SBRE‐24‐0378).
Please use the following link to fill out the consent form and questionnaire. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
You are welcome to recommend this recruitment information to qualified young adults in Hong Kong.

Announcements
“In Dialogue with China” Study Trip to Ganzhou (Deadline Extension) 「訪談中國」贛州研學團（延長報名截止日期） - Office of University General Education
From: General Education China Programme, Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear students,
The application deadline for the “In Dialogue with China” Study Trip to Ganzhou, Jiangxi, has been extended to
1 November 2026
.
The Long March of the Chinese Red Army from the Central Soviet Area in Jiangxi to northern Shaanxi between 1934 and 1936, a journey of 12,500 km, was a great human epic that changed the course of Chinese history. The renowned American journalist Harrison Salisbury, who retraced the route of the Long March in 1983 and wrote The Long March: The Untold Story, called it “the crucible of the Chinese revolution.” The Long March has no parallel in human history, and “its heroism has fired the dreams of a nation of 1.1 billion people.”
This study trip will explore the history of the Red Army’s Jiangxi Soviet Area and visit the departure point of the Red Army’s Long March. It will also visit Gannan Normal University for exchanges with its faculty and students and examine how the Ganzhou region fosters community governance and rural revitalization in the new Long March of Chinese modernization.
The details of the study trip are as follows:
Theme
Ganzhou: Long March and Chinese Modernization
Period
26-29 December 2026 (4 days)
Tentative Itinerary
Jiangxi Soviet Area in Ruijin (瑞金中央蘇區); Site of the First National Congress of the Chinese Soviet Republic (中華蘇維埃共和國第一次全國代表大會舊址); Shazhouba Revolutionary Sites (沙洲壩革命舊址); Memorial Hall of the Departure Point of the Central Red Army’s Long March (中央紅軍長征出發地紀念館); Red Army Long March Trail (紅軍長征小道); Gannan Normal University (贛南師範大學); Fushougou Museum (福壽溝博物館); and Former Residence of Chiang Ching-kuo (蔣經國舊居), etc.
Quota
20 CUHK undergraduate students
Language Requirements
Cantonese and Putonghua
Programme Fee
HK$500
Application Deadline
1 November 2026
Online Registration
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13744977
Remarks:
A deposit of HK$4,000 is required, which will be refunded to students who have completed the whole trip and all other related activities and requirements after deducting the programme fee.
Participants are required to read relevant articles, attend a briefing session before departure, present individual reflections in a post-trip sharing session, and submit a written report of at least 1000 words in English or 1000 characters in Chinese after the trip.
Participants should possess valid travel documents to China.
Should you have any queries, please feel free to contact the General Education China Programme of the Office of University General Education at 3943 0595 or write to
ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk
.

「訪談中國」贛州研學之旅的報名截止日期已延長至
2026
年
11
月
1
日
。
中國紅軍1934-1936從江西中央蘇區轉移到陝北的二萬五千里長征，是人類歷史上的一篇史詩，改變了中國的歷史。美國著名記者索爾茲伯1983年重游長征路而寫成《長征：前所未聞的故事》，說長征是舉世無雙的，它是「中國革命的熔爐」，「所表現的英雄主義激勵著一個有十一億人口的民族」。
這次研學團，將學習紅軍中央蘇區歷史，參觀紅軍長征出發地，與贛南師範大學師生交流，並考察贛州地區在中國式現代化的新長征過程中如何進行社區治理與鄉村振興。
研學團的詳情如下：
主題
贛州：長征與中國式現代化
日期
2026年12月26至29日
目的地
贛州
行程
瑞金中央蘇區；中華蘇維埃共和國第一次全國代表大會舊址；沙洲壩革命舊址；中央紅軍長征出發地紀念館；紅軍長征小道；贛南師範大學；福壽溝博物館；蔣經國舊居
名額
20名中大本科生
語言要求
粵語和普通話
費用
$500
報名截止日期
2026年11月1日
網上報名連結
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13744977
備註：
(i)        參加者須繳付按金$4,000，完成所有行程和項目相關活動及要求後，將獲退還扣除活動費用的餘額。
(ii)       參加者須閱讀相關文章，出發前參加說明會，並在完成研學行程後參加分享會，作個人報告及提交一份以英文或中文書寫不少於1000字的報告。
(iii)       參加者須持有前往中國內地的有效旅遊證件。
如有查詢，請電郵至ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk，或致電3943 0595 聯絡大學通識教育部通識中國課程。
View Count

To investigate whether aspirin increases the risk of bleeding after polyp removal.
To evaluate the cardiovascular impact of temporarily stopping aspirin.
Eligibility
Aged 45 or above.
Currently taking aspirin for heart, cerebrovascular, or vascular disease.

Have not undergone a colonoscopy within the past 2 years.

You will be randomly assigned to one of the following groups.

Announcements
Let's listen to some music!! Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion 一齊聽歌! 招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Xiuyang Meng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?
Please click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact eligible participants to explain the study details in full:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants Ms. Chan or Mr. Meng.

Recruitment of student interns for a community health research project 招募社區健康研究項目實習生 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Edwin Chung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
shunkitchung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院研究團隊現正進行一項
社區研究。本計劃透過免費提供空氣清新機，幫助居住在空氣質素欠佳環境
的 6 至 17 歲哮喘兒童及青少年改善居住環境。
我們誠邀中大本科生加入參與實習，
一同走進社區，透過科學方法協助家庭。
工作範疇
- 研究期間：即日起至 2027 年 10 月 31 日（按團隊編排彈性參與）
- 協助研究團隊在指定的日期和地點進行研究對象招募。
- 按日子到研究對象的住所設置空氣監測儀器、放置空氣清新機，並為研究對象進行呼吸測試。
- 執行研究團隊指派的其他工作。
招募條件
- 現正就讀大學學士學位課程的學生（醫學、護理、公共衛生或相關課
程更佳）。

年齡18歲以上；

100 HKD 作為酬謝

To develop a reading ability assessment scale tailored for native Chinese speakers.
Recruitment Criteria:
Aged 18 or above;
Native Cantonese speakers;
Individuals with a background in psychology or linguistics are also welcome to participate.
Compensation & Benefits:
HK$100 honorarium;
Experiment Information:
Venue: In-person session at Room 323, Sino Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Duration: Approximately 60-90 minutes.
Procedure: Paper-and-pencil language tests and questionnaire completion.
Interested participants may scan the QR code on the poster or click the link below to register:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScAJRZ13jq65jueJYiRoWbWsQebmL_uk1yeQjTqgsyqopUU-w/viewform?usp=header

Announcements
HKPFS & Ph.D. in Public Health, CUHK 2027-28 - deadline on 1 Dec 2026  歡迎報名2027-28 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: MPhil and PhD Programmes in Public Health Enquiry
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
phtraining@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
CUHK PhD in Public Health
香港中文大學
公共衛生哲學博士課程
The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) is a government initiative to support outstanding students from around the world (including local HK) to study in Hong Kong. For Intake 2027-28, the academic year starts on 1 August 2027.
We invite excellent students to apply for CUHK PhD programme in Public Health and welcome students to apply for HKPFS. These provide opportunities to study full-time with financial support in Hong Kong.
Please note that both application deadlines are on December 1, 2026.
Our research themes include:
•          Non-communicable disease and aging, and Family Medicine & Primary Healthcare
•          Environmental health and infectious diseases
•          Global health policy, health system & healthcare delivery
•          Mental well-being, social & health behaviours
•          Bioinformatics, machine learning and big data
CUHK HKPFS offers:
- HKPFS stipend at HK$344,400 (approx. US$44,200) per year; Up to HK$1.38 Million (approx. US$176,620)
- Conference and Research-related Travel Allowance is HK$14,400 (approx. US$1,850) per year; Up to HK$87,600 (approx. US$11,230)
- And CUHK Vice-Chancellor HKPFS Scholarship - an award of total HK$80,000 (approx. US$10,260)
- Tuition Fee Waiver - Up to HK$198,0000 (approx. US$25,390)
- Lodging Award - Up to HK$100,000 (approx. US$12,820)
- 1st Year Accommodation Fee Waiver and Guaranteed On-campus Accommodation
Step 1: To submit an initial application to RGC. Application deadline: 1 Dec 2026 at 12:00 noon (GMT+8, Hong Kong Time); and
Step 2: To submit full application to CUHK. Application deadline: 1 Dec 2026 at 11:59pm (GMT+8, Hong Kong Time).
Details of MPhil-PhD programme in Public Health can be found on webpage
https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/programme/medicine#mphil-phd-in-public-health
or
https://sphpc.cuhk.edu.hk/rpg-programme/
For more info about our School’s Research Themes and list of on-going grants, please refer to webpage
https://sphpc.cuhk.edu.hk/research-themes/
You can find the scholarship information at
https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/scholarships-fees/scholarships
You may also refer to the "FAQs" Section at
https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/faqs
for more information.

[Student Helper Recruitment] Chinese Language and Culture Experience Activities | Cross-cultural Exchange  - Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
From: Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
CLA_UPD@CUHK.EDU.HK
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【學生助理招募】中國語言文化體驗活動｜跨文化交流
雅禮中國語文研習所將於本學期舉辦一系列面向國際學生的中國語言文化體驗活動，主題涵蓋漢字與書法、傳統節慶、手工文化體驗、中文詩歌與文化分享。現誠邀中大學生擔任學生助理，協助活動籌備與現場支援。
活動時間：逢星期五下午，每次兩小時，預計本學期共舉辦5至6次
活動地點：方潤華堂（東鐵線大學站D出口對面）
申請條件：
對跨文化交流充滿熱情，性格開朗，有親和力，具備良好英語溝通能力，並能說標準普通話或粵語；
具備與中華文化相關的才藝，如中國結、詩歌賞析，並樂意與國際學生交流分享；
會編製不同類型的中國結，了解中國結的歷史和種類；
對古詩詞有較為深入的認識，能簡單講解詩詞背景與含義；
懂得古詩詞的押韻、平仄，能簡單從音樂角度賞析詩詞；
會做手工，如拓印、剪紙等的學生獲優先考慮。
待遇：時薪 HKD$67 + 5% MPF
總工作時數：約15小時
有意者請於11月13日前填妥以下表格，合則約見：

報名表格
如有疑問，請聯絡陳小姐：
liyuanchen@cuhk.edu.hk
[Student Helper Recruitment] Chinese Language and Culture Experience Activities | Cross-cultural Exchange]
The Yale-China Chinese Language Academy will host a series of cultural workshops this semester for international students, focusing on themes in Chinese language and culture, including Chinese characters, calligraphy, traditional festivals, handicrafts, poetry, songs, and cultural sharing. We are now recruiting CUHK students to assist with planning and running these events.
Schedule: Friday afternoons, 2 hours per session, approximately 5–6 sessions throughout the semester
Venue: Fong Yun Wah Hall (opposite University Station Exit D)
Requirements:
Passionate about cross-cultural communication, outgoing, friendly, fluent in English, and able to speak Putonghua or Cantonese;
Possess talents or skills related to Chinese culture and be willing to share and interact with international students;
Capable of making Chinese knots and familiar with the history and different types of Chinese knots;
Familiar with classical Chinese poetry and songs and be able to explain the background and meaning;
Understand the rhyme and tone patterns of classical poetry, and be able to offer simple appreciation of poems from a musical perspective;
Priority will be given to students with skills in handicraft such as Chinese rubbing and paper cutting.
Compensation: HKD$67/hr + 5% MPF
Total working hours: Around 15 hours
Interested applicants should complete the form below by November 13. Interviews will be arranged for shortlisted candidates:

liyuanchen@cuhk.edu.hk

UGED1146/CLCE1103
Chinese Language, Culture and Language Learning
中國語言及文化與語言學習
UGED1146 is double-coded with CLCE1103. The course is designed for all CUHK students who want to explore the relationship between language and culture. Prior knowledge of the Chinese language is not required. Course details are as follows:
Course outline:
Introduce the relationship between language and culture
Examine theories and practices in teaching and learning Chinese as a second language
Outline the language policies in China
Discuss Cantonese and its relationship with other major dialects in China
Medium of instruction:
English
Registration:
CUSIS
(Please register for UGED1146* if the study credits are for fulfilling your university’s general education requirement)
For more details:
Please visit the CLA website
Enquiry:

/ 3943-8224
*Not suitable for students who have taken CLCE1103, CCSS1010
,
or UGED2760.
University Programme Section
Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
UGED1146與CLCE1103列為雙重編號科目，為對中國語言及文化有興趣的中大學生而設，不受中文背景多寡限制。科目資料如下：
科目大綱：
介紹語言及文化的關係
探討對外漢語的教與學的現狀
概述香港與中國內地的語言政策
討論粵語及其與中國和香港其他主要方言的關係

Announcements
Recruitment of participants aged 6-80 years old with LONG COVID 誠邀 6-80 歲有長新冠症狀的患者參加「中醫/西醫治療長新冠症狀」的研究  - Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine
From: Wendy LI
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hkiimresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正進行一項為期8周，以內服中藥(沖劑)或西藥改善長新冠患者症狀的臨床研究，以下是研究安排：
研究對象：
年齡介乎6至80歲；
願意接受中醫或西醫治療4星期；
每星期一次覆診跟進病程；
目的         : 比較中藥與西藥對治療長新冠患者在改善生活質量、臨床症狀和生活社等治療效果和安全性。
研究內容：中/西醫評估*、問卷評估、抽血檢查、服用中藥或西藥等。
*注意: 本研究會隨機分「中藥組」或「西藥組」
研究地點： (a)中藥組: 沙田威爾斯親王醫院; (b)西藥組: 指定西醫診所 (中環)。
參與方式： 若有興趣，歡迎
1.透過以下方式報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13670048
2.亦歡迎您致電或WhatsApp我們6082-2583/ 2873-3245了解詳情。
Research Introduction:
The novel coronavirus has caused a global pandemic since the end of 2019. People are increasingly paying attention to the long-term effects of COVID-19 infection.People whose symptoms last for more than four weeks after COVID-19 infection are called [Long COVID]. The main symptoms include severe fatigue, shortness of breath, heart damage (such as myocarditis), cognitive impairment, sleep disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder syndrome, Muscle pain, decreased concentration, headache, impaired taste and smell, etc. affect the respiratory system, cardiovascular system, digestive system, urinary system, immune system, etc.
The Hong Kong Institute of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine at the Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting an 8-week clinical study on the improvement of symptoms of patients with COVID-19 by taking Chinese medicine (infusion) or Western medicine.
Target
: Age 6-80 who have recovered from COVID-19 infection.
Purpose
: To compare the therapeutic effects and safety of traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine on improving the quality of life, clinical symptoms and social functions of long-term COVID-19 patients.
Research Content
: Visits, questionnaire assessment, blood draw before and after taking medicine,taking research Chinese medicine or Western medicine, etc.
Study Location
:(a) Chinese medicine group: Prince of Wales Hospital, Shatin;
(b) Western medicine group: designated western medicine clinic.
Participation
： Free of charge. If interested, please
1. sign up through the following ：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13670048
2. You are also welcome to call or WhatsApp us at 6082-2583/ 2873-3245 for details.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

[Recruitment]
HCC: Historical and Cultural Innovation Experience Tour in Shekou
Have you ever wondered how Shekou evolved from a fishing village into a major trading port, and how its cultural heritage is being transformed into products and commercial ventures?
Join us on the Historical and Cultural Innovation Experience Tour in Shekou, organised by the Heritage and Cultural Conservation Ambassador Programme (HCC)! bodyText:

Invitation to the HKEAA Research Forum on Assessment and STEM Education 誠邀參加香港考試及評核局研究論壇 - EdDataX Research Centre
From: Angus NG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
angusmingho@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Colleagues and Students,
Greetings from the EdDataX Research Centre, CUHK
As part of our ongoing collaboration with the Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority (HKEAA) on international large-scale assessment projects, we are pleased to invite you to attend the upcoming HKEAA Research Forum.
Date:
5 November 2026 (Thursday)
Time:
9:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.
Venue:
HKEAA Hung Hom Office and Examination Centre
The forum will feature distinguished scholars and practitioners sharing insights on educational assessment, STEM education, and emerging developments in the age of artificial intelligence.
This forum offers an excellent opportunity for academics, researchers, teachers, and students to learn more about international large-scale assessments, current educational research, and the future of learning and assessment.
You and your colleagues are cordially invited to attend.
Registration:
https://www.hkeaa.edu.hk/en/events/registration.html
We look forward to your participation.
Kind regards,
EdDataX Research Centre
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
各位同事及同學：
您好！
教育數據研究中心一直與香港考試及評核局（HKEAA）合作推展多項國際大型教育評估研究項目。現誠邀各位參加由考評局舉辦的研究論壇，了解教育評估、STEM 教育及人工智能時代下的最新發展。
日期：
2026年11月5日（星期四）
時間：
上午9時30分至下午4時30分
地點：
考評局紅磡辦事處及考試中心
論壇將邀請多位學者及專家分享教育評估及 STEM 教育的最新研究與實踐經驗。
是次論壇為對教育研究、教育評估、人工智能、學習科學及 STEM 教育有興趣的教職員及同學提供寶貴的學習和交流機會，同時亦有助加深了解 TIMSS 等國際大型教育評估研究的最新發展。
誠邀各位老師、研究人員及同學踴躍參加。
報名連結：
https://www.hkeaa.edu.hk/en/events/registration.html
期待與大家在論壇見面！

From: ILC

【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 2 November to 6 November: (1) Ace Your Oral Presentations, (2) Job Preparation Series: Writing Impressive Application Letters, (3) Hong Kong Civil Service Interview Preparation, and (4) Global Citizenship Series: Sustainable Consumption. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
2 November (Mon): 10:30 – 12:30
3 November (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
4 November (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
5 November (Thu): 14:30 – 16:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================
【Weekly Highlights - Chinese Section 】中文部本週活動
A. Chinese Workshops 中文工作坊
The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 2 November to 6 November: (1) JRE Argumentative Writing I, (2) CV & Cover Letter Writing (Cantonese), and (3) Happy Hour. These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
自學中心十一月二日至十一月六日舉辦 (1) JRE 議論文寫作 (一), (2) 「天下之能事畢矣」—— 《易經》占筮入門 (粵), (3) 中文求職信及履歷寫作(粵), 及 (4) Happy Hour @ 逐粒字，執字粒：淺談活字印刷等工作坊，歡迎報名。
登記連結： https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in Chinese 自學中心中文輔導服務
Consultation service is available during the following time:
自學中心於十一月二日至十一月六日提供以下中文輔導時段。
2 November (Mon): 10:30 – 12:30
3 November (Tue): 14:30 – 16:30
4 November (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
5 November (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.

Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.

Cantonese and Putonghua Online Taster Courses

廣東話及普通話網上體驗科目
CLA is offering a series of 1-credit asynchronous Online Taster Courses for students who are interested in learning Cantonese and Putonghua (Mandarin) at their own pace. Students will learn in a low-pressure environment by watching prerecorded videos and completing online exercises. They will acquire a basic understanding of Cantonese/Putonghua upon completion of the course(s). These courses are ideal for students who would like to have a taste of language learning before taking a full 3-credit language course.
Please find the links below to register for the taster courses on KEEP:
1)
CLCC1001 Cantonese Taster Course for CUHK International Students
2)
CLCC1101 Cantonese Taster Course for CUHK Mandarin-speaking Students
3)
CLCP1001 Putonghua as a Second Language Taster Course for International Students
4)
CLCP1101 Putonghua Taster Course for Local Students

Minor Programmes in Chinese Language (Cantonese/Putonghua) as a Second Language
Jointly with the Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages (LING), CLA is pleased to announce that two minor programmes are offered to CUHK students whose native language is not Putonghua or Cantonese admitted in 2022-23 and thereafter:
Minor Programme in Chinese Language (Cantonese) as a Second Language
Minor Programme in Chinese Language (Putonghua) as a Second Language
In each programme, students are required to complete a minimum of 21 units of courses, including 2 courses offered by LING and 5 Cantonese/Putonghua courses offered by CLA.
The minor programmes aim to provide systematic Cantonese/Putonghua language training to students from the perspective of contemporary theories of language study. In addition to nurturing students’ language proficiency with substantive knowledge regarding the lexicon and grammar of Cantonese/Putonghua, the curriculum design of the programmes also features applications of current theories of linguistics in language acquisition, cognitive science, as well as culture and society.
For more details on the programmes’ study schemes, course lists and course descriptions, please visit the website (
https://www.yccla.cuhk.edu.hk/minor-prog
). We look forward to seeing you in class!

[UGEB2991] Re-running the Four Areas University GE Course: Viewing Communication from Speech Therapy [UGEB2991] 再次開辦課程通識四範圍科目 — 「從言語治療看溝通」 - Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: CHEUK KIT CHING
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cynthiacheuk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你有否試過失聲、聲音沙啞、口齒不清或者口吃？你身邊有沒有人說話不清、患有認知障礙、自閉症、聽力障礙或者中風？你知道如何幫助他們嗎？
每 10 個人中就有一個人患有至少一種溝通障礙。人們在一生中幾乎不可避免地會遇到言語不清、聲音嘶啞、口吃、自閉症譜系障礙、聽力障礙和認知障礙（癡呆）等症狀的人。沒有言語和聽力科學背景的同學，現在你們有機會學習從語言病理學的角度，瞭解人類交流的基本原理及其障礙！由醫學院言語治療科再次開辦的通識四範圍科目 – 「從言語治療看溝通」，將會用13個星期，帶你認識人類交流基本要素、各種溝通障礙的成因和特徵，以及一些跟患者溝通的實用技巧。想透過通識科目擴闊眼界的你，絕對不能錯過：
科目：UGEB2991 從言語治療看溝通
上課時間：逢星期一09:30 – 12:15（2026-27學年下學期）
地點：信和樓UG層2號演講廳
期待你的參與！
如有任何查詢，歡迎電郵至cynthiacheuk@cuhk.edu.hk。
Have you ever experienced loss of voice, hoarseness, unclear speech, or stuttering? Do you know someone around you who has unclear speech, cognitive impairments, autism spectrum disorder, hearing impairment, or has had a stroke? Do you know how to help them?
One in every 10 people suffers from at least one kind of communication disorder. It is almost inevitable for people to have encountered individuals with unclear speech, hoarse voice, stuttering, autism spectrum disorder, hearing impairment and dementia etc. in their lifetime. For those without a background in speech and hearing sciences, now you can learn more about the fundamentals of communication science from the perspective of speech-language-pathology! The general education course offered by the Division of Speech Therapy, "Viewing Communication from Speech Therapy" is being re-run and will take you through a 13-week journey to explore the essential elements of normal communication, the causes and characteristics of various communication disorders, and practical tips for communicating with patients. If you are eager to broaden your horizons, this is an opportunity you cannot miss:
Course: UGEB2991 Viewing Communications from Speech Therapy
Class Schedule: 09:30 – 12:15, weekly on Monday (Term 2, AY26-27)
Venue: Lecture Theatre 2, UG/F, Sino Building
Looking forward to your participation!
Should you have any queries, please contact us on cynthiacheuk@cuhk.edu.hk.

title: Recruitment of Student Helpers for the Academic Year 2026–2027 2026–2027 年度學生助理招聘
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/10/30
»
Announcements
Recruitment of Student Helpers for the Academic Year 2026–2027  2026–2027 年度學生助理招聘 - Brain and Mind Institute
From: Eva Lai
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
evalai@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Brain and Mind Institute
is currently seeking highly motivated undergraduate and graduate students to join our research team as
student helpers
in our laboratory. As a member of our team, you will work on research projects focused on the neural basis of language and cognitive development in infants across their lifespan. For more information regarding our research projects, please visit our website:
http://bmi.cuhk.edu.hk.
Responsibilities of this position include collecting EEG and behavioral data; assisting with the preparation of research materials; data entry, management, and analysis; preparing research reports; coding socio-communicative behaviors; transcribing and editing transcripts; providing daily office housekeeping and administrative support; and completing other duties as assigned by supervisors.
Students with the following skills and attributes are encouraged to apply:
A good command of Chinese and English (fluency in Cantonese is advantageous);
Research experience in EEG/fNIRS, big data, and experimental psychology is an advantage;
Proficiency in MS Office or G-Suite and Chinese typing;
Meticulous and detail-oriented;
Punctual, reliable, and trustworthy; and
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
The appointee may work at the University campus, at other locations as required by research needs, or remotely from home.
Availability to work on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays
is highly preferred. Students from the disciplines of Linguistics, Psychology, Education, and Nursing are preferred, but students of other majors are welcome to apply. Previous experience working with infants or young children is a definite plus.
How to Apply:
Interested parties please complete the online application form:
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/iRJSf5nH52
Review of applications will start as soon as possible and continue until
30 November 2026
, or until the post is filled. Questions or enquiries can be sent to hkbrain@cuhk.edu.hk. Please note that all personal data collected will be used solely for recruitment purposes.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Recruit Student Helpers for Clinical Research Project  - Department of Medicine & Therapeutics
From: Catherine Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
catherinecheung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Recruitment: Student Helper
Position Description:
The Infectious Disease Research Team at the Department of Medicine & Therapeutics, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, cordially invites CUHK students to join our clinical vaccine trial support work! Our team is led by experienced medical professionals dedicated to clinical research. We are recruiting student helpers to participate in important clinical preparation work before and after vaccination. Under our guidance, you will gain valuable hands-on experience in clinical research, learning while working and experiencing the real value and significance of scientific research first hand. Work is based at Prince of Wales Hospital in a comfortable, relaxed environment with no fieldwork required—an ideal internship platform.
Responsibilities:
Pre-trial preparations (e.g., sample container labelling, document organization, material setup)
Assist with biological sample and data collection before/after vaccination when needed
Perform clinical research tasks assigned by research supervisor
Requirements:
CUHK undergraduate or postgraduate student
Available for at least one session per week, minimum 3-4 hours per session (flexible scheduling, to be arranged with supervisor, working hours to be adjusted based on subsequent research workload and needs)
Responsible, detail-oriented, and reliable
Proficient in English and Chinese.
Preferred Qualifications:
Science, medicine, nursing, pharmacy or related fields preferred; other disciplines also welcome
Interest in clinical research or vaccine trials
Salary: HKD$80 / hour
Application:
Please email your CV to
catherinecheung@cuhk.edu.hk
Applications welcome immediately!
招聘：學生研究助理
職位簡介：
香港中文大學內科及治療學系傳染病學研究團隊誠邀中大同學加入我們的臨床疫苗試驗支援工作！本團隊由經驗豐富的醫護人員領頭，專業致力於臨床研究。我們正在招募學生助理參與疫苗注射前後的重要臨床準備工作。在我們的指導下，您將獲得寶貴的臨床研究實務經驗，邊學習邊工作，親身體驗科研的價值與意義。工作地點固定於威爾斯親王醫院，環境輕鬆舒適，無需外出，是理想的實習平台。
職責：
負責臨床試驗前期準備工作（如生物樣本容器標籤、文件整理、材料配置）
必要時協助疫苗注射前後的生物樣本及數據收集
執行研究主管安排的相關臨床研究任務
要求：
中大本科生或研究生
每週至少能參與一次，每次至少3至 4小時（具體時間彈性，可與研究主管協商，並根據後續工作内容及需求調整）
責任心強，細心可靠
需具備良好的中英文溝通能力
優先條件：
科學、醫學、護理學、藥學等相關專業優先，其他專業亦歡迎
對臨床研究或疫苗試驗有興趣
酬金：每小時$80
申請方式：
請將CV電郵至
catherinecheung@cuhk.edu.hk
歡迎即時申請！

Beyond Preservation: AI, Memory, and the Future of Testimony  - Centre for Cultural Studies
From: Miss Manuela Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
manuelawong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Beyond Preservation: AI, Memory, and the Future of Testimony
How can emerging technologies help us preserve and encounter memories that might otherwise fade from collective consciousness?
Eternal Testimony
is an ongoing project initiated in 2018 to explore new ways of preserving and experiencing the testimonies of survivors of Japanese military sexual slavery. The project creates a virtual experience in which visitors can meet and interact with survivors. In this talk, Prof. Jusub Kim introduces the vision, technological development, and exhibition experiences behind
Eternal Testimony
. He discusses how computational media can transform historical testimony from a static archival record into an interactive and emotionally engaging encounter. Through the project’s development and exhibitions, the talk reflects on the possibilities and challenges of using AI to mediate memory, presence, and human connection. Ultimately,
Eternal Testimony
asks how technologies can contribute to the ongoing transmission of history and the preservation of voices across generations.
Date: 13 Nov 2026, Fri
Time: 4:00 PM – Lecture Begins
Venue: CKB LT3, UG/F, Chen Kou Bun Building, CUHK
Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13742513
Speaker: Prof. Jusub Kim, Sogang University
Moderator: Prof. PARK SaeHim, CUHK
About the speaker:
Jusub Kim is a creative technologist, researcher, and educator exploring the intersection of art and technology. He previously worked at Rhythm & Hues Studios in Los Angeles, contributing to major Hollywood films including the Oscar-winning Life of Pi. He holds a Ph.D. from the University of Maryland, College Park, and is currently a professor in the Department of Art and Technology at Sogang University, Seoul.

Announcements
^[Research Invitation] Speech Intervention Study for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate 【研究邀請】招募參與「唇顎裂兒童及青少年語音介入」之學術研究 - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
各位香港中文大學成員：
我們誠邀閣下及其子女參與由香港中文大學耳鼻喉科、頭頸外科進行的學術研究 。
研究題目： 「探索針對唇顎裂兒童及青少年的語音介入框架：隨機對照試驗」
研究目的：患有唇顎裂的兒童有較高風險出現語音/發音困難，這可能嚴重影響其說話清晰度。本研究旨在比較兩種不同的實證語音介入框架（線性與非線性語音介入）在改善這些語音錯誤方面的成效。
招募對象：
說廣東話的兒童及青少年 (4歲 – 17歲)；
4 至 17 歲，母語為廣東話嘅兒童及青少年。
患有唇顎裂，並有發音/語音問題。
於 24 個月大前已完成唇顎裂之修復手術；
無已知認知障礙，或任何會影響其獨立參與語音任務能力的醫療狀況。
研究程序：
全面評估：參與者將經歷全面的語音評估程序，包括多項標準化語音測試及填寫問卷。
個別治療：參與者將接受由專業言語治療師設計的語音治療方案。請注意，候補名單對照組的參與者將在主要研究觀察階段結束後接受治療。
錄影記錄：參與者的語音將被錄影，以作進一步記錄和分析。所有語音數據及錄音將受密碼保護並嚴格保密 。
費用與報酬：
潛在益處：參與者能透過治療方案提升整體說話清晰度，並為唇顎裂語音的臨床護理程序及機制提供貢獻。
參與費用：參與本研究無需支付任何額外費用。
聯絡方式： 如有興趣參與或有任何疑問，請致電 3943 9609 聯絡首席研究員 何皓賢先生。
感謝閣下對本研究計劃的興趣與支持。亦可以使用以下連結報名:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
此研究項目已獲香港中文大學 – 新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會（Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC）批准。
Dear Members of the CUHK Community,
We are cordially inviting children and adolescents with Cleft Palate ± Lip to participate in a research study conducted by the Division of Speech Therapy (Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Study Title: Exploring Speech Intervention Frameworks for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate +/- Lip: A Randomized-Controlled Trial.
Children born with Cleft Palate ±Lip (CP±L) are at high risk for speech difficulties, such as glottal stops or backing errors, which can significantly impact how well they produce speech sounds and are understood. This study investigates the effectiveness of two different evidence-based speech intervention frameworks (Linear vs. Non-linear phonological intervention) in improving these speech outcomes.
Who Can Participate?
Cantonese-speaking children and adolescents (aged 4 to 17) with CP±L
Individuals exhibiting cleft speech errors that require intervention;
Primary repair of the palate done prior to 24 months old;
No known cognitive or hearing impairment, or other medical conditions that prevent independent participation in speech tasks.
What is Involved?
Comprehensive Assessment: Participants will undergo standardized speech assessments and questionnaires.
Treatment: Participants will receive speech therapy protocols designed by professional speech therapists. Please note that participants in the waitlist group will receive treatment after the primary study observation phase.
Recording: Speech sessions will be video-recorded for data analysis and will remain strictly confidential.
Benefits and Costs:
Potential Benefits: Improvement in overall speech clarity and contribution to the clinical management of cleft palate speech.
Costs: There is no additional cost to participate.
Contact Information: If you are interested or have questions, please contact Mr. Choco Ho (何皓賢), Speech Therapist and Principal Investigator, at 3943 9609 or click the link below:

Announcements
^[Research Invitation] Speech Intervention Study for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate 【研究邀請】招募參與「唇顎裂兒童及青少年語音介入」之學術研究 - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
各位香港中文大學成員：
我們誠邀閣下及其子女參與由香港中文大學耳鼻喉科、頭頸外科進行的學術研究 。
研究題目： 「探索針對唇顎裂兒童及青少年的語音介入框架：隨機對照試驗」
研究目的：患有唇顎裂的兒童有較高風險出現語音/發音困難，這可能嚴重影響其說話清晰度。本研究旨在比較兩種不同的實證語音介入框架（線性與非線性語音介入）在改善這些語音錯誤方面的成效。
招募對象：
說廣東話的兒童及青少年 (4歲 – 17歲)；
4 至 17 歲，母語為廣東話嘅兒童及青少年。
患有唇顎裂，並有發音/語音問題。
於 24 個月大前已完成唇顎裂之修復手術；
無已知認知障礙，或任何會影響其獨立參與語音任務能力的醫療狀況。
研究程序：
全面評估：參與者將經歷全面的語音評估程序，包括多項標準化語音測試及填寫問卷。
個別治療：參與者將接受由專業言語治療師設計的語音治療方案。請注意，候補名單對照組的參與者將在主要研究觀察階段結束後接受治療。
錄影記錄：參與者的語音將被錄影，以作進一步記錄和分析。所有語音數據及錄音將受密碼保護並嚴格保密 。
費用與報酬：
潛在益處：參與者能透過治療方案提升整體說話清晰度，並為唇顎裂語音的臨床護理程序及機制提供貢獻。
參與費用：參與本研究無需支付任何額外費用。
聯絡方式： 如有興趣參與或有任何疑問，請致電 3943 9609 聯絡首席研究員 何皓賢先生。
感謝閣下對本研究計劃的興趣與支持。亦可以使用以下連結報名:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
此研究項目已獲香港中文大學 – 新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會（Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC）批准。
Dear Members of the CUHK Community,
We are cordially inviting children and adolescents with Cleft Palate ± Lip to participate in a research study conducted by the Division of Speech Therapy (Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Study Title: Exploring Speech Intervention Frameworks for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate +/- Lip: A Randomized-Controlled Trial.
Children born with Cleft Palate ±Lip (CP±L) are at high risk for speech difficulties, such as glottal stops or backing errors, which can significantly impact how well they produce speech sounds and are understood. This study investigates the effectiveness of two different evidence-based speech intervention frameworks (Linear vs. Non-linear phonological intervention) in improving these speech outcomes.
Who Can Participate?
Cantonese-speaking children and adolescents (aged 4 to 17) with CP±L
Individuals exhibiting cleft speech errors that require intervention;
Primary repair of the palate done prior to 24 months old;
No known cognitive or hearing impairment, or other medical conditions that prevent independent participation in speech tasks.
What is Involved?
Comprehensive Assessment: Participants will undergo standardized speech assessments and questionnaires.
Treatment: Participants will receive speech therapy protocols designed by professional speech therapists. Please note that participants in the waitlist group will receive treatment after the primary study observation phase.
Recording: Speech sessions will be video-recorded for data analysis and will remain strictly confidential.
Benefits and Costs:
Potential Benefits: Improvement in overall speech clarity and contribution to the clinical management of cleft palate speech.
Costs: There is no additional cost to participate.
Contact Information: If you are interested or have questions, please contact Mr. Choco Ho (何皓賢), Speech Therapist and Principal Investigator, at 3943 9609 or click the link below:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC.

Recruiting CUHK Students as Climate Mentors — Join Project CLIMATE  - Department of Curriculum and Instruction
From: Eric Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cuhksdg@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear CUHK Students, Are you interested in climate action, sustainability, global learning, community engagement, education, communication, or working with young people?
Project CLIMATE: Community-engaged Learning, Inclusive Mentoring and AI-supported Transformative Education is recruiting CUHK students from all disciplines to become Climate Mentors. You will work alongside secondary-school students, teachers, community partners, and international youth peers in a local–global–local climate-learning journey.
As a Climate Mentor, you will have opportunities to:
Join mentor preparation and language-support workshops.
Facilitate small-group dialogue on Hong Kong climate and sustainability issues.
Support secondary students to prepare for English-language global dialogues with youth in partner schools.
Develop mentoring, communication, intercultural, teamwork, and community-engagement skills.
Learn about ethical and carefully governed uses of AI for dialogue preparation, rehearsal, and storytelling.
Contribute to student-led public communication and the Project CLIMATE showcase.
Connect climate issues with everyday life, community perspectives, the Sustainable Development Goals, and global dialogue.
Who can apply?
Current CUHK undergraduate or postgraduate students from any discipline.
Students with an interest in climate action, sustainability, education, youth work, communication, community engagement, design, science, social science, humanities, or global learning.
No prior specialist climate knowledge is required. Commitment, curiosity, respect for others, and willingness to learn are essential.
Indicative activities (exact dates to be finalized in accordance with the CUHK students' schedule)
2 half-day Climate Mentor preparation and 1 language-support workshops: December 2026 –January 2027
2 Local dialogue and mentoring activities with secondary students: February 2027
1 Global dialogue preparation and online exchange with international youth peers: March–April 2027
1 Public communication & exhibition preparation, and 1 student-led showcase: April–July 2027
Project CLIMATE will use generative AI only in an optional and carefully supervised support role. Students’ final reflections, captions, and core dialogue contributions will remain their own work and voice.
To express interest, please complete the registration form by November 13, 2026:
https://forms.gle/mN1By3Ng1eJsAHGz7
For enquiries, please contact: Dr Sally Wai-Yan Wan, Project Lead of Project CLIMATE: Community‐engaged Learning, Inclusive Mentoring and AI‐supported Transformative Education, Faculty of Education, CUHK Email:
cuhksdg@cuhk.edu.hk
We welcome students from diverse disciplines, backgrounds, and levels of prior experience. Join us to learn, listen, mentor, and communicate for a more sustainable future.

Announcements
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial 靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗 - School of Public Health and Primary Health Care
From: NGAI CHUN HO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
alfonsengai@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial
現正誠邀合資格人士報名參加！
We are now recruiting eligible participants to join our programme.
完成所有研究程序後，
參加者最多可獲價值$300的禮券
。
賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院現誠邀
60歲或以上
人士參加一項靜觀課程研究，探討靜觀訓練對有慢性壓力的長者腸道微生物群的影響。
很多長者長期承受慢性壓力，若未能妥善處理，對心理及生理健康均可能造成深遠影響。研究顯示，慢性壓力會擾亂腸道微生物群的平衡。雖然靜觀已被證實能有效改善心理健康，但目前仍甚少研究探討靜觀課程如何影響參與者的腸道微生物。
本項研究將在社區招募
138名年滿60歲的人士
，邀請他們參與專為長者而設的靜觀課程或健康教育課程，比較兩者在改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物方面的成效。
參加者將被隨機分派至以下其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組
參加者將接受為期八週、每週一次、每次約1小時30分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂課程將會錄音，以確保課程質素及一致性。
b) 健康教育組
參加者將接受為期八週、每週一次、每次約1小時30分鐘的健康教育課程，內容涵蓋營養、運動及健康生活習慣等主題。
招募對象（需同時符合以下條件）：
年齡60歲或以上
能聽講廣東話
需持續照顧有長期病患的親屬
照顧者負荷指數達7分或以上
沒有經醫生診斷的精神病患或認知問題
沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題
目前並非接受心理治療
過去兩年內未曾參加過正規的靜觀課程
被照顧的親屬並非剛離世
過去三個月內未曾使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間
：暫定於1月中開始，下午時段
地點
：沙田瀝源健康院
形式
：共8節，每週1次，每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，以及結束後3個月，填寫共3次問卷調查，並提供3次糞便樣本。
費用全免

Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!] 🚹🧪🧫🧬🔍!!!注意: 男性特定群組 HPV 病毒篩查   [費用全免] [$400交通津貼]💰💰💰💰 - Department of Surgery
From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
(參加者太多, 其他組別優先)
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
[
As there are too many participants, other groups will take priority.
]
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.
For inquiries, please email:  timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk

本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
(參加者太多, 其他組別優先)
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
[
As there are too many participants, other groups will take priority.
]
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.

General Education Foundation Programme: 2026-27 Student Activity Fund - Call for Application
Dear students,
Since 2012, the General Education (GE) Foundation Programme has been fully launched in CUHK.  Gradually, UGFH and UGFN have become a common learning experience of the CUHK. In 2026-27, the GE Foundation Programme will continue to offer the
Student Activity Fund (SAF)
to encourage student-initiated activities related to the two foundation courses. Through these activities, we hope to promote classics reading by nourishing an enjoyable atmosphere of classics reading in various communities in and out of the campus, and to appreciate the impacts of classics on contemporary society.
The SAF fund accepts applications from
both individuals and groups
. We encourage diversified activities to promote classics reading, including exhibitions, reading groups, performance, APPs, websites and art designs, etc.  Each project should be completed within one year, and could be supported up to HKD 30,000.
The deadline for 2026-27 SAF fund application is 22 November 2026.
If you are interested, please refer to the following website for more details and application forms:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/extended-learning/student-activity-fund/
For enquiries, please contact us by email (
gef-info@cuhk.edu.hk
) or phone (3943 3730). We look forward to hearing from you.
Regards,
General Education Foundation Programme,
Office of University General Education

Digital Place-Making: Media Technology, Related Population, and Urban-Rural Relations in Japan  - Department of Cultural and Religious Studies
From: Master of Arts Programme in Cultural Management
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
zhuoyueli@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
More people than ever are on the move, and new technologies increasingly shape how we experience the places we live in or leave behind. This talk asks how people make place with the use of digital media technologies such as social media, blockchain, metaverse, and artificial intelligence. It focuses on a group of young and middle-aged urbanites in Japan who came to be identified as the “related population”: city dwellers who never fully move to the countryside, yet stay deeply involved in shrinking rural communities through work, visits, and online connection. I trace where the idea of “related population” came from, explore what these place-makers actually do with technology, and show how they see themselves as belonging to multiple places at once. I argue that today’s urban-rural relations are better understood as cycles rather than one-way moves, but we still need to ask what and who can circulate, how, and with what consequences for the places left behind.
Date
: 10 Nov 2026, Tuesday
Time
: 18:45-20:15
Venue
: KKB 101, Leung Kau Kui Building, CUHK
Guest Speaker: Zhang Jinjin
Jinjin Zhang is a Ph.D. Candidate in the Department of Japanese Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. Her research examines digital media, sociotechnical innovation, lifestyle migration and mobility, sensory and multi-modal storytelling, and regional revitalization in Japan and China. She previously served as a “Science, Technology, and Society in Asia” Visiting Fellow at the Harvard-Yenching Institute (2025–2026) and as a Japan Foundation Japanese Studies Fellow at Waseda University (2023–2024). Jinjin cares about public humanities and shares her work through blogging, video-making, and podcasting.

Assistant Professor, Department of Cultural and Religious Studies, CUHK

Communication Seminar Series - AI and Advertising – New Theoretical Frontiers
Date: 12 November 2026 (Thursday)
Time: 2:30 pm-4:00 pm
Venue: C-Centre (NAH313, Humanities Building, CUHK)
Speaker:Prof. Jisu Huh
Associate Dean & Endowed Chair Professor
College of Liberal Arts
University of Minnesota Twin Cities, USA
Bio:
Dr. Jisu Huh, Ph.D. is a Professor and the Raymond O. Mithun Endowed Chair in Advertising at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities in the USA, where she also serves as the Associate Dean for Research & Graduate Programs in the College of Liberal Arts. A leading voice in her field, Dr. Huh is a past President of the American Academy of Advertising and the current Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Advertising, the discipline's flagship, top-ranked journal. She is the founder and director of the interdisciplinary Minnesota Computational Advertising Lab (MCAL) (
https://mcal.umn.edu/
). Her cutting-edge research spans computational advertising, AI advertising, consumer trust and information diffusion, social media marketing, and the direct-to-consumer advertising of healthcare products.
Abstract:
Since generative AI’s public release, its rapid adoption across advertising has sparked a surge in scholarly research. While AI enables hyper-personalized content creation at scale, AI-powered search, and agentic shopping, it raises critical questions and concerns. Consumers are increasingly engaging with AI-generated media experiences, blurring the line between the real and the artificial. AI also transforms how consumers search for and process product information, disrupting SEO/SEM strategies. These developments challenge foundational advertising concepts and advertising effect theory. Furthermore, ethical considerations around content ownership, misinformation, and societal impact further underscore the urgent need for thoughtful, responsible frameworks. This seminar examines various topics related to the rise of generative AI in advertising and its implications for advertising practice and scholarship. Through interactive discussion, the speaker will challenge traditional advertising concepts, address key societal risks, and outline a future research agenda to build new theoretical frontiers in the AI era.

From: Cynthia Lai

Online Health Webinar: Fertility Insights – Understanding the Causes of Miscarriage Through Reproductive Genetics
Moderator: Dr. Jacqueline Chung
Speakers: Prof. Elvis Dong & Prof. Matthew Chau
Date: 3 November 2026 (Tuesday)
Time: 6:00 PM to 7:00 PM
Platform: Zoom (Conducted in Cantonese)
Fee: Free of Charge
About the Webinar:
Miscarriage is often linked to complex genetic factors, ranging from chromosomal abnormalities to gene mutations. Many scientific questions surrounding its causes remain unanswered. Through the lens of reproductive genetics, this webinar will explore the underlying causes of miscarriage, helping participants gain a deeper understanding of the role genetics plays in reproductive medicine and offering new hope for future family-building journeys.
Registration
Scan the QR code on the poster or register online at:
https://forms.gle/smNEA2XPd3HD5Vkh9
Enquiries
Tel: 3505 1456
網上健康講座 - 生育知多少： 從生殖遺傳學探討流產成因
主持：鍾佩樺醫生
講者：董梓瑞教授、周海鍵教授
日期：2026年11月3日（星期二）
時間：下午6:00至7:00
平台：Zoom（以廣東話進行）
費用：全免
內容簡介：流產往往源於複雜的遺傳因素，從染色體異常到基因突變，背後隱藏著許多尚待解答的科學謎題。本研討會將透過生殖遺傳學的角度，探討流產成因，讓大家能更清楚理解遺傳學在生殖醫學中的角色，並為未來的生育之路帶來新的希望。

Turn environmental data into solutions for a more sustainable future. CUHK’s M.Sc. in Earth and Environmental Analytics for Sustainability Programme combines earth system science with data analytics, AI, and environmental modelling to address the most pressing sustainability issues our world faces today. bodyText:

2026/10/30

Announcements
【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged under 33 months) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請33個月或以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀3歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 33個月或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿3歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on the gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between the gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is under 33 months old (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 3 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

誠邀您參加一項運動幹預研究!本研究將有助於瞭解您的運動代謝表現並提高您的代謝健康。
研究題目
：比較不同有氧運動訓練對超重或肥胖絕經後女性代謝及循環血液指標影響的隨機對照試驗
親愛的女士：
您好！
隨着年齡增長與絕經後的荷爾蒙變化，您是否覺得體重逐漸增加、脂肪容易囤積，或者開始擔心體脂、血脂等健康指標？香港中文大學體育運動科學系目前正開展一項研究以了解不同有氧運動訓練對絕經後超重或肥胖女性代謝健康的影響。我們誠邀符合條件的華人女性參與，一起通過科學運動重拾健康！
參與本研究，您將免費獲得：
1. 全面身體成分評估：精準檢測體脂率、肌肉量、內臟脂肪等。
2. 專業血液指標檢測：了解您的血脂、血糖等核心代謝指標。
3. 專家級運動能力測試：精準測量您專屬的運動代謝表現，以評估您的體能與代謝反應。
4. 為期 12 週的免費運動指導：由專業研究人員全程跟進，保障運動安全與效果。

我們在尋找這樣的您：
華人女性，且已自然絕經 12 個月或以上（距離最後一次月經少於 6 年）。

過去 3 個月體重相對穩定，且無嚴重運動禁忌（如嚴重心臟病、中風等）。

The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education, The Chinese University of Hong Kong,
Sports Nutrition and Physical Activity Laboratory,
sincerely invites you to participate in an exercise intervention study! This study will help us understand your exercise metabolic performance and improve your metabolic health.
Study Title
: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing the Effects of Different Aerobic Exercise Training on Metabolic and Circulating Blood Indicators in Postmenopausal Women with overweight or obesity
Dear Madam:
With aging and postmenopausal hormonal changes, do you feel that your weight is gradually increasing, fat is easily accumulated, or you begin to worry about health indicators such as body fat and blood lipids? The Department of Sports Science and Physical Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a study to understand the effects of different aerobic exercise training on metabolic health in postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity. We sincerely invite eligible Chinese women to participate and regain health together through scientific exercise!
By participating in this study, you will receive for free:
1. Comprehensive body composition assessment: accurate measurement of body fat percentage, muscle mass, visceral fat, etc.
2. Professional blood indicator testing: understand your core metabolic indicators such as blood lipids and blood glucose.
3. Expert-level exercise capacity test: accurately measure your exercise metabolic performance to evaluate your physical fitness and metabolic response.
4. 12 weeks of free exercise guidance: full follow‑up by professional researchers to ensure exercise safety and effectiveness.
We are looking for:
1. Chinese women who have been naturally postmenopausal for 12 months or more (less than 6 years since the last menstrual period).
2. Are overweight or obese (BMI ≥ 23 kg/m² or body fat percentage > 30%; will be confirmed by laboratory testing).

From: Michael Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
tsztsunng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼
如對本研究有興趣，請透過以下連結報名參加：
[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 3919 7792 / 9568 9006 或 WhatsApp 9568 9006與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。謝謝
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:
Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample
Incentive:
All assessments are free of charge.
Eligible participants may receive up to HKD 500 in supermarket vouchers upon completion.

The Practice of New Museology in Humanistic Buddhism: Venerable Master Hsing Yun’s Museum Vision 【Hybrid Lecture】 人間佛教的新博物館學實踐:星雲大師的博物館情懷 - Centre for the Study of Humanistic Buddhism
From: 人間佛教研究中心 Centre for the Study of Humanistic Buddhism
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cshb@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【精彩上線｜紀念星雲大師百歲誕辰系列講座】
為紀念星雲大師百歲誕辰，香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心與佛學研究中心聯合舉辦 「人間佛教的文本、行跡與時代開展」 系列講座。我們特別邀請了宗教學、文學、哲學、出版、媒體與博物館學等領域的頂尖專家學者，帶來 9 場重磅專題演講！內容橫跨跨跨文化對話、文學考察、媒體實踐到新博物館學，從多元視角深化對星雲大師思想的理解。本次系列講座全面開放線上參與，歡迎大眾踴躍共霑法益。
題目：
人間佛教的新博物館學實踐:星雲大師的博物館情懷
時間：11月4日 | 週三 10:00 - 12:00
講者：張譽騰教授 | 國立台南藝術大學博物館學研究所兼任教授
主持：陳劍鍠教授 | 香港中文大學人間佛教研究中心主任
形式：現場講座 & ZOOM網絡會議
地點：香港中文大學馮景禧樓 & 會議ID: 964 5779 7423，密碼: 999999
報名：https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741301
演講簡介：
「人間佛教」主張佛法不離世間，強調將佛法落實在日常生活，服務社會，讓佛教從山林走入社會，此正與新博物館學訴求遙相呼應。星雲大師是宗教開創者，但很少人知道他在博物館方面也建樹良多，疊有新意。本講座將從三個面向探討大師在新博物館學的成就:
一、從生態博物館角度說明整座佛光山其實就是一座無牆博物館。
二、從博物館與科技、社區和永續三個層次，說明佛陀紀念館成立迄今，如何與時俱進，踐行新博物館學理念。
三、從佛光山核心館與衛星館發展策略談佛光緣美術館群如何與在地道場結合，將佛光山能量有效輻射出去。
"Humanistic Buddhism" advocates that the Buddha-Dharma is not separate from the world, emphasizing the implementation of Buddhist teachings in daily life, serving society, and guiding Buddhism from isolated mountains into secular society. This philosophy echoes the core pursuits of "New Museology."
While Venerable Master Hsing Yun is widely recognized as a religious pioneer, few are aware of his profound achievements and innovative ideas in the field of museum studies.This presentation will explore the Master’s achievements in New Museology through three main dimensions:
1. The Ecomuseum Perspective: Illustrating how the entirety of Fo Guang Shan functions as a "Museum without Walls."
2. Technology, Community, and Sustainability: Examining how the Fo Guang Shan Buddha Museum has kept pace with the times since its inception, putting the principles of New Museology into practice.
3. Core and Satellite Museum Development Strategy: Discussing how the Fo Guang Yuan Art Galleries integrate with local Buddhist centers (dojos) to effectively radiate Fo Guang Shan's energy outward.
嘉賓簡介：
張譽騰教授，畢業於國立台灣大學動物學系，1992年獲得英國萊斯特大學(University of Leicester)博物館學博士。曾任國立台南藝術大學博物館學研究所教授和文博學院院長、行政院文化建設委員會政務副主委、國立歷史博物館館長、中華民國博物館學會理事長、佛光大學講座教授。主要學術著作有: 《當代博物館探索》、《博物館大勢觀察》、《生態博物館:一個文化運動的興起》。現為國立台南藝術大學博物館學研究所兼任教授，並擔任佛光山顧問與學術委員會委員。

張譽騰教授，畢業於國立台灣大學動物學系，1992年獲得英國萊斯特大學(University of Leicester)博物館學博士。曾任國立台南藝術大學博物館學研究所教授和文博學院院長、行政院文化建設委員會政務副主委、國立歷史博物館館長、中華民國博物館學會理事長、佛光大學講座教授。主要學術著作有: 《當代博物館探索》、《博物館大勢觀察》、《生態博物館:一個文化運動的興起》。現為國立台南藝術大學博物館學研究所兼任教授，並擔任佛光山顧問與學術委員會委員。
