Announcements
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!!] !!!注意: 男性特定群組 HPV 病毒篩查   [費用全免] [$400交通津貼] - Department of Surgery
From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
(參加者太多, 其他組別優先)
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
[
As there are too many participants, other groups will take priority.
]
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.
For inquiries, please email:  timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
[HK$300]Brain Health Study  [HK$300]中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究 - CUHK Psychiatry Sleep Assessment Unit
From: Wong Yuen Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yuentungwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
便秘？嗅覺變差？睡覺拳打腳踢？有腦退化家族史？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
參與研究
費用全免
，成功完成相關研究程序者最多可獲
HK$300元超市禮券
作為津貼
階段一：
下載手機程式並完成問卷 （約需 15–20 分鐘）
完成後可獲得早期柏金遜病風險分數
符合資格並完成問卷者可獲 HK$100元超市禮券
階段二：
部分參加者將獲邀進一步參與臨床評估
包括身體檢查、臨床訪談、居家睡眠測試及神經認知測試
符合資格並完成階段二者，可額外獲 HK$200元超市禮券
立刻掃描海報右下方
二維碼 (QR Code)
或
點擊連結
下載程式「柏健通」參與研究
IOS用戶：
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android用戶：
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
查詢（致電或WhatsApp）：3919 7792 / 5282 5786（研究助理 黃小姐）
Constipated？Weakened sense of smell？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) ？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance.
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher
Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
or
scanning the QR Code
in the poster to download the "柏健通" mobile application:
IOS users:
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android users:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
For details and registration enquiries, please contact our hotline: 39197792 or 5282 5786 (WhatsApp) (Research Assistant, Ms Wong)

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Mr Ben Law
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
Benlaw@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Applications Now Open: CUHK MA in Chinese Art History (2027–2028)
The Master of Arts in Chinese Art History at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is the first master's programme in Hong Kong focusing on Chinese art history. It offers broad and robust academic training for students who inspires to explore the historical development of Chinese Art.
Grounded in both ancient and modern Chinese art, the programme adopts diverse Asian perspectives and guides students to understand critical Chinese art history topics across different periods. Students will also have opportunities to engage directly with art professionals and cultural institutions, gaining valuable insights into the latest developments in Chinese art across academia, museums, cultural heritage, and the creative industries.
Online Information Session
Date: 11 November 2026 (Wednesday)
Time: 6:30pm (GMT+8, Hong Kong Time)
Format: Zoom
Programme Information:
https://www.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/~fadept/programmes/ma-in-chinese-art-history/
Registration for Information Session:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741196
香港中文大學中國藝術史文學碩士課程（2027
–2028
）現正招生
中國藝術史文學碩士課程為香港首個聚焦中國藝術史的課程，為有志於探索中國藝術古今發展史的同學，提供廣博而紮實的學術訓練。
課程以古今藝術為中心，並以多元的亞洲視角探討跨時代的藝術脈絡與相關研究。學生亦有機會與本地專業人士和藝術機構直接交流，掌握中國藝術在全球學術、文化產業等各個領域的發展趨勢，為未來投身學術、教育、文博、創意等產業奠下重要基礎。

~[Research Invitation] Speech Intervention Study for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate 【研究邀請】招募參與「唇顎裂兒童及青少年語音介入」之學術研究 - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
各位香港中文大學成員：
我們誠邀閣下及其子女參與由香港中文大學耳鼻喉科、頭頸外科進行的學術研究 。
研究題目： 「探索針對唇顎裂兒童及青少年的語音介入框架：隨機對照試驗」
研究目的：患有唇顎裂的兒童有較高風險出現語音/發音困難，這可能嚴重影響其說話清晰度。本研究旨在比較兩種不同的實證語音介入框架（線性與非線性語音介入）在改善這些語音錯誤方面的成效。
招募對象：
說廣東話的兒童及青少年 (4歲 – 17歲)；
4 至 17 歲，母語為廣東話嘅兒童及青少年。
患有唇顎裂，並有發音/語音問題。
於 24 個月大前已完成唇顎裂之修復手術；
無已知認知障礙，或任何會影響其獨立參與語音任務能力的醫療狀況。
研究程序：
全面評估：參與者將經歷全面的語音評估程序，包括多項標準化語音測試及填寫問卷。
個別治療：參與者將接受由專業言語治療師設計的語音治療方案。請注意，候補名單對照組的參與者將在主要研究觀察階段結束後接受治療。
錄影記錄：參與者的語音將被錄影，以作進一步記錄和分析。所有語音數據及錄音將受密碼保護並嚴格保密 。
費用與報酬：
潛在益處：參與者能透過治療方案提升整體說話清晰度，並為唇顎裂語音的臨床護理程序及機制提供貢獻。
參與費用：參與本研究無需支付任何額外費用。
聯絡方式： 如有興趣參與或有任何疑問，請致電 3943 9609 聯絡首席研究員 何皓賢先生。
感謝閣下對本研究計劃的興趣與支持。亦可以使用以下連結報名:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
此研究項目已獲香港中文大學 – 新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會（Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC）批准。
Dear Members of the CUHK Community,
We are cordially inviting children and adolescents with Cleft Palate ± Lip to participate in a research study conducted by the Division of Speech Therapy (Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Study Title: Exploring Speech Intervention Frameworks for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate +/- Lip: A Randomized-Controlled Trial.
Children born with Cleft Palate ±Lip (CP±L) are at high risk for speech difficulties, such as glottal stops or backing errors, which can significantly impact how well they produce speech sounds and are understood. This study investigates the effectiveness of two different evidence-based speech intervention frameworks (Linear vs. Non-linear phonological intervention) in improving these speech outcomes.
Who Can Participate?
Cantonese-speaking children and adolescents (aged 4 to 17) with CP±L
Individuals exhibiting cleft speech errors that require intervention;
Primary repair of the palate done prior to 24 months old;
No known cognitive or hearing impairment, or other medical conditions that prevent independent participation in speech tasks.
What is Involved?
Comprehensive Assessment: Participants will undergo standardized speech assessments and questionnaires.
Treatment: Participants will receive speech therapy protocols designed by professional speech therapists. Please note that participants in the waitlist group will receive treatment after the primary study observation phase.
Recording: Speech sessions will be video-recorded for data analysis and will remain strictly confidential.
Benefits and Costs:
Potential Benefits: Improvement in overall speech clarity and contribution to the clinical management of cleft palate speech.
Costs: There is no additional cost to participate.
Contact Information: If you are interested or have questions, please contact Mr. Choco Ho (何皓賢), Speech Therapist and Principal Investigator, at 3943 9609 or click the link below:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

[Free of charge] UP TO HKD$1000 ALLOWANCE! Assess the safety, efficacy and tolerability of a CUHK proprietary Chinese medicine formula – A 9-month trial targeting patients with diabetes <6-year disease duration and on two or less oral drugs 津貼高達一千港元!以確認香港中文大學研發的專利中藥配方的安全性、療效及耐受性。招募糖尿病人(六年內確診，飲食控制或服用2種或以下口服糖尿藥)參與為期九個月的研究 - Department of Medicine and Therapeutics
From: Maggie Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
maggielee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期九個月，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至80歲華人
沒有重大疾病 (例如:心臟病或中風等重大併發症)
沒有服用中藥
身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
患糖尿病6 年或以下
目前飲食控制或用2種或以下口服糖尿藥 [例如metformin（品牌藥名：Glucophage）或/及 gliclazide（品牌藥名：Diamicron）]
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，但具備以下其中一項風險因素，我們會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）作篩查
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 9-month clinical study on the use of oral Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 80 years
No major illnesses (e.g., heart disease or stroke)
Not taking Chinese medicine
Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes within the past 6 years
Diet control alone or taking no more than 2 oral diabetes medications [e.g., metformin (Glucophage®) and/or gliclazide (Diamicron®)]
Not sure if you have diabetes? If you have any of the following risk factors, we can arrange a 75 g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) for diabetes screening
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes

Study Procedures: Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1EK8XyC5ac5ykiG
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver

History of gestational diabetes

bodyText:

CALL FOR PROPOSALS | Participation in the 17th Chinese National Arctic Research Expedition 2027 | HKPSIC  - Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre
From: Yolanda YIM
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yolandayim@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
An Opportunity to Conduct Research in A
rctic Regions
_________________________________________________________________________________________
The Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC) is pleased to invite proposals from scientists and researchers interested in participating in the
17th
Chinese National Arctic
Research Expedition 2027
.
Research opportunities are available at
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2, Yellow River Station
and
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
in Arctic Regions. All proposals and personnel nominations will be reviewed and selected by the Polar Research Institute of China (PRIC).
This opportunity is primarily open to researchers from universities in Hong Kong.
Expedition Purpose
The expedition will be conducted for
scientific research purposes
.
Research Opportunities
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2
Quota:
Tentatively 1-2 participants
(Subject to adjustment based on the approved research proposals.)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 months at the station
Tentative departure from Shanghai aboard the icebreaker
Xuelong
or
Xuelong 2
in June or July 2027
Return to Shanghai in Sep or Oct 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Shanghai
Yellow River Station
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Longyearbyen to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Longyearbyen and from Hong Kong
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Akureyri and drive to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights from Hong Kong to Reykjavík, onward travel to Akureyri, and ground transportation to the station.
Priority consideration:
Applicants with existing research collaborations or academic connections in Iceland
Research Instruments
As the icebreakers
Xuelong
and
Xuelong 2
will depart from Shanghai, PRIC recommends that any required research instruments be shipped to Shanghai no later than
April-May
for loading and transportation to the Arctic research stations.
Health and Visa Requirements
Selected participants will be required to:
Complete a medical examination specified by PRIC
Submit a medical report for review
Obtain a Schengen visa for Yellow River Station or CIAO
Participants should allow sufficient time for medical examinations and visa applications.
Clothing and Equipment
PRIC will provide basic expedition clothing and equipment, including:
Expedition jackets
Trousers
Thermal wear
Sunglasses
Other essential gear
These items will be provided to selected participants before departure.
Expenses to Be Covered by Participants
Participants are responsible for all associated expenses, including:
International airfares
Accommodation on the stations before and after station entry/exit or during the expedition in the stations
(Accommodation on Xuelong or Xuelong 2 is provided free of charge)
Travel insurance
Visa application fees (if applicable)
Medical examination fees
Shipment and transportation costs for research instruments and equipment
Any other incidental expenses
Proposal Submission
Researchers who are able to meet the above requirements and schedule are invited to submit an email request to obtain the proposal template.
Submission Deadline
10 November 2026 (Tuesday)
All proposals will be forwarded to PRIC for evaluation and selection. HKPSIC will provide support to participating researchers and facilitate communications with PRIC throughout the application and preparation process.
Enquiries
Secretariat
Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)
Email: hkpsic@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 3943 0345
We sincerely encourage interested researchers to take advantage of this unique opportunity to conduct scientific research in Arctic Regions and contribute to polar research collaboration.
We look forward to receiving your proposals.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

bodyText:

Announcements
Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Group Projects Without the Drama  - ITSC
From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We all know group projects can be... challenging. What if you had an
AI project manager
that breaks down tasks, writes meeting notes, and helps resolve disagreements?
Use Copilot
to keep your team on track and your project drama-free.
Prompt 1 — copy & paste it!
Break it down
"Our group project is: [describe]. We have 4 members and 3 weeks. Break into specific tasks with: 1) Clear deliverables per person 2) Dependencies 3) Deadlines 4) A risk and mitigation plan."
Prompt 2 — keep the conversation going!
Meeting minutes in seconds
"Here are rough notes from our group meeting: [paste notes]. Turn these into professional minutes with: attendees, key decisions, action items (who/what/when), and next meeting items."
Prompt 3 — go advanced!
Resolve disagreements
"Our team disagrees on [issue]. Person A thinks [A] and Person B thinks [B]. Give an objective pros/cons analysis, then suggest a compromise taking the best of both."
Why this works:
Copilot is the neutral third party every group project needs. No sides, no drama, just clear action plans!

Bonus tip:
Before final submission:
"Review our project for consistency in writing style, formatting, and tone — make it sound like one person wrote it"

Want to enhance your Copilot skills? Check out previous
All IT - Microsoft Copilot Chat Usage Tips
for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

Unlock Your Potential: Join the CUHK eLearning Student Ambassadors 2026/2027! Registration is NOW open for all CUHK students (UG & PG)  - Information Technology Services Centre (ITSC)
From: Rudi C. (ITSC)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rudichow@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Are you someone who has a strong interest in communication, digital media, publication, information technology, AI trends, and online learning?
Would you like to develop your own multimedia and online portfolio while assisting other fellow students to have a better online learning experience?
If the answer is YES, we would like to invite you to apply and join us to become a
CUHK eLearning Student Ambassador (eLSA)
.
We are seeking applicants (Year 1 - 4 UG students, and all PG students) who are:
Driven to perform a
creative
and
dynamic
role to help fellow students in utilising various eLearning resources (including AI trends and its application in education).
Committed
and
motivated
to learn and improve IT, AI tools, online media, and digital skills to support their studies and future careers.
eLSA programme offers you:
An opportunity to develop digital, media production, IT, communication, organisation and teamwork skills.
Regular trainings that cover the fundamental IT and digital production skills you would need to support the work.
An opportunity to create and showcase your digital and online portfolio. (including CUHK SDP - Student Development Portfolio programme)
A space to contribute innovative ideas and exercise creative thinking to improve the CUHK eLearning environment.
eLSA ambassadors will receive subsidies under the
University’s Campus Work Scheme
.
Please complete the webform at:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13741495
Application deadline
(extended)
: October 3, 2026 - 11.59 PM.
To learn more about eLearning@CUHK, please visit
https://www.cuhk.edu.hk/eLearning
.
For more information, please contact ITSC-EDT via email at:
rudichow@cuhk.edu.hk

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
adopted by the United Nations.

CUHK students, student groups and university units

Projects must respond to one or more of the 17 SDGs, be self-initiated and be conducted in Hong Kong.

Whether you're passionate about Japanese studies or planning a career with a Japan focus, this programme is your gateway to meaningful growth and development.

bodyText:

CALL FOR PROPOSALS | Participation in the 17th Chinese National Arctic Research Expedition 2027 | HKPSIC  - Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre
From: Yolanda YIM
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yolandayim@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
An Opportunity to Conduct Research in Arctic
Regions
__________________________________________________________________________________
The Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC) is pleased to invite proposals from scientists and researchers interested in participating in the
17th
Chinese National Arctic
Research Expedition 2027
.
Research opportunities are available at
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2, Yellow River Station
and
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
in Arctic Regions. All proposals and personnel nominations will be reviewed and selected by the Polar Research Institute of China (PRIC).
This opportunity is primarily open to researchers from universities in Hong Kong.
Expedition Purpose
The expedition will be conducted for
scientific research purposes
.
Research Opportunities
Arctic Ocean Expedition with Xuelong or Xuelong 2
Quota:
Tentatively 1-2 participants
(Subject to adjustment based on the approved research proposals.)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 months at the station
Tentative departure from Shanghai aboard the icebreaker
Xuelong
or
Xuelong 2
in June or July 2027
Return to Shanghai in Sep or Oct 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Shanghai
Yellow River Station
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Longyearbyen to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Longyearbyen and from Hong Kong
China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory (CIAO)
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
Duration:
Approximately 1- 2 week(s) at the station
Tentative departure from Akureyri and drive to the station in Aug or Sep
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights from Hong Kong to Reykjavík, onward travel to Akureyri, and ground transportation to the station.
Priority consideration:
Applicants with existing research collaborations or academic connections in Iceland
Research Instruments
As the icebreakers
Xuelong
and
Xuelong 2
will depart from Shanghai, PRIC recommends that any required research instruments be shipped to Shanghai no later than
Mar-April
for loading and transportation to the Antarctic research stations.
Health and Visa Requirements
Selected participants will be required to:
Complete a medical examination specified by PRIC
Submit a medical report for review
Obtain a Schengen visa for Yellow River Station or CIAO
Participants should allow sufficient time for medical examinations and visa applications.
Clothing and Equipment
PRIC will provide basic expedition clothing and equipment, including:
Expedition jackets
Trousers
Thermal wear
Sunglasses
Other essential gear
These items will be provided to selected participants before departure.
Expenses to Be Covered by Participants
Participants are responsible for all associated expenses, including:
International airfares
Accommodation on the stations before and after station entry/exit or during the expedition in the stations
(Accommodation on Xuelong or Xuelong 2 is provided free of charge)
Travel insurance
Visa application fees (if applicable)
Medical examination fees
Shipment and transportation costs for research instruments and equipment
Any other incidental expenses
Proposal Submission
Researchers who are able to meet the above requirements and schedule are invited to submit an email request to obtain the proposal template.
Submission Deadline
10 November 2026 (Tuesday)
All proposals will be forwarded to PRIC for evaluation and selection. HKPSIC will provide support to participating researchers and facilitate communications with PRIC throughout the application and preparation process.
Enquiries
Secretariat
Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)
Email: hkpsic@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 3943 0345
We sincerely encourage interested researchers to take advantage of this unique opportunity to conduct scientific research in Arctic Regions and contribute to polar research collaboration.
We look forward to receiving your proposals.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

各位同學：
自2012年始，大學通識教育基礎課程已在中大全面推行。UGFH和UGFN不知不覺已成為中大人的共同學習經驗。在2026-27學年，大學通識教育基礎課程將繼續推出
學生活動資助計劃
，鼓勵同學們自發設計、推廣及活化與課程相關的活動，在校園內外推廣經典閱讀，鼓勵校內外社群發掘閱讀經典的趣味及當代意義。
本資助計劃接受
個人或小組申請
，以多元形式推廣經典閱讀，包括展覽、讀書會、表演、應用程式、網站及藝術品設計等。申請項目一般須在一年內完成，每個項目最高可獲得港幣3萬元資助。
2026-27
年學生活動資助計劃截止報名日期為
2026
年
11
月
22
日
。

https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/extended-learning/student-activity-fund/
如對本計劃有任何疑問，請電郵至
gef-info@cuhk.edu.hk
或致電3943 3730查詢。我們期待收到你們的申請。

General Education Foundation Programme: 2026-27 Student Activity Fund - Call for Application
Dear students,
Since 2012, the General Education (GE) Foundation Programme has been fully launched in CUHK.  Gradually, UGFH and UGFN have become a common learning experience of the CUHK. In 2026-27, the GE Foundation Programme will continue to offer the
Student Activity Fund (SAF)
to encourage student-initiated activities related to the two foundation courses. Through these activities, we hope to promote classics reading by nourishing an enjoyable atmosphere of classics reading in various communities in and out of the campus, and to appreciate the impacts of classics on contemporary society.
The SAF fund accepts applications from
both individuals and groups
. We encourage diversified activities to promote classics reading, including exhibitions, reading groups, performance, APPs, websites and art designs, etc.  Each project should be completed within one year, and could be supported up to HKD 30,000.
The deadline for 2026-27 SAF fund application is 22 November 2026.
If you are interested, please refer to the following website for more details and application forms:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/extended-learning/student-activity-fund/
For enquiries, please contact us by email (
gef-info@cuhk.edu.hk
) or phone (3943 3730). We look forward to hearing from you.
Regards,
General Education Foundation Programme,
Office of University General Education

Are you someone who has a strong interest in communication, digital media, publication, information technology, AI trends, and online learning?
Would you like to develop your own multimedia and online portfolio while assisting other fellow students to have a better online learning experience?
If the answer is YES, we would like to invite you to apply and join us to become a
CUHK eLearning Student Ambassador (eLSA)
.
We are seeking applicants (Year 1 - 4 UG students, and PG students) who are:
Driven to perform a
creative
and
dynamic
role to help fellow students in utilising various eLearning resources (including AI trends and its application in education).
Committed
and
motivated
to learn and improve IT, AI tools, online media, and digital skills to support their studies and future careers.
eLSA programme offers you:
An opportunity to develop digital, media production, IT, communication, organisation and teamwork skills.
Regular trainings that cover the fundamental IT and digital production skills you would need to support the work.
An opportunity to create and showcase your digital and online portfolio. (including CUHK SDP - Student Development Portfolio programme)
A space to contribute innovative ideas and exercise creative thinking to improve the CUHK eLearning environment.
eLSA ambassadors will receive subsidies under the
University’s Campus Work Scheme
.

Call for Papers 11th Conference of the International Society for Gesture Studies - ISGS 2027  - Department of Educational Psychology
From: Catherine So
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wingchee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Call for Papers
11th Conference of the International Society for Gesture Studies - ISGS 2027
Conference Dates: 14-16 December 2027, Hong Kong
Abstract Submission Dates: July 2, 2026 - November 30, 2026
Conference website:
https://events.polyu.edu.hk/isgs2027/home
Abstract Submission Link:
https://cems.polyu.edu.hk/abstract-submission?id=68&eventId=2DC9D9A1-D4F9-4BD9-9B8C-D5E229D92760
We cordially invite abstracts on topics related to Futures for Gestures within the following thematic areas: “Theory, Practice, Technology, Ecology” and their subthemes.
Theory
Mind, embodiment, and cognition
Perception and social understanding
Psychology and philosophy
Meaning and multimodality
Gesture studies theory
Practice
Knowledge, competence, and skill
Habitualisation, routine, and culture
Learning, pedagogy, and performance
Interaction, conduct, and communication
Intervention, impact, and profession
Technology
Artificial Intelligence, computer vision, and big data
New, digital, and social media
Screen, film, and cinema
Kinematics and capture
Human-Computer Interaction
Ecology
Organism, environment, and nature
Vitality, life, and living
Growth, movement, and process
Relationality and materiality
Dynamic and complex systems
We welcome all submissions that explore these themes and sub-themes.
Presentation Formats:
Paper presentation   20 minutes & 5 minutes Q & A
Poster presentation   Print: Size: A0 (Width: 841mm x Height: 1189mm)
Thematic Panels   90 min slot. Maximum 5 presentations + minimum 15 minutes discussion/ Q & A
Abstract Submission Guidelines for papers and posters:
Abstracts should be anonymous. Please delete all references to the authors.
Each abstract should include the following:
a. Title (max: 15 words)
b. Abstract (max: 350 words excluding references)
c. Citation style: APA (7th edition)
Please submit your abstract online following this format.
For Thematic Panels:
Add the details of the panel chair as the submitting author and of all the authors using the "Add Co-author" function. (Please indicate which contributing authors are also panel co-chairs, if any).
Add a title line with the title of the panel under "Abstract Title".
Upload one document with all the abstracts including a 250-word rationale for the panel + 150 words per paper (max. 5 papers).
Remember to delete all references to the authors.
Each presenter can appear on a maximum of three abstracts (whether paper / poster presentation, panel) and only once as the first author (excluding thematic panels).
Authors should ensure that the same abstract has not been presented at another conference.
Deadline for submission: 30 November 2026, 11:59PM (Hong Kong Time) (UTC+8)
Selection Process
All submissions will undergo a double (or triple) blind review and the first author of accepted submissions will be informed by the beginning of April 2027.
The ISGS will offer a restricted number of bursaries to student presenters, including PhD candidates, at the conference as a waiver of the registration price. Information regarding the application process will be provided following review of conference abstracts.
International Sign interpreting will be provided by Overseas Interpreting. We will inquire about your requirements during registration.
Pre-conference Workshops
Pre-conference workshops are being organised and will take place the day before the conference (December 13th 2027). More information will be shared once available.
Abstract Submission Link
https://cems.polyu.edu.hk/abstract-submission?id=68&eventId=2DC9D9A1-D4F9-4BD9-9B8C-D5E229D92760
Please contact us at
isgs2027.hk@polyu.edu.hk
if you have any enquiries.
On behalf of the Organizing Committee for the 2027 Conference of the International Society for Gesture Studies
ISGS 2027:
https://events.polyu.edu.hk/isgs2027/home
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Professional Certificate Programme in Management of Student Activities in Primary and Secondary Schools 中小學學生活動管理專業證書課程2026–2027 - Hong Kong Institute of Educational Research
From: Jasmine Lo
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jasminelo@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
****
中小學學生活動管理專業證書課程
2026–2027****
香港中文大學教育學院、香港教育研究所與香港課外活動主任協會於2026–2027學年舉辦兼讀制 「中小學學生活動管理專業證書課程」，以回應中、小學學生活動的發展情勢，並配合學員的專業需要。
課程對象
負責或協助籌辦及帶領學生活動的現職中、小學教師，尤以現任及新任課外活動主任、全方位學習統籌主任、新高中「其他學習經歷」統籌主任、「學生學習概覽」統籌主任及課程發展主任為合。需持有教師資歷及認可大學之學士學位。
課程內容
課程包括四個必修單元和一個選修單元，共126小時。
必修單元
選修單元
DSA0001學生活動的基礎知識與理論
DSA0002學生活動的管理
DSA0003學生活動的實踐
DSA0004學生活動專題探究
DSA0101小學學生活動的組織與運作
DSA0102中學學生活動的組織與運作
修讀日期
2026年11月至2027年6月（除實習單元外，上課時間暫定為星期二及四晚上）
截止報名日期
2026年9月21日（星期一）
請於網上填寫及提交申請表格：
https://hkier.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/csa
課程查詢
香港中文大學香港教育研究所
地址：香港新界沙田香港中文大學何添樓204室
電話：3943 6999
傳真：2603 6850
電郵：
hkier-training@cuhk.edu.hk
****Professional Certificate Programme in Management of Student Activities in Primary and Secondary Schools 2026-2027****
The Faculty of Education and the Hong Kong Institute of Educational Research (HKIER) of the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and the Hong Kong Extra-curricular Activities Masters’ Association collaborate in offering the one-year Professional Certificate Programme in Management of Student Activities in Primary and Secondary Schools in the 2026–2027 academic year. This programme is designed to respond to the development of student activities and to accommodate the needs of professional training of educators.
Target Participants
Serving teachers in primary or secondary schools who are responsible for or involved in organizing and managing student activities, and holders of teacher qualification and a Bachelor's degree from a recognized university.
Curriculum
The curriculum consists of four compulsory modules and one elective module, a total of 126 hours.
Study Period
November 2026 to June 2027 (mainly on Tuesday and Thursday)
Application Deadline
21 September 2026
Please submit your application online:
https://hkier.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/csa
Enquiries
Hong Kong Institute of Educational Research, CUHK
Address: Room 204, Ho Tim Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T., Hong Kong
Tel: 3943 6999
Fax: 2603 6850
Email:
hkier-training@cuhk.edu.hk

二、熱愛藝術文化，對博物館充滿好奇，並有興趣尋找文物與生活的聯繫

To become an AMA, you must:
1. be a current CUHK student (full-time or part-time).
2. be passionate about arts and culture, curious about museums, and eager to explore the connections between artifacts and everyday life.
3. attend the interview-cum-briefing session (details in the application form).

Announcements
【Public Health and Health Service Research】 Student Helper Recruitment | Literature Review, Data Extraction and Fieldwork  - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Ng Sammi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
samming001@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The
JC School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
is recruiting student helpers to support several research projects about health promotion, evidence-based medicine, and Chinese medicine, led by Prof. Martin Chi-sang WONG, Prof. Jason Junjie HUANG, Prof. Claire Chenwen ZHONG.
The main responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:
Data extraction and data entry
Literature review and article screening
Fieldwork and survey data collection
Interview transcription and data management
Other research-related and administrative duties as assigned
This position provides an excellent opportunity for students who are interested in gaining hands-on experience in public health and health services research.
Requirements:
Training will be provided. Students should be responsible, detail-oriented, and committed to completing assigned tasks reliably and on time.
Good communication and organizational skills
Proficiency in English and Chinese
Prefer BSc Public Health, Community Health, & Chinese Medicine, and students from the Faculty of Medicine.
Working arrangements:
Flexible working schedule (We do not have a specific reporting schedule for students. We will reach out personally to coordinate the working schedule)
On-site work (work from home can be arranged depending on project needs)
Training will be provided
Expected Working Period: August 2026 to 2027
Salary (in hourly rate): 64
Application deadline
: Recruit on an ongoing basis
If you are interested, please send your
CV
,
academic programme/year of study
, and
weekly availability
to
samming001@cuhk.edu.hk
. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please feel free to contact us at the same email address.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/
